Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): the word produced by the independent substitution (substituted until it has at least 3,025 letters) has length 4,181, starts with `0100101001001010` and holds 1,155 ones in its first 3,025 letters; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (1, 2), (47, 4), (6, 18) and (2, 28), with maximum fit errors of 0.01495/0.01475/0.01489/0.01468; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 27.18%–27.60%, color is 0.02536–0.02597 to 0.85393–0.85422 with a mean of 0.30453–0.30639, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8468–0.8476 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 27.16%–27.57%, color is 0.02512–0.02534 to 0.85454–0.85472 with a mean of 0.30452–0.30639 and height is at most 0.8489–0.8501 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 74.5% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05 (53.4% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (90.5, 42.3, 57.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0356 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: nearly vertical coral red stripes on dark purple-black that now and then slip by one cell, with stripes of long and short widths. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`zeckendorftable` adds a Zeckendorf table, bringing the current catalog from 1025 to 1026 kinds (1027 gallery choices including plain). The numbers 1 to 2,304 are laid out row by row as a 48×48 table of rounded square tiles, the tile in row `row` and column `col` holding `n = row·48 + col + 1`, and its tone is decided by how many Fibonacci numbers (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 ..., non-consecutive) the Zeckendorf representation of `n` uses: the more terms the brighter, with the tone `0.7·((terms − 1) / (largest number of terms − 1))`; the Fibonacci numbers themselves (one term) are the darkest. The Zeckendorf representation is found greedily, and it is also the fewest Fibonacci numbers that add up to `n`. The 2,304 numbers need 1 to 8 terms: 16, 105, 362, 693, 710, 351, 65 and 2 numbers need 1 to 8 terms respectively, so most tiles sit at the middle tones. The table shows blocks of light and shade along rows and columns (I only describe what I see in the preview and did not verify whether it is self-similar). Lime green rounded square tiles lie on a dark green-black gap ground, and the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic number-theory table, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 48×48 size, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14, exponent 1), the lime green and dark green-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: the first version used the tone `terms / largest number of terms` directly and, on viewing the preview, since most numbers fall at 3 to 5 terms all tiles were about the same mid green with very low contrast, so I changed it to `(terms − 1) / (largest number of terms − 1)`, counted from one term (I viewed the preview again: the contrast is somewhat better, but most tiles are still a mid green, which is a result of the distribution itself and I did not force it with a stronger exponent). That the greedy Zeckendorf representation is also the representation with the fewest terms is a known standard theorem that I did not prove here; but the tests replace the sampler's greedy method with **another, independent method** — dynamic programming over all `n ≤ 2304` for the fewest Fibonacci numbers that add up to `n` — so that the two agree on all 2,304 numbers is itself tested. The tests check the numbers of cells needing 1 to 8 terms (16, 105, 362, 693, 710, 351, 65, 2) and that the largest count is 8, and compare the colour at every cell centre against all 2,304 possible shifts, checking that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0280).

At start-up (per sampler) the Fibonacci numbers not above 2,304 are listed (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …, 1597, 16 in all), for every `n = 1 … 2304` the code greedily takes, from the largest down, each Fibonacci number not above the remainder and counts them into an `Int32Array(2305)`, takes the largest count (8), and stores the tone `0.7·((terms − 1) / 7)` in a `Float64Array(2304)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 6, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 6, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 48): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(2304)` of 18,432 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 149,504 B in all, with a build-time `Int32Array(2305)` (9,220 B), all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): the independent dynamic programming gives the distribution of 1 to 8 terms as 16, 105, 362, 693, 710, 351, 65 and 2 numbers (2,304 in all), with the 16 Fibonacci numbers at one term each; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (38, 40), (16, 12), (41, 36) and (1, 7), with maximum fit errors of 0.01498/0.01498/0.01495/0.01479; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 34.91%–34.96%, color is 0.02548–0.02601 to 0.85044–0.85170 with a mean of 0.35986–0.35992, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8356–0.8390 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 34.28%–34.29%, color is 0.02525–0.02535 to 0.84195–0.85237 with a mean of 0.35983–0.35995 and height is at most 0.8361–0.8439 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 76.0% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05 (36.6% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (75.8, 104.6, 53.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0280 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: a table of lime green tiles, mostly mid green, with blocks of light and shade along rows and columns. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`walshmatrix` adds a Walsh matrix, bringing the current catalog from 1024 to 1025 kinds (1026 gallery choices including plain). The 32×32 Walsh–Hadamard matrix in sequency order, drawn as rounded square tiles: along row `r` the sign changes exactly `r` times (row 0 is all +1 and row 31 changes sign at every cell); +1 cells glow (fading by 0.3 from the first to the last row) and −1 cells stay at the floor tone. The matrix has order `2^5 = 32`; the Hadamard row of row `r` is `h = bitReverse(grayCode(r))`, and the value in column `c` is `(−1)^popcount(h & c)`. Any two different rows are orthogonal (dot product 0), so the picture is a binary square with a lot of structure, with the frequency increasing downwards. Amber gold tiles lie on a deep blue ground, and the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic mathematical table, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 32×32 size, the row fade of 0.3, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the amber gold and deep blue colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler builds the sequency order with a Gray code and a bit reversal; the tests build the whole table in **another, independent way** — the Sylvester doubling method (`H = [[H, H], [H, −H]]`) with the rows sorted by their number of sign changes — and check that the sorted rows have exactly 0 to 31 sign changes, read ±1 back from the sampler's cell-centre colours (a lit cell is +1) and check that the matrix read back is a Hadamard matrix (any two different rows have dot product 0 and every row has dot product 32 with itself, whatever the shift), and then compare the colour at every cell centre against all 1,024 possible shifts and check that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). This shows that the sampler's matrix agrees with the independently built Walsh matrix (including the sequency order) and that the signs read back really are orthogonal. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0177). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below), because the cell width (8 and 16 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ, not because of different seeds.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(1024)` tone table is built: for row `row` take `gray = row xor (row >> 1)` and reverse its 5 bits to get `hadamard`, and for column `col` take `parity = popcount(hadamard & col) mod 2`; if `parity = 0` (+1) `tones = 0.7·(1 − 0.3·row / 31)`, otherwise 0; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 5, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 5, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 32): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(1024)` of 8,192 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 139,264 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction or the sampling time. Measured (tool-run): the independently built Walsh matrix has the sign-change counts 0, 1, 2, …, 31 for its rows; for the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) the matrix read back is a Hadamard matrix (0 non-orthogonal row pairs), and each has a **unique** fitting shift, (12, 22), (4, 1), (22, 13) and (2, 6), with maximum fit errors of 0.01499/0.01499/0.01500/0.01498; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 32.09%–32.17%, color is 0.02581–0.02604 to 0.85314–0.85387 with a mean of 0.32965–0.32984, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8431–0.8452 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is always 37.06%, color is 0.02523–0.02538 to 0.85422–0.85461 with a mean of 0.33488–0.33499 and height is at most 0.8463–0.8492 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 76.2% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05 (35.9% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (90.7, 74.9, 44.0), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0177 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview: amber gold tiles on deep blue with one fully lit horizontal row (row 0) and vertical stripes and checker structures getting denser towards the bottom. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hermitemodes` adds Hermite-Gauss modes, bringing the current catalog from 1023 to 1024 kinds (1025 gallery choices including plain). An 8×8 chart of the Hermite–Gauss modes, which are the transverse modes TEM(m, n) of a laser beam (and the states of the 2D harmonic oscillator): the column is the index m along x and the row is the index n along y (each 0 to 7); every cell shows the intensity `I = (f_m(x)·f_n(y) / (peak_m·peak_n))²`, where `f_k(x) = H_k(x)·exp(−x² / 2)` and `H_k` is the physicists' Hermite polynomial, each 1D function normalised by its largest absolute value over the range so that the brightest point of each cell is close to 1. In every cell x and y run from −4.2 to 4.2, so low modes are a small spot in the middle and high modes are grids of bright lobes separated by dark nodal lines (m and n count the nodal lines in each direction). Orange-red lobes lie on a dark purple-black ground as rounded square tiles, and the seed moves the whole chart around the torus (in whole cells). It is a schematic mathematical chart, not a physical simulation of a laser beam (the beam waist of a real beam changes with the mode order, whereas here all modes share one range).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8×8 cells, the coordinate range ±4.2, the size of the rounded-square kernel, the tones (floor 0.1, span 0.74), the orange-red and dark purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview; it is rather dark and the lobes of the high modes are dense, and I did not tune it further). That Hermite–Gauss modes are laser transverse modes and eigenstates of the harmonic oscillator, and that the classical turning point of `m = 7` is about `√15 ≈ 3.87` (so the range ±4.2 is enough), are standard physical and mathematical facts which I did not verify here. The sampler computes the Hermite polynomial with the recurrence `H_(k+1) = 2x·H_k − 2k·H_(k−1)` and finds the 1D peak on a fine grid of 4,097 points; the tests recompute it in **another, independent form** — the explicit sum `H_k(x) = k!·Σ_j (−1)^j (2x)^(k − 2j) / (j! (k − 2j)!)`, with the peaks found on a grid of 8,193 points (a different size from the sampler's) — at 8,000 golden-ratio points and compare it with the sampler's colour (inside the kernel (quartic norm at most 0.65) the intensity tone, outside the kernel (norm above 1.02) the gap tone, and the soft edge zone in between is not compared), trying all 64 possible shifts and checking that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03); they also check the 1D peaks (1 for `k = 0`, between 580 and 590 for `k = 7`) and `H_1(0) = 0`. This shows that the intensity formula, the normalisation, the coordinate mapping and the arrangement of every cell agree with the independently written formula, **but not the shape of the soft edge zone of the kernel**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.00274, nearly flat).

At start-up (per sampler) the largest `|f_k|` is found for each `k = 0 … 7` at 4,097 equally spaced points between −4.2 and 4.2 (`peaks`), 8 sets and about 32,776 function evaluations (I did not measure the time of this part); at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), the position `(fx, fy)` (−0.5 to 0.5) inside the cell maps to `x = fx·2·4.2` and `y = fy·2·4.2`, and the cell index shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 4, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 4, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 8) gives `(m, n)`, with `amplitude = f_m(x)·f_n(y) / (peaks[m]·peaks[n])` and `tone = amplitude²`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + toneSpan·tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.1, `toneSpan` 0.74), height is `0.8·dome·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the 8 peaks, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (each sample runs two recurrences of up to order 7 and two exponentials). Measured (tool-run): the 1D peaks for `k = 0 … 7` are 1.0000, 1.2131, 2.2920, 5.4226, 14.9596, 46.3971, 158.1936 and 584.0201; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (0, 2), (2, 4), (3, 4) and (5, 1), with maximum fit errors of 0.01500/0.01489/0.01482/0.01477 (of 8,000 points per seed, 6,718 are used for the comparison, 5,081 of them inside the kernel); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 4.81%–4.83%, color is 0.02551–0.02588 to 0.84838–0.85010 with a mean of 0.15925–0.15940, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8541–0.8609 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 4.55%–4.57%, color is 0.02519–0.02543 to 0.8526–0.8544 with a mean of 0.15929–0.15944 and height is at most 0.8671–0.8774 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 9.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (47.4, 19.4, 29.7), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.00274 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the preview: a regular 8×8 grid on a dark purple-black ground, the plainest small spot (m = n = 0) in the one cell where the seed's shift put it, and ever denser grids of orange-red lobes the larger m and n are. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`supershapes` adds superformula stars, bringing the current catalog from 1022 to 1023 kinds (1024 gallery choices including plain). A chart of 8×8 Gielis-style superformula shapes, one per cell: the column sets the number of folds `m` (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, even values only) and the row sets the sharpness exponent `n` (0.35, 0.5, 0.7, 1, 1.4, 2, 3, 5, from very spiky at the top to nearly round at the bottom). The radius of a shape at the angle `t`, relative to its longest radius, is `(2·(cos⁴(m·t / 4) + sin⁴(m·t / 4)))^(−1 / n)`: 1 at the odd multiples of `t = π / m` (m tips in all), and falling to `2^(−1 / n)` in the valleys between tips (about 0.138 for n = 0.35 and 0.871 for n = 5); the fourth powers and even m keep the radius function smooth across the branch cut of the angle. The tone of a shape grows with column plus row (dark sea green to bright mint), and mint stars and flowers lie on a dark blue-black ground with softened edges and a domed height inside. The seed moves the whole chart around the torus (in whole cells). It is a schematic mathematical chart, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8×8 cells, the series of folds and sharpness values, the disc radius of 0.46, the edge softness of 0.05, the tones (floor 0.14, span 0.7), the mint and dark blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The shape formula is my own simplification (both exponents 4, a = b = 1), not the full Gielis superformula, and I did not compare its parameters with the original paper. One thing worth noting: because the range of `cos⁴ + sin⁴` is [0.5, 1], the smallest ratio of the shape radius is fixed at `2^(−1 / n)`, so the smaller n is, the more needle-like the star, and the tips for n = 0.35 are very thin. The tests recompute the formula in **another, independent form** (`cos⁴x + sin⁴x = 1 − sin²(2x) / 2`, giving the radius `(2 − sin²(2x))^(−1 / n)`) at 8,000 golden-ratio points and compare it with the sampler's colour (inside a shape, more than 0.06 cell from the rim, the shape tone; outside the rim by more than 0.005 disc radius, the gap tone; the soft rim zone in between is not compared), trying all 64 possible shifts and checking that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.01497, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03); they also check that the radius is 1 at a tip and `2^(−1 / n)` in a valley. This shows that the position, size, fold count, sharpness and tone of the shapes agree with the independently written formula, **but not the shape of the soft rim zone** (that zone is covered only by the C1 and bounded-value checks, which pass). My first run of the tests failed on one assertion: I had written the test comment and expectations as 'angle 0 is a tip', but angle 0 is actually a valley and the tips are at `π / m` (the sampler's comment was already right); I fixed the test's comment and expectations and re-ran. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0378).

There is no precomputation at start-up (only the 128² fine grain noise is created); at sampling time `x = fract(u)·8` and `y = fract(v)·8`, the position inside the cell divided by the disc radius gives `(px, py)` and `radius r = hypot(px, py)`, and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 3, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 3, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 8); `t = m·atan2(py, px) / 4`, `edge = (2·(cos⁴t + sin⁴t))^(−1 / n)`, `mask = smoothstep(clamp((edge − r)·discRadius / 0.05))`, `dome = smoothstep(clamp(1 − (r / edge)²))`, `tone = (column + row) / 14`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + toneSpan·tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, `toneSpan` 0.7), height is `0.8·dome·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the shapes and metallic is 0; the retained cache is only a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction or the sampling time (each sample costs one `atan2`, one `cos`, one `sin` and one power). Measured (tool-run): each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (7, 1), (5, 5), (7, 7) and (3, 4), with maximum fit errors of 0.01473/0.01497/0.01479/0.01489 (of 8,000 points per seed, 7,057–7,098 are used for the comparison, 2,129–2,167 of them inside shapes); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 17.07%–17.13%, color is 0.02528–0.02590 to 0.85335–0.85415 with a mean of 0.20254–0.20261, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8583–0.8717 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 17.13%–17.19%, color is 0.02520–0.02528 to 0.85391–0.85458 with a mean of 0.20219–0.20228 and height is at most 0.8600–0.8736 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 28.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.7, 58.1, 64.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0378 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: a regular 8×8 grid of stars and flowers, very spiky in the upper rows and nearly round in the lower rows, with the fold count increasing to the right. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`zernikemodes` adds Zernike modes, bringing the current catalog from 1021 to 1022 kinds (1023 gallery choices including plain). An 8×8 grid of discs, each disc showing one Zernike polynomial, arranged in the OSA / ANSI single-index order (`j = (n(n + 2) + m) / 2`: cell 0 is `n = 0, m = 0`, cells 1 and 2 are `n = 1, m = −1, 1`, cells 3 to 5 are `n = 2, m = −2, 0, 2`, and so on, 64 modes in all, the last being `n = 10, m = 6`). Each mode is a radial polynomial times the cosine (`m ≥ 0`) or sine (`m < 0`) of the azimuth angle, and the radial polynomial is 1 at the rim of the disc so `|Z| ≤ 1`; the tone of a disc is `(1 + Z) / 2` from dark to bright, so each disc contains concentric rings, petals and saddles of light and shade, like a chart of optical aberrations (the n = 0 disc is bright all over). Pale cream discs lie on a dark blue-black ground with softened edges. The seed moves the whole table around the torus (in whole discs). It is a schematic mathematical chart, not a simulation of anything real and not the true wavefront of any optical system.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8×8 cells, the disc radius of 0.46 cell, the edge softness of 0.08, the tones (floor 0.1, span 0.72), the pale cream and dark blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The OSA / ANSI single index and the sign convention of sine and cosine are what I used from memory, **and I did not check them against the standard document this time**; that the Zernike radial polynomial equals 1 at the rim and `|Z| ≤ 1` is a standard theoretical fact that I did not prove here, I only saw in the probe's samples that all output colours lie in [0, 1]. The sampler computes the radial polynomial with the factorial series; the tests recompute it in **another, independent form** — the binomial sum of the Jacobi polynomial (`R = (−1)^k r^|m| P_k^(|m|,0)(1 − 2r²)`, `k = (n − |m|) / 2`) — at radius 0.6 inside every disc at four angles (256 points) and compare it with the sampler's colour, trying all 64 possible shifts and checking that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0134, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03); they also check the indices of the first six modes and the last mode, and the rim value of 1. This shows that the sampler's polynomials, signs and arrangement agree with the independently written formula, **but not that the formula itself matches the standard Zernike definition** (the formula in the tests was also written by me). Because the relief reuses 0.0008 and the height varies little across a disc, the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is only 0.00126 (nearly flat); that is expected and I did not tune it. My first run of the tests failed on one assertion because the mode list held `m = -0` where the expected value had `m = +0` (`toEqual` distinguishes them); I fixed the test (`m + 0`) and re-ran, and also replaced a clumsy `Math.cos(0)` expectation with 1.

At start-up (per sampler) the 64 pairs `(n, m)` are listed in order (n from 0, m from −n to n in steps of 2), and for every mode the powers `n − 2k` and coefficients `(−1)^k (n − k)! / (k! ((n + |m|) / 2 − k)! ((n − |m|) / 2 − k)!)` (k from 0 to `(n − |m|) / 2`) of the radial polynomial are precomputed and kept, with one `Int32Array(64)` each for n and m and small per-mode arrays; at sampling time `x = fract(u)·8` and `y = fract(v)·8`, the position inside the cell divided by the disc radius gives `(px, py)` and `radius r = hypot(px, py)`, and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 2, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 2, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 8); `Z = R(min(r, 1))·cos(m·atan2(py, px))` (m ≥ 0) or `·sin(−m·atan2)` (m < 0), `tone = 0.5 + 0.5·Z`, `mask = smoothstep(clamp((1 − r) / 0.08))`, `dome = smoothstep(clamp(1 − r²))`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + toneSpan·tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.1, `toneSpan` 0.72), height is `0.8·dome·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the discs and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the small per-mode arrays (I did not count the bytes of these). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction or the sampling time (each sample evaluates the polynomial of one cell, at most 6 terms, plus one `atan2` and one `cos` or `sin`). Measured (tool-run): each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (5, 2), (2, 5), (4, 1) and (4, 2), with maximum fit errors of 0.01265/0.01343/0.01269/0.01304; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 16.84%–16.90%, color is 0.02549–0.02579 to 0.83229–0.83345 with a mean of 0.30005–0.30010, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8587–0.8693 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 16.83%–16.86%, color is 0.02517–0.02525 to 0.8337–0.8339 with a mean of 0.30003–0.30012 and height is at most 0.8653–0.8723 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 24.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (82.0, 79.2, 79.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.00126 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the preview: a regular 8×8 grid of discs, each with a different pattern of concentric rings, petals and saddles, the n = 0 disc the brightest. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`rule110` adds rule 110, bringing the current catalog from 1020 to 1021 kinds (1022 gallery choices including plain). It draws the one-dimensional elementary cellular automaton rule 110 as a 96×96 space-time diagram: row 0 is a random row (every cell lights with probability 0.5), and every cell of every following row is decided by the states of the three cells above it (left, centre and right, wrapping around) read as a three-bit number (left = 4, centre = 2, right = 1), taking the matching bit of the rule number 110 to make it lit or dark; each row is a generation, evolving downwards. The result is the typical pattern of dark triangles of different sizes and diagonal gliders (these structures of rule 110 are known, a standard theoretical fact that I did not verify here). Lit cells are orange and dark cells deep purple, as rounded square tiles. The seed decides the random state of row 0 and moves the whole picture sideways; there is no vertical shift (the time axis is fixed). It is a schematic automaton space-time diagram, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; rule 110, the 96×96 size, the density of 0.5 in row 0, the orange and deep purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview; the picture is busy and high-frequency with about four tenths of the area lit, and I did not tune it further). Rule 110 is deterministic, so the tests **can verify the dynamics independently**: the tests read the state of every cell back from its centre colour (a colour above 0.5 is lit, and it must sit within the grain of one of the two tones, an error below 0.03), apply the rule written independently (left = 4, centre = 2, right = 1 as bits) and check that **every cell of rows 1 to 95** follows rule 110 (the number of cells that do not must be 0), and check that about half of row 0 is lit and that 50% to 60% of all cells are lit. Because the rule is translation-invariant, the horizontal shift does not affect this check, so the shift does not have to be found. To make sure the check is not vacuous I changed the rule number to 30 in a temporary probe and got 3,214, 3,218, 3,193 and 3,301 non-conforming cells for the four seeds (0 for rule 110 itself). This verifies that the space-time diagram produced by the sampler obeys the update of rule 110, but the randomness of row 0 (the hash) is not independently verified. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0468).

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(9216)` tone table is built: in row 0 `tones[col] = hash(col, 0, seed ^ salt) < 0.5 ? 0.7 : 0`, and every cell of row `row` forms `4·left + 2·centre + right` from the left, centre and right cells of the row above (wrapping modulo 96) and takes `(110 >> that value) & 1` to decide a tone of 0.7 or 0; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the column index is shifted by an amount decided by `hash(0, 1, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 96): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(9216)` of 73,728 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 204,800 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler in bun at about 1.5 ms (one build each for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7/2, all about 1.5–1.6 ms), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run): for the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) the number of cells that do not follow rule 110 is 0 in every case; 5,121/5,127/5,090/5,256 cells of the table are lit (55.6%/55.6%/55.2%/57.0%); row 0 has 45/47/52/49 lit cells (of 96); the last row has 51/55/55/58 lit cells; the colours match the two tones within a maximum error of 0.0150; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) covers 38.10%–38.25%, color is 0.02549–0.02613 to 0.85415–0.85447 with a mean of 0.38544–0.38724, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8472–0.8475 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area covers 39.75%–41.04%, color is 0.02523–0.02550 to 0.85463–0.85485 with a mean of 0.3917–0.4008 and height is at most 0.8497–0.8503 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 46.5% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05 (33.3% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (108.2, 68.9, 46.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0468 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview: fine orange squares on deep purple with dark triangles of different sizes. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`chromaticant` adds a chromatic ant, bringing the current catalog from 1019 to 1020 kinds (1021 gallery choices including plain). A multi-colour Langton's ant runs on a 96×96 torus: the board starts as all colour 0, the ant stands in the middle facing up, and the rule string is `RRLLLRLLLRRR` (12 colours); at each step the ant looks at the colour c of the cell under it, turns right if `rule[c]` is R and left if it is L, advances the cell's colour to `(c + 1) mod 12` and steps one cell forward (wrapping around); 100,000 steps are made in all. Finally every cell is shown as a rounded square tile with the tone `0.7·colour / 11`: cream to dark teal. The result is a chaotic block in the middle surrounded by large flat regions bounded by straight diagonal and horizontal or vertical lines that wrap around because of the torus (I only describe what I see in the preview and did not analyse the dynamics of this rule). The 12 colours occupy 4,869, 521, 293, 180, 337, 246, 1,288, 292, 234, 275, 319 and 362 of the 9,216 cells (colour 0 the most, then colour 6). The simulation of the ant does not depend on the seed (it is deterministic); the seed only moves the whole board around the torus. It is a schematic simulation result, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 96×96 size, the rule string, the 100,000 steps, the teal and cream colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: with a separate small prototype I ran five rules once each (RLLR for 20,000 steps, LLRR for 20,000, RLR for 12,000, LRRRRRLLR for 60,000 and RRLLLRLLLRRR for 100,000) and viewed the previews of three of them (LRRRRRLLR, RLLR and RRLLLRLLLRRR): RLLR grew only a small symmetric figure in the middle that did not fill the tile; LRRRRRLLR had diamond-shaped lines and a chaotic block; RRLLLRLLLRRR had the largest chaotic block and many wrapped straight lines, so I chose it (for LLRR and RLR I only printed the count of non-zero cells and did not look at a picture). The ant's rule is deterministic, so the tests **can rewrite it independently**: the tests simulate the ant again written differently (direction vectors instead of a heading counter), check that the numbers of cells of the 12 colours are exactly the ones above, rebuild the tone table and, for each seed, compare the colour at every cell centre against all 9,216 possible shifts and check that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). I did not analyse the behaviour of the rule itself (for example whether an ant highway appears), only that the sampler agrees with an independent simulation. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0468). The first version of a test comment described the 4,347 cells with a non-zero colour as 'cells that have been visited', which is wrong (a cell visited 12 times returns to colour 0), and I corrected it after running the tests.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Uint8Array(9216)` colour board is built by running 100,000 steps from `(48, 48)` facing up (see above), after which every cell's tone `0.7·colour / 11` is stored in a `Float64Array(9216)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 0, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 96): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Uint8Array(9216)` of 9,216 B, a `Float64Array(9216)` of 73,728 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 214,016 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler (100,000 steps) in bun at about 29.3 ms (first, including JIT), 9.5 ms, 9.1 ms, 6.9 ms and 1.9 ms (one build each for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7/2), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run): the cell counts of the 12 colours are as above; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (87, 75), (74, 2), (55, 37) and (76, 34), with a maximum fit error of 0.01496–0.01500; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 17.75%–17.89%, color is 0.02549–0.02601 to 0.85372–0.85416 with a mean of 0.23586–0.23604, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8440–0.8460 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 21.15%–21.20%, color is 0.02526–0.02547 to 0.8545–0.8549 with a mean of 0.23939–0.23951 and height is at most 0.8483–0.8503 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 31.7% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (64.4, 73.3, 63.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0468 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview: a dark teal ground with chaotic cream blocks and straight wrapped lines. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`gaussianprimes` adds Gaussian primes, bringing the current catalog from 1018 to 1019 kinds (1020 gallery choices including plain). A 64×64 table is laid out as rounded square tiles, every cell standing for a Gaussian integer `a + bi` (a and b each from −32 to 31, with the origin near the middle of the table), and the cells of Gaussian primes glow: an `a + bi` on an axis (`b = 0` or `a = 0`) is a Gaussian prime when `|a|` (or `|b|`) is a prime leaving remainder 3 on division by 4, and any other `a + bi` is a Gaussian prime when its norm `a² + b²` is an ordinary prime; the other cells stay at the base tone. The glow weakens with the distance to the origin (tone `0.7·(1 − 0.55·√(norm / largest norm))`), so the middle is brighter and the outskirts darker. The 64×64 cells hold 844 Gaussian primes, 24 of them on the axes (±3, ±7, ±11, ±19, ±23, ±31, on the four half-axes); the table is mirror-symmetric about both axes and both diagonals (the row and column at −32 have no symmetric partner because the range is −32 to 31), giving dot lattices of nested diamonds and stars. Rose pink dots lie on a dark purple ground, and the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic number-theory table, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 cells, the norm fade of 0.55, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the rose pink and dark purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler decides primality by trial division; the tests decide Gaussian primality in **another, independent way** — a brute-force search for a Gaussian-integer factor `c + di` of smaller norm (whether both the real and the imaginary part of `(a + bi)(c − di)` are divisible by `c² + d²`) — which is independent of the sampler's standard-theorem formula (on an axis check remainder 3, elsewhere check whether the norm is prime); I did not prove that theorem (the characterisation of Gaussian primes) separately, the tests only show that the two ways agree on all 4096 cells. After rebuilding the whole tone table the tests compare the colour at every cell centre for each seed against all 4096 possible shifts and check that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03), and check 844 primes, 24 of them on the axes, and a few special cases (1 + i is prime; 2, 5, 0 and the units are not; 3 is). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0377). The statistics at 256² and 512² differ (see below) because a cell is only 4 (or 8) pixels wide and the sample points fall at different places within the cells, not because of different seeds; the tests use the 256² values.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(4096)` tone table is built: for every cell take `a = |col − 32|` and `b = |row − 32|`, on an axis check `max(a, b) % 4 === 3` and primality, otherwise check whether `a² + b²` is prime (trial division), and if so `tones[row · 64 + col] = 0.7 · (1 − 0.55·√((a² + b²) / 2048))`, otherwise 0; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 0, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 64): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(4096)` of 32,768 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 163,840 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction time (trial division over 4,096 cells) or the sampling time. Measured (tool-run): 844 Gaussian primes, 24 of them on the axes; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (22, 34), (40, 21), (51, 61) and (51, 37), with a maximum fit error of 0.01499–0.01500; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 14.94%–14.98%, color is 0.05897–0.05967 to 0.8357–0.8397 with a mean of 0.21017–0.21026, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8395–0.8433 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 11.58%–11.63%, color is 0.02517–0.02532 to 0.8353–0.8390 with a mean of 0.18475–0.18484, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8443–0.8462 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 23.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (58.5, 30.3, 49.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: a lattice of rose pink dots on dark purple, brighter in the middle, with a symmetric structure of diamonds and stars. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`fordcircles` adds Ford circles, bringing the current catalog from 1017 to 1018 kinds (1019 gallery choices including plain). Ford circles: for every reduced fraction `n / d` (0 ≤ n < d, denominators d ≤ 12, 46 in all) a disc of radius `1 / (2 d²)` stands on the bottom edge of the tile with its centre at `u = n / d` (the disc of `0 / 1` has a diameter equal to the whole tile height), and a copy mirrored about the middle line of the tile stands on the top edge (91 discs in all, since the big disc of `0 / 1` and its mirror are the same one); the discs of consecutive Farey fractions touch exactly, and between the big discs strings of ever smaller discs line up like stair-stepped fractal beads. The tone of the discs brightens as the denominator shrinks (`0.55·((13 − d) / 12)^1.5`), amber gold discs lie on a dark navy gap ground with softened edges, and the inside of a disc has a domed height. The seed moves the whole picture sideways (by multiples of 1/256). It is a schematic number-theory pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the denominator limit of 12, the 256 sideways shift steps, the edge softness of 0.2, the tones (span 0.55, floor 0.2, exponent 1.5), the amber gold and dark navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: the first version had only one row of discs standing on the bottom edge, and on viewing the preview the strings of small discs appeared along only one edge of the tile (the top edge in the preview) while the gaps between the big discs on the other side were empty, which made the picture asymmetric, so I added the row mirrored about the middle line for the top edge (the second preview, which I viewed, confirmed it: the two rows of small discs meet at the mirror line in symmetric strings of beads). I checked the disc geometry (tangency and non-overlap) with a probe, **not in the tests**: with independently written code I measured, for the 46 pairs of discs of consecutive Farey fractions, a largest difference of 1.1e-16 between the centre distance and the sum of the radii; comparing all pairs of the 91 discs (mirrored and wrapped) the smallest value of distance minus the radius sum is −9.7e-17 (the discs touch and their interiors do not overlap, within floating-point error). The tests compare the sampler with an independently written Ford-circle geometry (reduced fractions picked with the greatest common divisor, centre n / d, radius 1 / (2 d²), tones from the same formula as the preset): at 6,000 golden-ratio points, wherever the point is far enough from every disc edge (squared-radius ratio below 0.75 means inside, above 1.3 means gap, and the soft edge zone in between is not compared) the colour must be within 0.03 of the disc tone (or the gap tone), and all 256 possible sideways shifts are tried and the test checks that **exactly one** fits; this shows that the positions, sizes and tones of the discs follow the formula, **but not the shape of the soft edge zone** (that zone is covered only by the C1 and bounded-value checks). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0315). When I first ran the script that generates the tests it stopped part-way because the Hamming test sits at the end of the file and the search for a following describe failed; nothing had been written, and I fixed the script and re-ran.

At start-up (per sampler) the Euclidean algorithm picks the 46 reduced fractions and three arrays of length 46 (centre, radius, tone) are built; at sampling time `x = fract(u + shift)` and `y = min(fract(v), 1 − fract(v))`, and for every disc the wrapped horizontal distance `dx` and `dy = y − radius` give `s = (dx² + dy²) / radius²`; only discs with `s < 1` contribute (the interiors of the discs do not overlap, so at most one is non-zero): `mask = smoothstep(clamp((1 − s) / 0.2))`, `dome = smoothstep(1 − s)`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.05, `toneFloor` 0.2), height is `0.8·dome·(0.85 + 0.15·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the shift is `floor(hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt) · 256) / 256`; the retained cache is three arrays of 46 numbers plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B. Every sample loops over the 46 discs (I did not measure the time), and I did not measure the construction time either. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run): 46 reduced fractions; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, 133, 45, 240 and 173 (each over 256), with a maximum fit error of 0.01477–0.01488 (about the grain's maximum amplitude of 0.015; about 3,875–3,887 of the 6,000 points are used for the comparison per seed); the total disc area (including the mirrored discs, without softening) is 0.9560 of the tile; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5, which covers the discs of denominator ≤ 4) is 82.45%–82.49%, color is 0.03553–0.03645 to 0.76426–0.76446 with a mean of 0.63341–0.63359, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8205–0.8228 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 82.45%–82.56%, color is 0.03518–0.03558 to 0.76469–0.76490 with a mean of 0.63332–0.63349 and height is at most 0.8234–0.8244 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 26.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (160.5, 136.7, 86.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0315 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: amber gold discs on dark navy, with strings of small discs between the big ones and the two mirrored rows forming symmetric strings of beads. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hammingtable` adds a Hamming distance table, bringing the current catalog from 1016 to 1017 kinds (1018 gallery choices including plain). A 32×32 table is laid out as rounded square tiles: the tone of the tile in row `row` and column `col` is decided by how many bits differ between the binary representations (5 bits) of its two indices — the Hamming distance `popcount(row xor col)` — with distance 0 (the diagonal) the darkest and distance 5 (the two indices are each other's complement) the brightest, with the tone `0.7·(distance / 5)^1.6`. The 32×32 cells hold the distances 0 to 5 in 32, 160, 320, 320, 160 and 32 cells (32 times the binomial coefficients). Because the table uses the binary exclusive or, it repeats the same layout of blocks at every power of two (groups of 2, 4, 8 and 16), like a fractal grid that unfolds a hypercube, with the brightest tiles along one diagonal line. Amber yellow tiles lie on a dark plum gap ground, and the seed moves the whole table around the torus (by a number of cells chosen by the seed). It is a schematic number and bit-operation table, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 32×32 cells, the 5 bits, the tone exponent of 1.6, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the amber yellow and dark plum colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: I first tried 64×64 cells, 6 bits and a tone exponent of 1 and, on viewing the preview, found the tiles too small and the tones concentrated on the middle distances, so the picture was busy and the contrast low; I changed to 32×32 cells, 5 bits and an exponent of 1.6 (I viewed the preview of both versions, once each). Because of the symmetry of the exclusive or, shifting the whole table by 16 cells (half the table) in both directions at once gives exactly the same table, so for every seed there are **two** torus shifts that fit (the true shift and the one with 16 added in both directions); the test checks explicitly that there are exactly these two and that they are related by adding 16 (the half-table shift is a symmetry of the exclusive or, not two independent solutions). The tests rebuild the whole tone table from an independently written bit count (turning `row xor col` into a binary string and counting the ones) and compare it with the sampler's colour at the centre of every cell (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0177).

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(1024)` tone table is built, `tones[row · 32 + col] = 0.7 · (popcount(row xor col) / 5)^1.6`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 0, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 32): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(1024)` of 8,192 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 139,264 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Construction is only 1,024 bit counts and one noise table, **I did not measure the construction time**, and sampling is a constant number of operations, which I did not measure either. Measured (tool-run): every seed has two fitting torus shifts, for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 (30, 2) and (14, 18), (10, 13) and (26, 29), (21, 12) and (5, 28), (26, 9) and (10, 25), with a maximum fit error of 0.01498–0.01499 (equal to the grain's maximum amplitude of 0.015); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is always 10.94%, color is 0.02568–0.02574 to 0.8530–0.8535 with a mean of 0.2910–0.2911, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8401–0.8467 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is always 13.48%, color is 0.02509–0.02529 to 0.8540–0.8545 with a mean of 0.2955 and height is at most 0.8440–0.8475 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 24.7% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ, and 77.9% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (89.4, 66.1, 56.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0177 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview: amber yellow tiles on dark plum, with a brightest band of tiles running diagonally and nested block structure. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`aggregationfrost` adds aggregation frost, bringing the current catalog from 1015 to 1016 kinds (1017 gallery choices including plain). It runs diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) on a 96×96 torus: the cell at the centre is the first member, every further particle starts on a random free cell and steps at random to one of its four neighbours (wrapping around), sticking as soon as it shares an edge with a member of the cluster; 900 particles in all (the centre plus 899 random walkers) form a fractal, branching cluster like frost or a tree. Every particle has an 'age' given by the order in which it stuck, and the tone fades from the centre (the oldest) towards the branch tips; it shows thin ice-blue branches on a dark blue-black ground, one cluster per tile that does not join neighbouring tiles (the farthest branches are only about 37–44 cells from the centre while the torus half-width is 48). The seed decides every particle's start and every step's direction, so every seed gives a completely different branching pattern. It is a schematic simulation result, not a simulation of real frost or Lichtenberg figures. The catalog also has the similarly named `dendriticfrost` and `frost`, which are different materials unrelated to this simulated aggregation.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 900 particles, the 96×96 size, the cap of 60,000 steps per walk, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (line 0.72, age floor 0.3), the ice-blue and dark blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). I first used a separate small prototype (64×64 with 520 particles, only to confirm the method and its speed) to check that DLA is feasible and then changed to 96×96 and 900 particles. I did not check whether any walk reached the cap of 60,000 steps (in which case it is abandoned and the particle starts again), and I did not check whether the fractal dimension of the cluster matches the literature value for DLA, so I do not claim it is 'standard DLA', only the result of this implementation of the algorithm. The tests cannot reproduce the random walks independently (the hash random numbers are internal to the sampler), so I **did not rewrite the aggregation algorithm independently**: the tests read the occupied cells back from the node colours, use an independent breadth-first search to check that the cluster is connected and has exactly 900 cells, and that the colour falls with the graph distance from the centre (a correlation below −0.6), **which shows that the cluster really is a connected tree-like structure and that the age tone has the right direction, but does not prove that the random walks are uniform**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0377). My first attempt at generating the test failed part-way because one expected string did not match (the lower height bound of the percolation test is 0.98, not 0.99); nothing had been written, and I fixed it and re-ran.

At start-up (per sampler) the centre cell `(48, 48)` is set as the first member of the cluster (tone 1), and for every particle `particle = 1 … 899` the code repeats: the starting cell is chosen with `hash(particle, attempt, seed ^ salt)` (if it is already occupied, the next attempt is tried), the walk lasts at most 60,000 steps, in each step the particle sticks if it shares an edge with the cluster (one of its four neighbours is occupied: the cell is marked occupied with tone `1 − particle / 900`), and otherwise it moves in one of four directions (wrapping) chosen by `hash(particle × 65537 + attempt, step, seed ^ (salt + 3))`; at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the occupancy map and `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))` re-sharpens it, while a second `latticeField` blends the age tone map: color is `0.05 + 0.72·line·(0.3 + 0.7·age) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·line·(0.7 + 0.3·age) + 0.2·grain`, roughness drops by 0.2 on the line (base 0.4), AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is two `Float64Array(9216)` (occupancy and age) plus a `Float64Array(128²)`, 278,528 B, with a build-time `Uint8Array(9216)` occupancy table, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler in bun at about 150 ms (first), 135 ms, 126 ms and 130 ms (one run per seed), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: 900 cells are occupied and for all four seeds all 900 can be reached from the centre over four-neighbour edges (the cluster is connected); the largest graph distance in the cluster is 59/62/51/59; the farthest cell from the centre (shortest torus distance) is 41.1/40.5/36.9/44.0 cells away; the colours of the occupied nodes are 0.2564–0.7794, the brightest empty node is 0.0651 and the centre node is 0.7561–0.7733; the correlation between graph distance and colour is −0.7945/−0.7536/−0.8800/−0.8088; on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 3.95%–4.06%, color is 0.0356–0.0358 to 0.7725–0.7758 with a mean of 0.0922–0.0925, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9697–0.9848 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 3.97%–4.05%, color is 0.0352–0.0353 to 0.7734–0.7779 with a mean of 0.0922–0.0925 and height is at most 0.9795–0.9870 relief; the occupied cells of seeds 0 and 1 differ in 14.8% of positions; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (23.0, 31.2, 45.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): frost-flower-like ice-blue branches on a dark blue-black ground, one per tile, brighter near the centre and darker at the tips. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`cyclicwaves` adds cyclic waves, bringing the current catalog from 1014 to 1015 kinds (1016 gallery choices including plain). It runs an eight-state cyclic cellular automaton on a 96×96 torus: every cell has a state from 0 to 7, started at random; in every synchronous step a cell in state k advances to `k + 1` (7 is followed by 0) if at least one of its four neighbours up, down, left or right (von Neumann neighbourhood, wrapping) is already in state `k + 1`, and otherwise stays; 150 steps are run. The result is rings of waves that follow one another (every state right after the previous one), forming spirals and labyrinth-like waves wherever the random start happened to be locally ordered; states 0 to 7 map to eight tones from dark indigo to amber yellow, and the wave fronts show short steep ramps from bright to dark. The eight states each take about an equal share (11.96%–13.19% per state across the four seeds), and about 97% of neighbouring cells differ by at most one state (only 37.5% at the random start). The seed decides the starting states, so every seed gives completely different waves. It is a schematic automaton snapshot, not a simulation of chemical waves or of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8 states, the von Neumann neighbourhood, the threshold of 1, the 150 steps, the 96×96 size, the tone (span 0.72), the indigo and amber yellow colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: I first tried a few rules with a separate small prototype (Moore neighbourhood with threshold 2 or 3 and so on): after 100 steps the Moore neighbourhood with threshold 2 or 3 gave a share of neighbours differing by at most one state of only 0.18–0.68 (0.684 for 8 states with threshold 2, 0.371 with threshold 3; 0.242 for 12 states with threshold 3; 0.182 for 16 states with threshold 3; 0.344 for 10 states with threshold 2), the Moore neighbourhood with threshold 1 (6, 8, 10 and 12 states, 150 to 250 steps) gave 0.74–0.88, and the von Neumann neighbourhood with threshold 1 gave 0.95–0.98 (0.952 for 5 states and 0.976 for 8 states), so I chose the von Neumann neighbourhood with 8 states; every setting was run once with the same seed, so this is a rough comparison; the prototype's random numbers differ from the sampler's hash and were used only to choose the rule. I looked at only one preview. The tests cannot reproduce the dynamics independently (the hash random numbers are internal to the sampler), so I **did not rewrite the update rule of the cellular automaton independently**: the tests read the state of every cell back from the sampler's node colours (the nearest of the eight tones), check that the colours sit on the eight tones, and check statistics (about 97% of neighbour pairs differ by at most one state, every cell has a neighbour whose state is one more or one less than its own, and each of the eight states has a share between 11.5% and 14%), **which shows that the result is not random noise, that all states occur and that the colouring logic is right, but does not prove the update rule itself is right**. In the first draft of a test comment I wrote the share of neighbour pairs within one state at the random start as 'about a quarter', which is wrong (with 8 states it is 3/8 = 37.5%) and I corrected it before the commit. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0120).

At start-up (per sampler) the initial state of every cell is `floor(hash(x, y, seed ^ salt) · 8)`, followed by 150 synchronous steps: a cell moves to `(own + 1) mod 8` if any of its four (wrapped) neighbours is in that successor state and otherwise stays, swapping two `Uint8Array(9216)` buffers; afterwards every cell's tone is `state / 7`; at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the tone map: color is `0.05 + 0.72·tone + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·tone + 0.2·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(9216)` of 73,728 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 204,800 B in all, with two build-time `Uint8Array(9216)` buffers, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler (150 steps) in bun at about 78 ms (first), 39 ms, 44 ms and 40 ms (one run per seed), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: among the 96×96 nodes (sampled at the nodes) each state has 1,102–1,216 cells (11.96%–13.19%); the share of neighbour pairs differing by at most one state is 0.9779/0.9746/0.9782/0.9715; every cell has at least one neighbour whose state is one more or one less than its own (all 9,216 cells for all four seeds); the colours at all 9,216 nodes match the eight tones within a maximum error of 0.0150 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03); on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 35.93%–37.11%, color is 0.0378–0.0398 to 0.7800–0.7816 with a mean of 0.4049–0.4120, roughness is always 0.4, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9792–0.9899 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 36.22%–37.50%, color is 0.0366–0.0389 to 0.7818–0.7831 with a mean of 0.4049–0.4120 and height is at most 0.9862–0.9884 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 49.3% of the cells with state ≥ 4 are at different positions and 46.5% of the nodes with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (109.8, 93.9, 67.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0120 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7): spiral and labyrinth-like waves in indigo and amber yellow, the wave fronts showing short gradients. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`isingdomains` adds Ising domains, bringing the current catalog from 1013 to 1014 kinds (1015 gallery choices including plain). It is a snapshot of Metropolis dynamics of the two-dimensional Ising model on a 64×64 torus: every cell is an up or down spin, started at random and run for 150 sweeps in checkerboard order at a temperature of 2.35 (coupling and Boltzmann constants set to 1; the critical temperature of the two-dimensional Ising model is about 2.269, a standard value that I did not verify here); a flip that changes the energy by dE is accepted when `dE ≤ 0` or when a hash-derived uniform number is below `exp(−dE/temperature)`; the result is domains of aligned spins: up is bright and down is dark, lightly tinted by the fraction of the four neighbours that share a cell's spin so that the domain walls are darker, in a lime-green camouflage-like pattern. The share of up spins of the four seeds lies between 24.3% and 55.3%, and the share of neighbour pairs with equal spins is about 79%–83% (50% at the random start). The seed decides the starting configuration and the random numbers of every step, so every seed gives a completely different pattern. It is a schematic snapshot of a model, not a simulation or measurement of a magnetic material, and it is not guaranteed to have reached equilibrium.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the temperature of 2.35, the 150 sweeps, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (spin 0.6, agreement 0.12), the lime green and dark green colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, whose pattern is mostly dark because it leans towards the majority spin). The tests cannot reproduce the dynamics independently (the hash random-number stream is internal to the sampler), so I **did not rewrite the Metropolis update independently**: the tests read the spins back from the sampler's node colours, check that the colours agree with (spin, number of equal neighbours), and check statistics (the share of equal neighbour pairs is about 0.78–0.84 and not the 0.5 of a random start; 100–150 same-spin regions; a largest region above 1,800 cells; an up share between 0.2 and 0.6), **which shows that the result is not random noise and that the colouring logic is right, but does not prove it is correct Metropolis sampling, and equilibrium was not verified**. One test failed along the way: I copied the roughness check from the percolation test (expecting it to drop to about 0.2 on lines) but this material has a constant roughness of 0.4, so the failing part was the copied expectation; I had met the same problem with the sandpile identity and still missed it this time; after changing it to check that the roughness equals the preset value the test passed. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0244).

At start-up (per sampler) the initial spins (±1) are decided by `hash(x, y, seed ^ salt) < 0.5`, followed by 150 sweeps, each split into two half-sweeps (the two parities of the checkerboard; cells of one parity are not adjacent and can be updated independently): for every cell the code sums the wrapped neighbour spins `around`, computes the energy change `dE = 2·spin·around` and flips when `dE ≤ 0` or `hash(cell, sweep × 2 + parity, seed ^ salt + 2) < exp(−dE / 2.35)`; afterwards it records for every cell whether it is up (`marks`) and the fraction of its four neighbours that share its spin (`agree`); at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the up map and `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))` re-sharpens it, while a second `latticeField` blends the agreement map: color is `0.05 + 0.6·line + 0.12·agree + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.7·line + 0.1·agree + 0.2·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is two `Float64Array(4096)` (the up map and the agreement) plus a `Float64Array(128²)`, 196,608 B, plus a 4,096 B `Int8Array` of spins. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler (150 sweeps) in bun at about 102 ms (first), 64 ms, 65 ms and 65 ms (one run per seed), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: the share of up spins is 55.3%/24.3%/52.4%/32.5%; the share of neighbour pairs with equal spins is 0.8164/0.8296/0.8115/0.7908; there are 109/144/133/127 4-connected same-spin regions, the largest has 2,153/3,058/1,863/2,683 cells and the second largest 1,590/573/1,834/619; the colours at all 4,096 nodes match the independent model of the test (spin and number of equal neighbours) within a maximum error of 0.0150 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03); on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.4) covers 55.39%/23.71%/52.35%/32.05%, color is 0.0415–0.0441 to 0.7830–0.7843 with a mean of 0.2931–0.4803 (it varies with the seed), roughness is always 0.4, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9895–0.9962 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 55.37%/23.85%/52.35%/32.17%, color is 0.0370–0.0388 to 0.7839–0.7846 with a mean of 0.2929–0.4803 and height is at most 0.9956–0.9983 relief; the up spins of seeds 0 and 1 differ in 54.0% of positions; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (77.6, 100.8, 36.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0244 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): lime-green domains on dark green with pixelated rounded edges and many isolated small dots. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`percolationclusters` adds percolation clusters, bringing the current catalog from 1012 to 1013 kinds (1014 gallery choices including plain). It runs critical site percolation on a 64×64 torus: every cell is occupied or not according to a hash, with an occupation probability of 0.5927 (the standard value I know for the critical probability of site percolation on the square lattice, which I did not verify here); occupied cells that are neighbours up, down, left or right (wrapping around) form a cluster, found with union-find; every occupied cell is toned by `ln(cluster size) / ln(largest cluster size)` (the largest cluster is brightest, a lone cell is darkest but still brighter than an empty cell), and empty cells are the dark ground, giving a camouflage-like pattern in sulfur yellow. Because of random fluctuation the actual occupied fraction is slightly below the target (2,358–2,414 cells for the four seeds, 57.6%–58.9%). The seed decides which cells are occupied, so every seed gives a completely different pattern. It is a schematic random pattern, not a simulation or measurement of real percolation.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the occupation probability of 0.5927, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (line 0.72, tone floor 0.3), the sulfur yellow and dark olive colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). Two of my test expectations were wrong at first: the lit-area range in my first test was written from probe numbers for `color > 0.3` while the test uses `color > 0.5`, so the first run failed (0.4475 < 0.55); after using the range measured with `color > 0.5` (44.75%–48.62% on a 256² grid) it passed; later the mean range failed once because I had computed only three seeds and missed seed 7 (0.3844), and I relaxed it to 0.38. Both were mistakes in my test expectations, not sampler problems. The cluster labelling of this material is checked by the test by reading the occupied cells back from the sampler's node colours, relabelling the clusters with an independent flood-fill algorithm and computing the expected colours, so it verifies the cluster logic (including the torus wrap) **but not the hash-determined occupancy itself**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0260).

At start-up, for every cell of the `64 × 64` grid the code decides occupancy with `hash(x, y, seed ^ salt) < 0.5927`, merges every occupied cell with its occupied right and lower neighbours (wrapping) using union-find (with path compression), counts the size of every cluster, `largest` is the size of the largest cluster (at least 2), and an occupied cell gets mark 1 and tone `ln(cluster size) / ln(largest)`; at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the occupancy map and `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))` re-sharpens it, while a second `latticeField` blends the tone map: color is `0.05 + 0.72·line·(0.3 + 0.7·tone) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·line·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.2·grain`, roughness drops by 0.2 on the line (base 0.4), AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is two `Float64Array(4096)` (occupancy and tone) plus a `Float64Array(128²)`, 196,608 B, with build-time scratch arrays (occupied 4,096 B, parents 16,384 B, cluster sizes 16,384 B), all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample does a constant number of operations; I did not measure the time. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: the independent flood-fill algorithm finds 2,358/2,414/2,391/2,408 occupied cells, 105–138 clusters, a largest cluster of 1,212–1,846 cells, a second largest of 72–639, 66–78 lone-cell clusters, and a largest cluster that covers all 64 rows (four seeds) and all 64 columns (three seeds; seed 1 covers 50); the colours at all 4,096 nodes match the independent model within a maximum error of 0.0150 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03); on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 44.75%–48.62%, color is 0.0357–0.0360 to 0.7837–0.7842 with a mean of 0.3844–0.3984, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9929–0.9962 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 40.83%–44.44%, color is 0.0352–0.0354 to 0.7844–0.7846 with a mean of 0.3840–0.3979 and height is at most 0.9974–0.9988 relief; the occupied cells of seeds 0 and 1 differ in 49.5% of positions; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (112.7, 107.6, 48.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0260 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): a camouflage-like sulfur-yellow pattern on dark olive, with the large cluster in bright yellow and small clusters darker. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`voronoifacets` adds Voronoi facets, bringing the current catalog from 1011 to 1012 kinds (1013 gallery choices including plain). The same Voronoi plates as `voronoicells` (one jittered site per cell of an 8×8 grid, soft-weight partition, 64 plates and dark thin seams), but a plate does not have a single tone: it has a linear gradient in a random direction (facet-like): every site has its own tone and gradient direction and size (up to ±0.35 of tone change per cell width), so the tone inside a plate shifts from darker on one side to brighter on the other, like the facets of an emerald or gem; in emerald green, with seams that are still dark, rough (the roughness rises by 0.4) and AO-darkened. The seed decides the sites, tones and gradients. It is a schematic faceted-gem look, not a real mineral, and nothing real was compared.
