`tulle` adds tulle, bringing the current catalog from 978 to 979 kinds (980 gallery choices including plain). A hexagonal honeycomb net knitted from fine ivory threads on a dark purple-black ground: pointy-top hexagons of circumradius 1, 7 columns × 8 rows (56 hexagons, 168 segments with each shared edge stored once) filling the tile; each thread is a compact-support quartic profile and the knots where three threads meet are brighter because the profiles add up. To let the honeycomb tile the square torus evenly, the horizontal and vertical periods are in the ratio `7√3 : 12`, which stretches the hexagons by about 1.04% (they are not regular). The seed only shifts the whole net around the torus (in steps of 1/64 of the tile). It is a schematic net textile, not a photograph of real tulle, and it is not translucent (the dark ground is just the colour behind the mesh).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 7 columns × 4 row pairs, the thread radius of 0.15, gain 1.8, the ivory and dark purple tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices. `sacksspiral` adds a Sacks spiral, bringing the current catalog from 977 to 978 kinds (979 gallery choices including plain). On a dark navy-black ground the integers 1 to 500 are laid out as dots on a Sacks spiral: the integer `n` sits on an Archimedean spiral at radius `0.45·√(n/500)` (in tile units) and angle `2π√n`, so the perfect squares line up along one ray; primes (95 of them) are bright gold dots and composites are dim gold-brown dots, with the primes particularly dense along a few curved arms. The spiral is centred in the tile and does not reach the tile edge, so tiles do not overlap; on the torus every tile holds one disc-shaped spiral. The seed only turns the whole spiral by a whole number of degrees (0 to 359). It is a schematic number-theory pattern, not a star chart or a photograph.

`divisorcount` adds a divisor-count table, bringing the current catalog from 975 to 976 kinds (977 gallery choices including plain). 48×48 rounded-square tiles; cell (col, row) stands for the integer `n = row × 48 + col + 1` (1 to 2304) and is toned by the number of divisors `d(n)`: primes (`d = 2`, 342 of them) are dim, composite numbers with many divisors (highly composite numbers) glow, and the largest `d` in the table is 40 (at `n = 1680`); because each row has 48 cells, a multiple of 12, the columns holding multiples of 12 form conspicuous bright vertical bars, with fainter bars for multiples of 6, 4 and so on. The seed only moves the whole table around the torus, so the statistics stay the same and only the position changes. It is a schematic number-theory table, not a mineral or a photographed material.

`juliatiles` adds Julia tiles, bringing the current catalog from 973 to 974 kinds (975 gallery choices including plain). A mosaic of a Julia set (`c = −0.8 + 0.156i`) made of 64×64 rounded-square tiles: cell (col, row) takes the complex number at its centre (real and imaginary parts both from −1.6 to 1.6) as `z₀` and iterates `z → z² + c`, and its tone is the escape iteration count (`|z| > 2`, at most 64) over 64 under a square root, from dark red-brown (fast escape) to bright orange (many iterations before escaping, near the set boundary); cells that never escape (404 of them, about 9.9%) are the darkest brown-black. The tiles are raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO), and the seed only moves the whole table around the torus. With only 64×64 resolution it is a pixel-art Julia set; it shares the sampler branch of `mandelbrottiles` and differs only in the start point and the constant.

`mandelbrottiles` adds Mandelbrot tiles, bringing the current catalog from 972 to 973 kinds (974 gallery choices including plain). A mosaic of the Mandelbrot set made of 64×64 rounded-square tiles: cell (col, row) iterates `z → z² + c` at the centre `c` of its small patch of the complex plane (real part from −2.2 to 0.8, imaginary part from −1.5 to 1.5), and its tone is the escape iteration count (`|z| > 2`, at most 48) over 48 under a square root, from dark blue (fast escape) to bright cyan-blue (many iterations before escaping, near the set boundary); cells that never escape (726 of them, about 17.7%) are the darkest blue-black. With only 64×64 resolution it is a pixel-art Mandelbrot set, and the set is not continuous across the torus seam, so it is not a seamless fractal.

`rhodoneatable` adds a rose-curve table, bringing the current catalog from 971 to 972 kinds (973 gallery choices including plain). A pink-neon table of rhodonea curves: 6×6 cells, where cell (col, row) draws `r = cos(k·θ)` with `k = (col + 1)/(row + 1)` (θ from 0 to 2π·(row + 1), so every rational k closes), from single circles through three- and four-petal roses and many-petal flowers to tangled rings, with a faint glow on a dark purple-black ground; the seed only rotates all the roses by one angle (0 to 0.5 radians). It is a mathematical pattern and not a real neon tube (no tube width variation, end electrodes or reflections). The diagonal cells with k = 1 are a small circle through the cell centre.

`primesieve` adds the sieve of Eratosthenes, bringing the current catalog from 969 to 970 kinds (971 gallery choices including plain). A 32×32 grid of rounded-square tiles standing for the integers 1 to 1024: primes (172 of them) are bright gold, 1 is dim, and a composite is toned `0.4·(1 − 1/p)` by its smallest prime factor `p` (multiples of 2 are darkest and composites with larger factors slightly brighter), so the multiples of 2, 3, 5 and 7 leave regular vertical bars and diagonals on an olive ground with the primes scattered among them. The tiles are raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO), and the seed only moves the whole table around the torus. It is a number-theory pattern, not any real material; the contrast between composites is low, so it reads as gold dots on an olive ground.

A 32×32 grid of rounded-square tiles where cell (col, row) stands for the integer `n = row·32 + col + 1` (1 to 1024) and its tone is the number of Collatz steps (halve an even n, triple an odd n and add 1) needed to reach 1 divided by 178 (the longest below 1025 is 178 steps for n = 871), varying continuously from dark purple to warm orange. It looks like structured noise (neighbouring integers have subtly related step counts, but the whole is close to random); it is not any real material, only a mathematical pattern.

`modulartable` adds a modular multiplication table, bringing the current catalog from 965 to 966 kinds (967 gallery choices including plain). A mosaic of 31×31 rounded-square tiles where the tone of cell (col, row) comes from the mod-11 multiplication-table residue `((a + col)·(b + row)) mod 11` (11 steps from dark purple to golden yellow, with the seed choosing the offsets a and b), the tiles raised and the gaps darker with occlusion (AO). It is not any real mosaic or tiling, only a mathematical pattern.

Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 512² grid: the light area (color>0.5) covers 35.6%–36.9%, color is 0.0351–0.0354 to 0.9345–0.9347 with a mean of 0.369–0.379, roughness is a constant 0.5, the lowest AO is 0.6 and height is at most 0.8755–0.8791 relief; the tones at the 961 tile centres match the multiplication table (exactly one offset pair (a, b) per seed: (10, 1), (2, 9), (1, 3) and (1, 1) for the four seeds, with a maximum error of 0.0178–0.0185, the amplitude of the fine grain); the light masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 36.7% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (109.0, 86.0, 67.8) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0412. `elementaryautomata` adds elementary cellular automata, bringing the current catalog from 964 to 965 kinds (966 gallery choices including plain). Four Wolfram elementary automata side by side on an amber LED matrix (each band 32 rows by 128 columns with the columns joined on a ring): rule 30 (the chaotic triangle from a single live cell), rule 90 (the Sierpinski triangle), rule 110 (a complex asymmetric structure) and rule 184 (diagonal traffic-flow stripes from a repeating "110" start pattern); the seed only rotates the columns of the whole picture and the pattern itself is fixed. Each cell is a rounded-square LED and unlit LEDs stay dark brown. Because the columns form a ring, the triangles of rules 30, 90 and 110 do not reach the edge within 128 columns, so they look the same as on an infinitely wide row.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 128 columns, the 32 rows per band, the four rules and start patterns, the amber tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices. It was adopted from the first preview; the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is only 0.0038 (relief 0.001) and was not adjusted.

`gameoflife` adds Conway's Game of Life, bringing the current catalog from 963 to 964 kinds (965 gallery choices including plain). Each cell is a rounded-square LED, and unlit LEDs stay dark.

`hilbertcurve` adds a Hilbert curve, bringing the current catalog from 962 to 963 kinds (964 gallery choices including plain). One cyan circuit trace on a dark navy ground follows an order-4 Hilbert space-filling curve: each of the 16×16 cells is visited exactly once, and the end is joined to the start across the tile seam to close the loop (the start and end of a Hilbert curve are neighbouring cells on a torus); the line is about half a cell wide with a faint glow outside it. The seed picks one of the eight square symmetries (mirror and transpose) and shifts the curve around the torus, so the statistics stay the same and only the orientation and position change. It is not a real circuit board (no pads, vias or multiple layers).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or circuit-board photograph cited and no photograph compared; the order of 4, the half-cell line width, the tanh sharpness of 8, the cyan tones and the 0.2 m nominal tile are authored choices. `quasicrystal` adds a quasicrystal-style interference pattern, bringing the current catalog from 961 to 962 kinds (963 gallery choices including plain). Five plane waves with integer wave vectors at nearly 72° steps interfere into a blue-and-white pattern that looks five-fold symmetric: dark blue dots, pentagon rings and star-like shapes over a pale blue ground. Because every wave vector is an integer, the pattern is **exactly periodic over the tile**, so it is an approximation by five-wave interference and not a true quasicrystal or Penrose tiling (the vector lengths are 14 and about 13.6 and the angles are 0°, 72.9°, 144.0°, 216.0° and 287.1°, only approximating equal 72° steps); the seed changes only the wave phases and the statistics stay the same.

`invaders` adds arcade invaders, bringing the current catalog from 955 to 956 kinds (957 gallery choices including plain). Arcade-style pixel aliens on a green LED matrix panel: three rows with one design each (8×8, 11×8 and 12×8 pixels), repeated 3 times per row on a 42×33 LED grid; each LED is a rounded square and unlit LEDs stay dark green. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.001 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 512² grid: color is 0.0305–0.0307 to 0.8688–0.8691, lit area (color>0.5) covers 18.0%, the mean is 0.2445, roughness is 0.150–0.350 and height is at most 0.9976–0.9987 relief; of the 1,386 LED nodes 426 are lit, the brightest unlit node is 0.1507 and the dimmest lit node is 0.8496, with no node between 0.3 and 0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (41.2, 71.4, 35.4) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0588. `fairisle` adds Fair Isle knitting, bringing the current catalog from 954 to 955 kinds (956 gallery choices including plain). A schematic of a Nordic Fair Isle knitted sweater pattern: 40×30 stitches, each a slanted V-shaped stitch; the pattern is made of horizontal bands in a 15-row group (solid bands, alternating peerie-dot bands and a diamond motif with an open centre repeated every 8 stitches) in one dark blue and one pale grey, with a 160² noise for fine fuzz. A dedicated sampler: at build time it computes a 40×30 0/1 stitch map from the rules (one stitch per lattice node; rows with `y % 15` of 0, 3, 11 and 14 are solid, 1 and 12 are even stitches, 2 and 13 are odd stitches, and 4 to 10 are a diamond ring where `|x%8 − 3.5| + |y%15 − 7|` lies in (1.5, 3.5]); it blends the map with `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) and re-sharpens with `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(7·(pattern − 0.5))`, so colour edges stay C-infinity inside each stitch; the stitch shape is a cos² column bulge `((0.5 + 0.5·cos(2π·40·u))^1.6)` times a leg ridge `0.5 + 0.5·cos(2π·(30·v + 0.22·sin(2π·40·u)))` whose phase leans with the column position to form the V; color is `(0.22 + 0.6·yarn)·(0.78 + 0.22·ridge) + 0.05·(fuzz − 0.5)`; height is `0.8·ridge + 0.2·fuzz`; roughness is a constant 0.92; metallic is 0; the cache totals 40×30 + 160² = 26,800 Float64 values / 214,400 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 512² grid: color is 0.1472–0.1477 to 0.8426–0.8430, dark (color<0.4) covers 37.5%, the mean is 0.4862–0.4863 and height is at most 0.9938–0.9975 relief; every stitch node matches the rules (720 of 1,200 stitches light and 480 dark, none between 0.4 and 0.6); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (129.1, 132.3, 144.0) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0668. `mackerel` adds mackerel, bringing the current catalog from 953 to 954 kinds (955 gallery choices including plain). Broken, curving dark blue wavy bands on a blue-green fish back, stacked along v (dark-light changes occur about 2.5 times more often along v than along u), with band shapes distorted by slow noise so they are irregular and a noise gate that breaks or fades some bands; the bands are slightly rougher and scales are a fine grain. `hestain` adds H&E-stained tissue, bringing the current catalog from 952 to 953 kinds (954 gallery choices including plain). A schematic of a microscope slide of hematoxylin-and-eosin stained tissue: a pale pink-violet cytoplasm with mottle and fibre streaks along v, scattered with dark purple oval nuclei whose positions and shapes come from the spot regime of periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion (a high threshold leaves only the cores), each with a very faint pale halo. It is not real histology: there are no cell membranes, no chromatin structure inside nuclei, no cell-type differences, vessels or tissue layers, the nuclei are more evenly spread than in real tissue, and because of the single dark-to-light gradient the cytoplasm is lavender rather than eosin pink.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source, histology atlas or measurement cited and no photograph compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters equal `cheetahfur`'s (feed 0.04, kill 0.065, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the nucleus threshold of 0.6 (higher than cheetahfur's 0.5, so the nuclei are smaller), the sharpness, the halo, the purple and pink tones and the 0.05 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real tissue. In the first preview the cytoplasm was a dark lavender (0.72); I raised the base to 0.8 and lowered the halo to 0.04 (also so that the sum of tones stays inside [0, 1]), and it is still lavender rather than pink, which is a limit of a single gradient.

It reuses `latticeField` and `grayScott`. A dedicated sampler takes the smooth nucleus mask `nucleus = 0.5 + 0.5·tanh(12·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.6 ± 0.1 moving with a slow 5×5 noise); the halo is a thin band around a lower iso-level, `exp(−((pattern − level + 0.14)/0.1)²)·(1 − nucleus)` (C-infinity); color is `0.8 + 0.14·(14×14 noise − 0.5) + 0.1·(110×26 fibre noise − 0.5) − 0.62·nucleus + 0.04·halo + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`; height is `0.6·nucleus + 0.4·grain`; roughness rises by 0.1 on nuclei; the cache totals 96² + 7² + 5² + 14² + 110×26 + 128² = 28,730 Float64 values / 229,840 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses about 294,912 B of scratch arrays, of which only v is kept). Defaults are a 0.05 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 190–296 ms and 512² maps about 281 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark).

This is a reaction-diffusion stripe pattern and **not a fingerprint** (fingerprint ridges are much finer and have whorls and bifurcations), nor real printing or ink; the preview has a single ink-to-paper gradient.

`cheetahfur` adds cheetah fur, bringing the current catalog from 949 to 950 kinds (951 gallery choices including plain). Black oval spots on short tawny fur, where the spot positions, sizes and shapes come from a periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion simulation, so they are irregular but similarly spaced like natural spots rather than random dots or a fixed grid; the fur carries fine fibres along v and the spots are slightly rougher. It is not a real cheetah's coat gradient, the pale halo around spots, white belly fur or fur direction, and the preview has only one tawny-to-black gradient.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of cheetah markings. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters (feed 0.04, kill 0.065, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the spot threshold and sharpness, the warp amount, the fur and spot tones and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real cheetah. It is the first material in this engine that runs a simulation while its sampler is built; every other material is still a pure noise function.

A dedicated sampler plus two shared helpers: `latticeField(values, nx, ny)` is a periodic lattice sampler (the same smoothstep blend as the existing `cachedNoise`, C1; `cachedNoise` now calls it), and `grayScott(size, seedCells, feed, kill, steps, seed)` runs Gray-Scott on a periodic size×size grid (Du 0.2097, Dv 0.105, dt 1; only additions, subtractions and multiplications are used, with no transcendental functions, so the bits do not depend on the engine). The initial perturbation is one 3×3 block per jittered `seedCells×seedCells` cell so that no seed can start as a long band, and the inhibitor concentration is normalised to [0, 1]. Sampling looks the pattern up after a light `warpField` distortion (±0.015 UV) and takes a smooth spot mask `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(7·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.5 ± 0.1 moving with a 5×5 slow noise, so spot sizes differ slightly); fur color is `0.86·(1 − spot) + 0.05·spot` plus a 200×28 fibre noise stretched along v and a 128² fine grain; the cache totals 96² + 6² + 5² + 200×28 + 128² = 31,261 Float64 values / 250,088 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses four 96² scratch arrays u, v, nextU and nextV, about 294,912 B, of which only v is kept). Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 169–176 ms and 512² maps about 271 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark). Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement).

`jade` adds jade, bringing the current catalog from 948 to 949 kinds (950 gallery choices including plain). This material is an authored schematic of the general look of polished nephrite jade. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts of the noise fields, the cloud weights, the iso-contour positions and widths of the veins, the dark and light green tones, roughness and the 0.15 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real jade.

`spectrogram` adds spectrogram, bringing the current catalog from 947 to 948 kinds (949 gallery choices including plain). A spectrogram-style surface on a deep blue ground: 12 horizontal yellow harmonic lines bent into waves by vibrato, 5 vertical broadband burst bands and scattered speckle, with a time-frequency energy field deciding where it shows (patches fade). It is not a real audio spectrum, real harmonic ratios, time/frequency scales, a colour-scale legend or text; every harmonic has the same vibrato depth (real higher harmonics wobble more), and colour is a single linear dark-blue-to-bright-yellow gradient rather than the multi-colour scales common on real spectrograms.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a spectrogram. No specific source document, photograph, audio data or measurement is cited and no real spectrogram was compared; the harmonic count (12), vibrato depth and cycles, drift amount, energy-field resolution and threshold, burst count and weight, the deep blue and bright yellow tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices.

A dedicated sampler draws the harmonic lines as an integer number (12) of `exp(−sin²(π·12·(v − shift))/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile) with shift = `(0.2·sin(2π·6·u) + 0.18·(drift(u) − 0.5))/12` (vibrato plus a slow drift from an 8×2 periodic noise field); the bursts are an integer number (5) of vertical `exp(−sin²(π·5·u)/w²)`; the speckle is a 96×96 periodic noise field; all three are multiplied by a smooth gate from a 20×14 energy field, `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(5·(noise − 0.35))`, and joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)` so intensity stays in [0, 1]; the cache totals 16 + 280 + 9,216 + 16,384 = 25,896 Float64 values / 207,168 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bright lines (color>0.5) cover 6.31–6.76%, color is 0.0400–0.939 with a mean of 0.155–0.161 and height is at most 0.971–0.982 relief; the harmonic line position follows the vibrato (about +0.2 of a spacing at a positive vibrato peak and about −0.2 at a negative one, verified by the tests for each seed, with a tolerance including the drift's upper bound of 0.09); the bright-area masks (color>0.2) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on more than 5% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (50, 41, 67), r>128 covers 7.0% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.092. This material is an authored schematic of the general look of ECG chart paper. No specific source document, photograph, medical standard or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the grid (40×40 per tile, major every 5), the strip and beat counts (3 strips × 6 beats), the wave positions and heights, line width, pink paper and maroon ink tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real ECG paper or to be usable for medical purposes.

A dedicated sampler draws the minor and major grids as one integer-count family per direction of `exp(−sin²(π·n·s)/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile), joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; each strip's heartbeat is five compact bumps for the P, Q, R, S and T waves — `a·smooth(1 − ((x − c)/s)²)` is exactly zero for `|x − c| ≥ s` and C1, so each beat is exactly zero at its own ends and the per-beat amplitudes leave no step between beats (I first used Gaussians, whose tails are not exactly zero and left a jump of about 10⁻¹² at beat boundaries, which the C1 test magnified to about 0.038 and failed on); the trace is `exp(−d²/w²)` of width 0.0035 with `d = dy / √(1 + slope²)` the first-order distance to the curve so steep strokes keep a similar thickness, limited by two C1 windows to the vertical range the curve can reach and to its own strip; the grid and paper grain are combined and the ink is mixed in by a convex mix; the cache totals 18 + 16,384 = 16,402 Float64 values / 131,216 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, trace height is about 0.6 relief plus 0.4 relief of paper grain and roughness drops 0.1 on ink; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: ink (color<0.3) covers 3.23–3.27% (3.13% at seed 7), paper (color>0.85) covers 73.8–73.9%, color is 0.05–0.955 with a mean of 0.859–0.860, roughness is 0.60–0.70 and height is at most 0.983–0.992 relief; the baseline of every strip and the top of every R wave are ink (the test verifies each beat, 3 strips × 6 beats); the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on only 0.75% of pixels (only the per-beat amplitudes and the paper grain change with the seed); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (228, 206, 206), r<110 covers 2.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.061. I viewed the preview: three repeating heartbeat traces on pink grid paper that read as ECG paper overall, though the R waves are short and the T wave is flat-topped, unlike a real waveform. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`redalder` adds red alder, bringing the current catalog from 944 to 945 kinds (946 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Alnus rubra face: an even light yellowish-tan to slightly reddish ground, a fine uniform texture, two very faint darker bands, longitudinal fibre grain and very few (about 0.15%) fine dark short marks (standing in for the occasional aggregate rays). It is not a heartwood/sapwood distinction, the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots, wavy grain or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Red Alder](https://www.wood-database.com/red-alder/) (Color/Appearance: light tan to reddish brown, darkening and reddening with age, no visible heartwood/sapwood distinction, occasional small streaks from aggregate rays; Grain/Texture: generally straight with a moderately fine, uniform texture; Endgrain: diffuse-porous with small to medium, numerous pores) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/alnus-rubra.jpg) (an even light tan face, very faint lengthwise color change and scattered tiny dark short marks). These are color and grain-form references only: the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots and wavy grain are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or real dimensions are not derived from the photograph; the numerous small pores are too small to show here, and a few dark marks stand in for the occasionally visible rays.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany`, `shagbarkhickory`, `eastindianrosewood`, `bubinga`, `jarrah` and `merbau`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 36×12 vessel-site table (13,824 B), two undulating (bandWarp 0.8), very low-contrast (bandContrast 0.1) dark bands, a 220×9 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,104 Float64 values / 160,832 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the dark marks are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Because the shared sampler keeps the body color at about 0.25–0.46 of the palette, I chose a lighter warm-brown palette (dark (178, 124, 80) / light (246, 204, 150)) so the body color approaches the photograph's light tan. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: dark marks (AO<0.9) cover 0.12–0.15%, undented body covers 99.8%, body color is 0.254–0.459, the across/along color-difference ratio is 9.98–10.64, roughness 0.50–0.602, height 0.45–0.503 relief and minimum AO 0.75; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (204, 155, 107), AO<230 covers 0.147% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0008. I viewed the preview: an even light tan face with very faint bands and scattered fine dark marks, similar to the photograph in overall tone and evenness; the photograph is finer and more orange-yellow (my by-eye estimate is about (215, 170, 120), not a measurement). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sherpafleece` adds sherpa fleece, bringing the current catalog from 943 to 944 kinds (945 gallery choices including plain). A cream curly-pile fabric surface: many randomly rotated, edge-roughened cream lumps pile up into fluffy curled tufts, with occasional occluded light-brown creases between them (about 1%) and a tone and domed highlight per lump. It is not a real fleece's fibres, curl volume, woven backing or pile direction, and the preview reads more like bumpy cream crumbs or popcorn, only a loose approximation.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of sherpa fleece. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts, probabilities, sizes and aspect ratios of the two lump layers, the edge noise, the tones, roughness and the 0.15 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real fabric.

It reuses the existing two-layer rotated-ellipse piece sampler of `granola` by fallthrough (the constructor only selects the preset; no new sampler): large lumps (12×12 grid, probability 1, semi-axes 0.7–1.1 cell × a 0.55–1.45 aspect) and small lumps (24×24 grid, probability 0.7, semi-axes 0.45–0.85 cell) are each jittered ±0.5 in their cell with a random rotation, and each pixel composites the pieces of its 5×5 cells in a fixed order (the lumps of this preset can extend about 1.8 cells, which a 3×3 window would cut — the reason I later widened the shared sampler to 5×5) — `value = value·(1 − m) + piece·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.6))`, `q` multiplied by an edge perturbation from a 64×64 periodic noise field — large lumps first, small lumps over them, so every term is C1; the uncovered part has colour 0.3 and AO 0.4; the cache totals 1,008 + 4,032 + 4,096 + 16,384 = 25,520 Float64 values / 204,160 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.85 relief plus 0.15 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.15 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I tuned this preset twice: the first version (22×22 grid, smaller lumps) looked like coarse sand or crumbs, and the second, with larger lumps, read more like fluffy tufts and was adopted; the first version's tones also let colour reach 1.01 (outside [0, 1]), and lowering the large/small lump tones to 0.52/0.58 and the dome to 0.2 brought the maximum back to 0.93. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bright tufts (color>0.7) cover 38.8–41.3%, the crease ground (AO<0.45) covers 0.92–1.72%, color is 0.234–0.931 with a mean of 0.659–0.670, the crease ground averages 0.296, roughness is always 0.92, minimum AO is 0.4 and height is at most 0.996–0.998 relief; the bright-tuft masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 48.2% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (203, 191, 174), AO<200 covers 5.2% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.788. I viewed the preview: fluffy cream lumps piled up, but not like a real fleece's fibres. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`tilledsoil` adds tilled soil, bringing the current catalog from 942 to 943 kinds (944 gallery choices including plain). A dark brown soil surface: randomly rotated, edge-roughened clods (mid brown, overlapping, covering about three fifths) with darker, occluded fine soil in the gaps, and a few (about 7–9%) smaller pale pebbles or grit. It is not a real soil's roots, worm holes, moist sheen, plant litter or grain-size distribution, and the preview can also read as a camouflage pattern.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of tilled soil. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts, probabilities, sizes and aspect ratios of the clod and pebble layers, the edge noise, the layer tones, roughness and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real soil.

It reuses the existing two-layer rotated-ellipse piece sampler of `granola` by fallthrough (the constructor only selects the preset; no new sampler): clods (8×8 grid, probability 1, semi-axes 0.34–0.62 cell × a 0.7–1.3 aspect) and pale pebbles (16×16 grid, probability 0.3, semi-axes 0.1–0.22 cell) are each jittered ±0.45 in their cell with a random rotation, and each pixel composites the pieces of its 5×5 cells in a fixed order (the largest piece, at maximum stretch and edge perturbation, can reach more than one cell past its own, so a 3×3 window would cut it) — `value = value·(1 − m) + piece·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.4))`, `q` multiplied by an edge perturbation from a 48×48 periodic noise field — clods first, pebbles over them, so every term is C1; the part not covered by any piece has colour 0.14 and AO 0.45; the cache totals 448 + 1,792 + 2,304 + 16,384 = 20,928 Float64 values / 167,424 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.8 relief plus 0.2 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). While writing this preset I first set the pebble tone to 0.78 and the probe showed colour up to 1.03 (outside [0, 1]); lowering it to 0.66 ± 0.08 fixed that. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: the gap ground between clods (AO<0.46) covers 35.9–41.8% (42.0% at seed 7), pale pebbles (color>0.5) cover 6.8–9.4%, color is 0.094–0.899 with a mean of 0.270–0.288, the gap ground averages 0.140, roughness is always 0.92, minimum AO is 0.45 and height is at most 0.994–0.997 relief; the cover masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 43.7% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (62, 47, 35), AO<200 covers 50.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.894. I viewed the preview: lighter brown clods and small pebbles over a dark brown gap ground that read as loose soil, but quite like a camouflage pattern and far flatter than real soil. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`heatsinkfins` adds heat sink fins, bringing the current catalog from 941 to 942 kinds (943 gallery choices including plain). An anodised extruded-aluminium heat sink: 20 fins per tile running along v with flat bright tops and deep, occluded narrow gaps (about as wide as the tops), fine extrusion lines along v on the tops, a very faint anodising mottle and fine grain; the whole surface is metal (metallic 1). It is not a real heat sink's fin height and thickness, base plate, heat pipes, clips or machining burrs.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of an extruded aluminium heat sink. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the fin count (20 per tile), the fin-top to gap ratio and sharpness, the metal tones, extrusion-line and mottle strength, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real heat sink specification.

A dedicated sampler takes the fin weight `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(3.5·sin(2π·20·u))` (tanh of a sine is a smooth square wave, C-infinity; the integer fin count wraps with the tile), which blends colour between the gap tone 0.14 and the fin tone 0.7; the fin tops also carry a 4×160 extrusion-line noise elongated along v (applied only on the tops), a 4×4 anodising mottle and a 128² fine grain; in the gaps roughness rises by 0.2 and AO drops to 0.5; the cache totals 640 + 16 + 16,384 = 17,040 Float64 values / 136,320 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). `metallic` is 1 over the whole sampled range, and the kind is added to the `ProceduralMaterial` metal-factor list and to the tests' non-metal exception list. Color is the metal's reflectance colour, fin-top height is about 0.8 relief, extrusion lines 0.1 and grain 0.1; there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.01 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: fin tops (color>0.5) cover 47.1–47.3% and gaps (color<0.25) 43.4–43.7%, the region with AO<0.9 is always 56.25% (seed-independent), color is 0.099–0.777 with a mean of 0.416–0.421, roughness is 0.38–0.58, minimum AO is 0.50, metallic is always 1 and height is at most 0.988–0.992 relief; on a fin top the per-pixel colour difference along u (across fins) is about 4.9–5.3 times that along v (the extrusion lines); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (76, 79, 86), the metallic channel averages 255 and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.716. I viewed the four-panel preview: neat straight fins with deep gaps that read as an extruded-aluminium heat sink, but very simplified (no fin height, chamfers or base plate). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`jerky` adds beef jerky, bringing the current catalog from 940 to 941 kinds (942 gallery choices including plain). A dried-meat strip surface: a dark red-brown ground with dense fibres elongated along u, a broad low-frequency tone variation in the same direction, position-dependent sheen (roughness) and scattered near-black cracked-pepper flecks. It is not a real jerky's shrunken outline, fat specks, salt crystals or oiliness, and the preview can also be mistaken for brushed dark wood grain.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of beef jerky. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts of the fibre and tone noise, the pepper density and size, the red-brown tones, roughness and the 0.12 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real jerky.

A dedicated sampler combines a 14×240 fibre noise (elongated along u), a 4×8 broad low-frequency tone noise, a 6×36 sheen noise (roughness ± 0.1) and a 128² fine grain; cracked-pepper flecks are `smooth(1 − q)` discs on a 36×36 grid (about 14% chance, radius 0.22 cell, jitter 0.26, so radius plus jitter stays under half a cell and each stays inside its own cell) that darken the meat colour **multiplicatively** (`color = meat × (1 − 0.85·pepper)`); the cache totals 2,592 + 3,360 + 216 + 32 + 16,384 = 22,584 Float64 values (180,672 B) plus a 1,296 B Uint8 pepper-presence table = 181,968 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height combines 0.45 relief of fibres, 0.15 of pepper and 0.4 of grain; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.12 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: near-black pepper (color<0.14) covers 0.84–0.95%, color is 0.020–0.562 with a mean of 0.336–0.343, roughness is 0.40–0.60 and height is at most 0.970–0.979 relief; the per-pixel colour difference along v is about 7.3–7.5 times that along u (the fibres are elongated along u); the mean colour difference between seeds 0 and 1 along one horizontal line is about 0.127; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (73, 39, 24) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.297. I viewed the preview: dark red-brown horizontal fibres and tiny black dots that read as jerky but also as brushed dark wood grain, lacking a real jerky's shape and relief. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`garlicskin` adds garlic skin, bringing the current catalog from 939 to 940 kinds (941 gallery choices including plain). A garlic bulb's outer skin: on a cream-white papery ground, about 11 pale purple lengthwise streaks running along v, warped by low-frequency noise and varying in width with position (they cover 36–40% in the measurements), with lengthwise fibres, soft wrinkles and fine grain; the streaks are slightly recessed and smoother. It is not a real skin's peeled edges, tears, soil, clove outlines or translucency, and the preview looks more like wavy purple-striped paper than garlic skin.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of garlic skin. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the streak count (11 per tile), warp and width variation, purple threshold and strength, fibre and wrinkle strength, paper and purple tones, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real garlic variety.

A dedicated sampler takes phase = `11·u + 0.9·(warp(u, v) − 0.5)` (`warp` is a 4×6 periodic noise field) and the purple weight `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(2.5·(sin(2π·phase) − 0.35 − 1.1·(width(u, v) − 0.5)))` (tanh of a sine is a smooth square wave, C-infinity; `width` is a 5×12 periodic noise field that varies streak width and appearance smoothly; the integer streak count wraps with the tile); the paper also has a 220×10 lengthwise (along v) fibre noise, a 24×40 soft wrinkle noise and a 128² fine grain; the cache totals 24 + 60 + 2,200 + 960 + 16,384 = 19,628 Float64 values / 157,024 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, purple lowers colour by 0.4, the streak ridge height is about 0.35 relief, wrinkles 0.35, fibres 0.15 and grain 0.15, and roughness drops 0.1 on purple; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: the purple streak area (color<0.7) covers 36.0–40.3% and the paper (color>0.82) 51.0–54.9%, color is 0.467–0.978 with a mean of 0.756–0.774, roughness is 0.45–0.55 and height is at most 0.917–0.939 relief; on the paper the per-pixel colour difference along u is about 3.9–4.5 times that along v; the streak masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 39.4% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (213, 196, 201) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.038. I viewed the preview: pale purple wavy lengthwise stripes on cream-white paper, but too regular, like striped paper rather than real garlic skin; I softened the streak strength and coverage twice (the first version looked like zebra stripes) and it remains only a loose approximation. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`pancake` adds pancake, bringing the current catalog from 938 to 939 kinds (940 gallery choices including plain). A pancake surface: a golden ground with low-frequency, lace-edged irregular browned patches (their area varies a lot by seed, about 25–63%) and scattered tiny pore dimples; the surface is slightly rough. It is not a real pancake's edge, thickness, caramel gloss, butter or syrup, nor any specific pancake, crêpe or flatbread.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a pancake surface. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts and weights of the two noise fields, the browning threshold and sharpness, the pore density and size, the golden and brown tones, roughness and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real pancake.

A dedicated sampler takes the browning as `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(6·(0.5 − (0.65·broad + 0.35·fine)))` where `broad` is a 5×5 and `fine` a 22×22 periodic low-frequency noise field (the tanh makes patch edges smooth, C-infinity, and the fine noise makes them lacy); pores are `smooth(1 − q)` dimples on a 30×30 grid (about 55% chance, radius 0.14–0.28 cell, centre jittered ±0.2, so radius plus jitter stays under half a cell and each stays inside its own cell); a 128² fine grain is added; the cache totals 25 + 484 + 16,384 + 3×900 = 19,593 Float64 values / 156,744 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height combines 0.4 relief of pore dents, 0.15 of browning and 0.45 of grain, and in the pores roughness rises by 0.08 and AO drops to 0.7; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: browned areas (color<0.45) cover 24.7–63.4% and golden areas (color>0.6) 18.3–44.3% (they depend on the low-frequency noise, so seeds differ a lot), pores (AO<0.9) cover 4.84–5.15%, color is 0.073–0.716 with a mean of 0.428–0.544, roughness is 0.62–0.70, minimum AO is 0.7 and height is at most 0.983–0.990 relief; the browned masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 41.2% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (161, 122, 73), AO<230 covers 4.87% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.325. I viewed the preview: lace-edged browned patches and small pores on a golden ground that read as a pancake or crêpe, but patch edges show a visible blocky noise look (from the 22×22 fine field) and there is no real pancake's gloss or thickness. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`kawung` adds kawung batik, bringing the current catalog from 937 to 938 kinds (939 gallery choices including plain). A cream wax-resist geometric pattern on dark indigo cotton: 4×4 cells with one ellipse per cell, the long axis along u in even cells and along v in odd ones (a checkerboard), each ellipse long enough to poke into its neighbours and cross their ellipses, giving the overlapping four-petal feel of the Indonesian kawung motif, with a small dot at each ellipse centre. It is not the exact geometry and proportions of a real kawung (this is a simplified schematic), the thickness variation of hand-drawn wax lines, wax cracks or dye bleed.

This material is an authored, simplified schematic of the general look of kawung batik. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph or pattern book was compared; the cell count (4×4 per tile), ellipse semi-axes (0.72 / 0.30 cell), line width, dot size, indigo and wax tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real kawung specification.

A dedicated sampler composites the ellipses of each pixel's 3×3 cells — one ellipse per cell, its long axis along u when `col + row` is even and along v when odd (the cell count is even, so the checkerboard wraps with the tile); a ring is `smooth(clamp(1 − ((q − 1)/0.14)²))` (`q` is the ellipse form; compact and C1), the centre dot is `smooth(1 − q)`, and all join as the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; the indigo ground also has a 5×5 periodic dye-noise field and 192² per-thread noise; the cache totals 25 + 36,864 = 36,889 Float64 values / 295,112 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, the wax lines are slightly raised (height 0.5 relief, thread 0.5) and roughness drops 0.06 on wax; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: wax (color>0.5) covers 12.75–12.78%, color is 0.072–0.907 with a mean of 0.2125–0.2146, the indigo ground (color<0.25) averages 0.121–0.123, roughness is 0.76–0.82 and height is at most 0.994–0.999 relief; the cell corners between four ellipses (no wax) reach at most about 0.140–0.164; the mean corner colour difference between seeds 0 and 1 is about 0.024; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (60, 64, 84), r>110 covers 13.5% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.450. I viewed the preview: alternating ellipses and dots arranged in a pattern similar to kawung, but with simpler geometry than real batik and overly even, mechanical lines; the first version, with four petal ellipses along the grid lines, looked like a chain grid rather than kawung and was adopted only after switching to the checkerboard of ellipses. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`granola` adds granola, bringing the current catalog from 936 to 937 kinds (938 gallery choices including plain). Two layers of randomly rotated elliptical pieces lie over a honey-brown ground: larger pale-cream oat flakes (about 0.4 of the area) and smaller dark nut and dried-fruit chunks, with noise-roughened edges, overlapping neighbours, a tone and domed shading per piece, and the bare ground between them darkened by occlusion. This material is an authored schematic of the general look of granola. A dedicated sampler keeps two piece layers (oat flakes on a 9×9 grid, nut and fruit chunks on a 14×14 grid), each piece jittered ±0.45 in its cell with a random rotation and a 0.65–1.35 aspect ratio; because pieces can spill into neighbouring cells, each pixel composites the pieces of its 5×5 cells in a fixed order (the largest piece, at maximum stretch and edge perturbation, can reach more than one cell past its own, so a 3×3 window would cut it) — `value = value·(1 − m) + piece·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.4))`, where `q` is the squared distance of a rotated ellipse times an edge perturbation `1 + 0.45·(noise − 0.5)·2` (a 40×40 periodic noise field) — flakes first and dark chunks over them, so every term is C1; the bare ground (not covered by any piece) has colour 0.3 and AO 0.6; the cache totals 567 + 1,372 + 1,600 + 16,384 = 19,923 Float64 values / 159,384 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.7 relief plus 0.3 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.2 m nominal tile and 0.008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bare ground (AO<0.61) covers 37.0–39.7% (41.1% at seed 7), pale pieces (color>0.5) cover 39.2–40.7%, dark pieces (color<0.2) cover 0.49–0.58%, color is 0.142–0.957 with a mean of 0.461–0.477, the bare ground averages 0.300, roughness is always 0.78, minimum AO is 0.6 and height is at most 0.993–0.996 relief; the cover masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 48.0% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (141, 116, 78), AO<200 covers 47.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.722. I viewed the preview: irregular cream pieces and small dark pieces on a brown ground that read as granola but also as camouflage, and far flatter than real dry granola; the first version (true ellipses with smooth edges) looked like beans or pills and was adopted only after adding edge noise. `raspberry` adds raspberry, bringing the current catalog from 935 to 936 kinds (937 gallery choices including plain). A raspberry surface: 16×18 round drupelets on a staggered lattice (odd rows shifted half a column), slightly overlapping, each with its own red tone, domed shading and an upper-left highlight, separated by darker, occluded thin creases. It is not a real raspberry's overall shape, fine hairs, calyx, hollow core or variation in drupelet size and shape.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a raspberry surface. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the lattice size (16×18), drupelet radius, crease tone and occlusion, tone variation, highlight position and size, roughness and the 0.08 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real variety or size.

A dedicated sampler places drupelet centres on a staggered lattice (odd rows shifted right by half a column; the even row count keeps the shift periodic with the tile); because drupelets overlap, each pixel composites the drupelets of its 3×3 cells in a fixed order — `value = value·(1 − m) + drupelet·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.35))` (`q` is the squared distance to a disc of radius 0.56 cell, row spacing converted to the same physical length via the column width) — so every term is C1; the drupelet tone is a 0.38 base plus a per-drupelet variation (±0.1), plus a `smooth(1 − q)` dome × 0.3 and an upper-left highlight × 0.18; in the creases roughness rises by 0.2 and AO drops to 0.55; the per-drupelet tone table is 18×16 = 288 Float64 values plus a 128² paper grain (16,384 Float64 values) = 16,672 values / 133,376 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.7 relief plus 0.3 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.08 m nominal tile and 0.006 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color is 0.035–0.956 with a mean of 0.517–0.529, drupelet-centre color is 0.567–0.792 (mean 0.672–0.685), the midpoints of the gaps between neighbours average 0.352–0.364, roughness is 0.42–0.62, minimum AO 0.55, creases (AO<0.9) cover 15.04% (seed-independent because the layout is a fixed lattice) and height is at most 0.993–0.998 relief; the mean drupelet-centre color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is about 0.068; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (154, 40, 54), AO<230 covers 15.0% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.256. I viewed the preview: neatly staggered round red drupelets with dark creases that read as a raspberry surface, but far more regular than a real one (every drupelet has the same size and shape, with no hairs); the first version, with too much overlap, looked like flat hexagonal paving, and it was adopted only after adjusting the radius, creases and highlight. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

A dedicated sampler places fat flecks on an 11×11 grid (about 55% of cells hold an ellipse with semi-axes of 0.2–0.45 cell times a 0.7–1.3 aspect, its centre jittered by ±0.45 in the cell); since they can spill into neighbouring cells, each pixel joins the flecks of its 3×3 cells with the union `1 − Π(1 − smooth(1 − q))`; peppercorns are `smooth(1 − q)` discs on a 40×40 grid (about 14% chance, radius 0.22 cell, jitter 0.26) whose radius plus jitter stays under half a cell, so they stay inside their own cell; fat first blends the meat colour toward cream, then pepper blends toward near-black by a convex mix, all C1; the ground also has 6×6 low-frequency mottling and a 128² fine grain; the cache totals 20,104 Float64 values (160,832 B) plus a 1,600 B Uint8 pepper-presence table = 162,432 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, fat height is about 0.5 relief, fibres 0.3 and grain 0.2, and roughness drops 0.14 on fat; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: fat (color>0.6) covers 38.4–39.7% and lean (color<0.4) 54.0–55.4%, color is 0.138–0.912 with a mean of 0.471–0.485, the fat mean is 0.829–0.839 and the lean mean 0.221–0.224, roughness is 0.410–0.550 and height is at most 0.693–0.697 relief; on the lean the per-pixel color difference along v is about 2.5–2.7 times that along u (3.6 times at seed 7); the fat masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 48.3% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (188, 124, 109) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.058. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the light network is built from three bent line families of my own design and only visually approximates a light net, it is not a physical caustics model. Family directions, widths, gain, tones, roughness and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real pool or optical specification.

A dedicated sampler uses three integer-wavenumber line families `(6,0)`, `(3,5)` and `(−3,5)`, each phase further bent by three integer-wavenumber sinusoids (with seed phases); each family contributes `exp(−sin²(π·phase)/w²)` (C∞), and the sum saturates through `S/(1+S)` into color and roughness; where bending squeezes lines together their glows add into brighter, thinner branches. The cache is a 96² pool-floor grain (9,216 Float64 values) plus 3 phases and 3 offsets, 9,222 Float64 values / 73,776 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Iteration: the first version (warpAmplitude 0.9, lineWidth 0.2, gain 0.9) rendered tangled thin loops that did not look like caustics; the second widened the lines (0.55) and lowered bending and gain, giving a soft light net with low contrast; the final version uses lineWidth 0.42, gain 0.9 and baseTone 0.16 for more contrast, and I viewed it to confirm a bright branching network with dark meshes. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color>0.55 covers 33.3–36.9%, color<0.3 covers 22.3–24.3%, color is 0.144–0.793 with a mean of 0.449–0.461, roughness is 0.554–0.698 and AO is 1; the bright masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 43.9% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (99, 138, 165) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.066. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`metalflakepaint` adds metal-flake paint, bringing the current catalog from 912 to 913 kinds (914 gallery choices including plain). Round metal flakes of random position, tilt and brightness (a 64×64 grid with about half the cells holding a flake) are scattered over a deep blue clear-coated base, covering about 21–22% of the area; the flakes are pale lavender-silver and form a partial metal mask in the metallic channel (at most about 0.68, not full metal), their small tilts make the normals sparkle and the clear base is non-metal. It is not pearlescent / color-shift (multi-hue) paint, polygonal flake shapes, independent reflection directions per flake or clear-coat thickness.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of metal-flake car paint. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; flake size, density, tones, metallic coverage, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real paint or color code.

A dedicated sampler stores five Float64 values per cell (jittered offset x, y, tilt x, y and tone; a missing flake has tone 0), 20,480 Float64 values for the 64² cells, plus a 128² clear-coat grain of 16,384 Float64 values, for 36,864 Float64 values / 294,912 B of lattice arithmetic in total (not total RAM). Flakes are summed rather than owned: each is a `smooth(1 − q/r²)` dome (radius 0.55 cell, zero value and slope at the rim) over the 3×3 neighbour cells (a flake reaches at most 0.9 cell from its cell centre, which the neighbourhood covers); height is the sum of each dome times `1 + 2·tilt·(tiltX·dx + tiltY·dy)`, so overlaps stay C1. The coverage `S/(1+S)` (S being the weighted sum times flakeGain 1.2) saturates smoothly into color, metallic, roughness and AO without hard clipping. This is why the kind is added to the metallic list in `procedural-material.ts` (metallic factor 1, controlled by the per-sample metallic channel) and to the generic 'non-metal' exception list in the tests. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. My first render used 48 cells, radius 0.78 and presence 0.85, and after viewing it the face was almost entirely silver with no blue base visible, so I changed to 64 cells, radius 0.55, presence 0.5 and flakeGain 1.2. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: metallic>0.3 covers 21.5–22.3%, metallic peaks at 0.671–0.683, bottoms at 0 and averages 0.117–0.121, color is 0.165–0.748, height runs from 0.25 to 1.31–1.38 relief, roughness is 0.052–0.12, minimum AO is 0.932 and the color–metallic correlation is about 0.999; the flake masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 33.3% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/b is about (73, 113), the mean metallic channel is 30.3/255 with 21.9% above 76 and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.351. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`tapemeasure` adds a tape measure, bringing the current catalog from 911 to 912 kinds (913 gallery choices including plain). One tile is a 100 mm segment of yellow tape: 100 millimetre ticks (0.2 of the tile height long), a longer tick every 5 mm (0.3) and the longest, thicker tick every 10 mm (0.42), all near-black and hanging from 0.08 below the band edge; the cross-section is a cosine bow with raised rims and a concave centre, so the glossy coat has a lengthwise normal gradient. It has no numerals, imperial scale, end hook, case or wear.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a metric tape measure. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; tick lengths and widths, the yellow, the bow depth, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile (exactly one 100 mm segment) are authored choices and do not claim to match any real tape standard or accuracy class.

A dedicated sampler finds the nearest tick with `k = round(u·100)` and picks the length by the k 1/5/10 mm hierarchy; ink = `smooth(1 − d²/w²)` times 0.004 top and bottom ramps, zero beyond the tick width, so the nearest-tick ownership change at half a millimetre never jumps; the bow height is `0.1 + 0.55·(0.5+0.5cos 2πv)`, with zero slope at both rims, so it is C1 across tiles, and the rims carry AO (at most 0.25). The cache is only a 64² paper/coat grain (4,096 Float64 values / 32,768 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Color is pigment, ink height is 0.04 relief; metallic is 0 (a painted tape) and there is no mortar. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.03 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices; I first used 0.01, then saw the normals were too flat and raised it to 0.03. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: at v = tickTop + 0.1 all 100 ticks are dark (color 0.016–0.043) and color between ticks is at least 0.886; at lengths 0.25 / 0.35 there are 20 / 10 dark ticks and 0 beyond the longest; overall color is 0.016–0.915, height 0.100–0.653 relief, AO 0.75–1 and roughness 0.375–0.544; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean r/g/b is about (217, 185, 35), yellow pixels (r>180, g>150, b<70) cover 94.3%, r<100 covers 4.3% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.111. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`ledmatrix` adds an LED dot-matrix panel, bringing the current catalog from 910 to 911 kinds (912 gallery choices including plain). A 48×48 grid of round LEDs split into 8×6 character cells (5×7 LEDs plus one blank column and row each); each cell lights 2–4 random short horizontal, vertical or diagonal strokes by seed (pseudo-glyphs, not a font); lit LEDs are bright red-orange, unlit ones dark red, the LED lenses are smooth and slightly domed and the black plate is rougher with AO. It is not a real font or readable text, scrolling animation, emission, color mixing or RGB sub-pixels.

This material is an authored schematic of the general structure of an LED dot-matrix display panel. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the LED count, character-cell size, stroke generation rule, tones, roughness, AO and the 0.16 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real product.

A dedicated sampler draws strokes per character cell from `hash` by seed at construction into a 2,304-entry Uint8 lit table, plus 2,304 Float64 brightness jitters (2,304 B + 18,432 B = 20,736 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). At sample time each LED owns its square cell; the lens is `smooth(1 − q/r²)` with r = 0.46 < 0.5, zero (value and slope) at the cell boundary, so lit/unlit tone changes never jump at a seam, and the black plate shows between lenses. Color is pigment (there is no emission), lit LEDs add a 0.1 lens highlight tone; height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.16 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. I first set litTone to 0.88; probing showed lit LED color reaching 1.0199 (outside [0,1]), so I lowered it to 0.84, after which lit LED color is 0.900–0.980. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: lit fraction 12.9–14.1%, lit LED color 0.900–0.980, unlit LED 0.150–0.170, lens height 1.0 relief / plate 0, lens roughness 0.17 / plate 0.62, plate AO 0.55 / lens 1, plate color 0.02; the lit masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 21.5% of LEDs; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 48.0, r>160 covers 3.07%, AO<200 covers 67.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.413. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`barcodelabel` adds a barcode label, bringing the current catalog from 909 to 910 kinds (911 gallery choices including plain). One tile is a full label width: 10-module quiet zones on both sides, a Code 128 Start B pattern (11 modules), nine data symbols (each six alternating bar/space widths of 1–4 modules summing to 11) and a 13-module stop pattern, 143 modules in total; the bars occupy only the v 0.1–0.9 label band with blank paper above and below. Near-black toner (slightly raised and smoother) is printed on bright rough paper with a fine paper-fibre grain. It is not a decodable Code 128: the data symbols are seed-chosen random widths with no check symbol and without the parity rule (bar widths summing to even, space widths to odd), and there is no human-readable text, other label elements or curvature.

The structure follows the actually read [Wikipedia “Code 128”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_128): each symbol is three black bars and three white spaces of 1–4 modules each summing to 11 modules and starting with a bar and ending with a space; the stop pattern is 13 modules including a final 2-module bar; the quiet zone is at least 10 modules on each side. The Start B bit pattern `11010010000` and the stop pattern `1100011101011` that I use come from my recollection of the standard's symbol table; the text extracted from that page did not include the tables, so those two bit strings are **not verified by the page**. The appearance (black bars on white paper, 0.14 m tile, toner height, roughness, paper color) is authored, with no specific label photograph or measurement cited.

A dedicated sampler, at construction, draws nine symbols from `hash` by seed (five widths of 1–4 each, the sixth derived from the sum of 11 and required to fall in 1–4, retried up to 4,096 times and falling back to the Start B widths on failure) into a 143-module bit array; at sample time x = fract(u)·143 finds the module and each bar edge blends over ±`edgeRamp/2` = 0.11 module with `smooth` (zero slope at both ends, hence C1), and the label band edges use a 0.012 `smooth` ramp. The cache is a 96² paper-fibre grain (9,216 Float64 values / 73,728 B) plus a 143-entry module-bit array. Color is pigment; toner has height 0.35 relief and paper grain at most 0.1; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.14 m nominal tile and 0.0006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color<0.5 covers 30.1–34.8%, the lowest color is 0.0276, the highest 0.982, mean toner height is about 0.39 relief versus about 0.055 for paper and roughness spans 0.445–0.575; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 173.3, r<128 covers 31.1% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0036. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`topographicmap` adds topographic contour paper, bringing the current catalog from 908 to 909 kinds (910 gallery choices including plain). On warm off-white paper, constant-width brown contour lines are printed over a terrain made of seven integer-wavenumber sinusoids (16 contour levels, every fifth an index contour that is heavier and darker), with a very faint elevation tint and fine paper-fibre grain; the ink sits slightly above the paper. It is not real terrain data, elevation labels, rivers, roads, a grid or legend text.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a contour map. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; level count, index interval, line width, ink and paper colors and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real map specification or scale.

A dedicated sampler sums seven integer-wavenumber sinusoids (seed-chosen phases, ±20% amplitude jitter) into a periodic analytic (C∞) terrain; the contour distance `sin²(πd)/π² ÷ (levels·|∇|)²` converts level distance to squared UV distance (|∇| has a 0.4 floor so summits and saddles stay smooth), so line width does not widen on flat ground; line = `smooth(1 − distance²/width²)` and the index weight is `((1+cos(2πd/5))/2)^6`, so width and ink are C∞. The cache is a 128² paper-fibre grain plus 7 phases and 7 amplitudes, 16,398 Float64 values / 131,184 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment; ink has height 0.6 relief and paper grain at most 0.15; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color<0.7 (including edge falloff) covers 9.3–10.5%, color<0.45 covers 6.7–7.6%, the lowest color is 0.14 (index ink), the highest 0.925–0.930, the mean 0.839–0.846 and mean ink height is about 0.575 relief versus about 0.077 for paper; the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 17.6% of pixels; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (222, 206, 180), b<170 covers 10.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.111. I viewed the first render and confirmed the line width looks consistent on both flat and steep ground before settling. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`eastindianrosewood` adds East Indian rosewood, bringing the current catalog from 907 to 908 kinds (909 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Dalbergia latifolia face: a deep purplish-brown ground, five darker near-black undulating streaks, fine longitudinal fibre grain and scattered short open-vessel pits (about 1.2%). It is not a golden-brown pale face, white sapwood, a polished surface, interlocked/wavy figure or oily luster.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database East Indian Rosewood](https://www.wood-database.com/east-indian-rosewood/) (Color/Appearance: heartwood from golden brown to deep purplish brown with darker blackish streaks, darkening with age to a deep brown) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/dalbergia-latifolia-1-300x600.jpg) (a deep brown, purple-tinged longitudinal face with darker streaks and fine pores). These are color and grain-form references only: the golden-brown variation, pale sapwood and real vessel distribution are not reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany` and `shagbarkhickory`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 40×14 vessel-site table (17,920 B), five strongly undulating (bandWarp 0.8), high-contrast (bandContrast 0.45) dark bands, a 220×9 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,616 Float64 values / 164,928 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the vessel pits are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.0025 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid, vessels cover 1.18–1.22%, body color spans 0.255–0.908, the across/along color-difference ratio is 8.6–10.2, roughness is 0.460–0.564 and height is 0.42–0.503 relief; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (97, 61, 49), vessels cover 1.18% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0052. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`lenticularsheet` adds a lenticular print sheet, bringing the current catalog from 906 to 907 kinds (908 gallery choices including plain). 32 parallel cylindrical lenses per tile (long strips along v), glossy smooth bright crests and low rougher seams with AO (0.65) between lenses; the blue-silver base is a diagonal 'flip' stripe (2 cycles per lens, 3 cycles along v) combined with an 8×8 low-frequency printed image. It is not a real interlaced multi-frame image, view-dependent animation, lens refraction or a readable picture.

This material is an authored schematic of the general structure of a lenticular print sheet. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; lens count, tones, flip stripe, roughness, AO and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real product or optical specification.

A dedicated sampler uses f = fract(u·32) per lens; lens height = 0.5 − 0.5·cos(2πf) (zero slope at crest and seam, so it is C1 across lenses); the flip stripe is sin(2π(2f + 3v)) (integer cycles so it wraps with the tile), plus an 8×8 cachedNoise low-frequency image (64 Float64 values / 512 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.008 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: crest height 1.0 relief, seam 0.1, crest roughness 0.1, seam 0.4, crest AO 1, seam 0.65; color spans about 0.094–0.902; the across/along color-difference ratio is about 21.0–21.1; the flip along a lens crest sweeps from 0.25–0.30 up to 0.87–0.90; the mean image color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is 0.070; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean blue channel is 179.1, AO<230 covers 37.5% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.323. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`europeanlarch` adds European larch, bringing the current catalog from 905 to 906 kinds (907 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished flatsawn Larix decidua face: a pale pink-brown / pale yellow-tan earlywood ground, 12 flowing reddish-brown latewood ring lines (moderately wide, about a quarter of the area, curving and undulating with arches) and fine longitudinal fibre grain. It is not resin pockets, knots, the narrow near-white sapwood/heartwood boundary, spiral grain or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database European Larch](https://www.wood-database.com/european-larch/) (Color/Appearance: heartwood from yellow to medium reddish brown, narrow nearly white sapwood clearly demarcated from heartwood, flatsawn sections showing interesting growth-ring patterns; Grain/Texture: generally straight or spiraled, medium to fine texture with a greasy feel) and the actually downloaded and viewed [flatsawn photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/european-larch-s-400x400.jpg) (pale pink-tan face with flowing reddish-brown ring lines and arches). These are color and grain-form references only: the sapwood/heartwood boundary, knots and greasy luster are not reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph. During development I first set warp to 1.4, which rendered closed swirling loops unlike the photograph; after viewing it I lowered it to 0.55 with 12 rings and arch 2.2, which is still more regular than the photograph but closer to its flowing arches.

It reuses the `douglasfir` ring-index sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `longleafpine`, `westernredcedar` and `sitkaspruce`); only the constructor selects the preset (rings 12, arch 2.2, warp 0.55, latewood 0.45–0.9, lateTone 0.52, earlyTone 0.86); a 36-value warp table plus a 180×6 fibre field and 128² fine grain total 17,500 Float64 values / 140,000 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0, latewood is slightly higher and ring color is pigment. The default 0.2 m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid, latewood-colored points (color<0.6) cover 25.7–26.5%, earlywood-colored points (>0.75) 62.6–63.6%, the color range is 0.316–0.907, roughness 0.531–0.610, height 0.498–0.662 relief and the across/along color-difference ratio 2.84–2.88; in the seed-7 512² maps g≥165 covers 69.9%, g<165 covers 30.1%, the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.028 and the mean base color is about (220, 176, 142).
