`deltoidaltrihexagonaltiles` adds an authored deltoidal trihexagonal (V3.4.6.4) tiling: the hexagon of points nearest to each point of a triangular lattice is cut into six kites by six spokes to its side midpoints, and the kites around a point take burgundy, rose and ivory glaze in turn, so the three kites of every lattice triangle also differ; the kites sit in bevelled glaze over rougher gray grout, and every straight edge lies on one of six parallel line families 30° apart. It is not `kisrhombilletiles` (30-60-90 triangles, V4.6.12), `trihexagonaltiles` (hexagons and triangles, 3.6.3.6), `rhombille` (three lozenges per hexagon), its dual `rhombitrihexagonaltiles` (3.4.6.4) or the other existing tile presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for 3.4.6.4 duals, deltoidal, tetrakis/triakis/floret and prismatic pentagonal found only the `kisrhombilletiles` entry that lists this tiling among related tilings; no preset implemented it. The actually read deltoidal section of the Wikipedia Rhombitrihexagonal tiling page (the redirect target of Deltoidal trihexagonal tiling) supplies: the faces are kites, the type is a dual semiregular (face-transitive) tiling, the face configuration is V3.4.6.4, the symmetry group is p6m [6,3] (*632) with rotation group p6, the dual is the rhombitrihexagonal tiling, Conway called it the tetrille, it relates to the trihexagonal tiling by dividing the triangles and hexagons into central triangles and merging neighboring triangles into kites, and face-transitive variations can distort the kites (p31m). The fetched text gives no coordinates, angles or edge lengths, so the construction on a triangular lattice of pitch 1 (hexagon apothem 0.5 cut by spokes through the side midpoints, so lattice points have degree 6, side midpoints degree 4 and lattice-triangle centers degree 3), the kite angles 60°, 90°, 120° and 90° (360° divided by those vertex degrees) with long and short sides in the ratio √3, and every other number are authored: the tones 0.1, 0.48 and 0.82 plus up to 0.12 per kite, the 102,34,44 / 238,228,204 palette, glaze roughness 0.3 against grout 0.92, relief 0.012, grout half-width 0.014 and bevel shoulder 0.01 in lattice units, and a 7 × 8 lattice (7 columns and 4 row pairs, 1% off square) per UV tile of 0.84 m (an authored lattice pitch of 0.12 m). No real tile dimensions, glaze or installation specification is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. The independent kernel stores 336 per-kite tones, 14 spoke components and a 96² grain, 76,528 B of tables, not total RAM; each point looks at nine lattice candidates and the six kites of the nearest one, so no square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar is the grout. Seeds change only the per-kite tone and grain while the geometry stays fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: a 768 × 768 raster at the half-height contour is labelled into connected kite faces and each face's corners are read from its radial extent peaks. Every seed has 336 faces (6 kites for each of the 7 × 8 = 56 lattice points), each with 4 corners and an area within 1.07% of the predicted inset kite (allowed 5%; the inset is the grout plus half the shoulder, and the kite is tangential so it shrinks to a similar kite), and a grout fraction within 0.00079 of the prediction (allowed 0.012). The interior angles of all 336 kites are within 3.57° of 60°, 90°, 90° and 120° (allowed 6°), the edge directions within 3.58° of multiples of 30° (allowed 6°) and the long-to-short side ratio within 4.16% of √3 (allowed 10%). Around each of the 56 lattice points exactly six kite centroids lie within 0.5 pitch, equally distant within 2.15% (allowed 4%), spaced 60° within 1.29° (allowed 4°) on the axes 30° off the spokes within 1.25° (allowed 4°), with consecutive kites in different tone classes and kites opposite each other in the same class. The three tone classes hold 112 kites each, with class means 0.343 and 0.375 apart (above 0.25), grout rougher than glaze by 0.5753 (above 0.4), glaze brighter in occlusion by 0.4564 (above 0.3) and no metallic pixels; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff keep every kite at the same place (centroid gap below 0.5 px) and move kite tone by up to 0.1147/0.1159 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, the lattice column and row lines, sweeps along all six 30°-apart line families through every lattice point at offsets of 0, 0.25 and 0.5 pitch, and curvature refinement: worst 0.0016687 (below 0.04) and signed-UV period error at most 3.6e-14 (below 5e-10). The 512 map has grout fraction 0.18589, grout minus glaze roughness 0.57038, luma range 152.28, AO 128-250, maximum tilt² 0.87957 (0.1-3) and all four signed normal directions at 0.1108-0.1214 (above 0.02); the 32 map has grout fraction 0.21875, roughness gap 0.59999, luma range 150.7 and tilt² 0.029558 (below 0.5). A regression control accepted 15 legal variants (12 preset variants: cobalt and forest glaze palettes, glaze roughness 0.2 and 0.4, relief 0.008 and 0.016, grout 0.01 and 0.02, bevel shoulder 0.006 and 0.014, and 5 × 3 and 9 × 5 lattices; plus three source variants: quintic bevel ramps, milder per-kite tone variation and shifted tone levels) and rejected 13 genuine faults (4 preset faults: no grout, grout of 0.12, glaze as rough as the grout, unresolved relief; 9 source faults: two tones only, an oversized hexagon apothem of 0.56, spokes rotated 30 degrees, no grout along the spokes, linear bevel creases, metallic glaze, seed ignored by the tone, seed shifting the lattice, a square lattice without the row offset). Two faults were rejected only marginally and are recorded as such: the oversized apothem of 0.56 by an area deviation of 5.33% against the 5% bound, and the missing grout along the spokes by 5.97% against 5%; the other faults failed by large margins (for example 8 faces instead of 336 without grout and 596.9 against 0.04 for the creased bevel). Compatibility: all 843 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,604 samples, 141,624 channel comparisons) and ten related kinds (`kisrhombilletiles`, `rhombitrihexagonaltiles`, `trihexagonaltiles`, `truncatedtrihexagonaltiles`, `snubsquaretiles`, `elongatedtriangulartiles`, `rhombille`, `hexagontiles`, `cairotiles`, `soroban`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (60 map sets, 300 buffers) are identical to the previous build; presets and tile sizes of the old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first version alternated only two tones around each lattice point, which made the three kites of every lattice triangle one color and hid the kites (seen in the prototype before any test), so it now takes three tones in turn; and the first fixture used not.toBe, which the nested control harness does not support (the first control run stopped at its first legal variant), so the comparison was rewritten and the whole control run repeated.

`soroban` adds an authored soroban tile: a seven-rod section of a Japanese abacus, biconical wooden beads on seven bamboo-like rods between a frame bar above and below and a reckoning bar, the beads showing 4567890 and the reckoning bar carrying a dot on every third rod. It is not `seedbeads` (loose seed beads) or any other existing preset, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for abacus, soroban, suanpan/reckoning and bicone/biconical found no abacus preset. The actually read Wikipedia Soroban page supplies the structure: an odd number of rods and never fewer than seven (standard models have thirteen), one five-bead (go-dama) above and four one-beads (ichi-dama) below a reckoning bar on each rod, a bi-quinary coded decimal where beads moved towards the reckoning bar are on (the five-bead moves down, the one-beads move up), the unit-rod dot on every third rod, usually biconal (double-cone) beads of wood and rods of wood, metal, rattan or bamboo, and the caption of its modern soroban whose right side shows 1234567890 with lower beads as ones and upper beads as fives. The page gives no dimensions, bead proportions, colors or frame layout, so the seven-rod section showing the last seven digits 4567890 of that caption, the dots on the first, fourth and seventh rod counted from the right, the frame bars 0.52 and the reckoning bar 0.5 thick in units of the rod pitch, the bead slot of 0.78 with beads 0.9 wide and 0.78 tall (a double-cone silhouette with a rounded equator ridge, height 0.7 rising to 1.0 relief units at the centre), the rods 0.1 wide, the dots of radius 0.11, the 48,28,18 / 228,198,142 palette, tones (board 0.6 + 0.08 × grain, beads 0.3-0.4, frame 0.1, reckoning bar 0.16, rods 0.88, dots 0.95), roughness 0.8 on the board and 0.45 on the beads, relief 0.03 and bead edge softness 0.08 are authored approximations; no real soroban dimensions, materials or teaching correctness is claimed, the frame sides are not drawn so the tile repeats as a longer abacus section, and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.056 m (seven rods at an authored 8 mm pitch). The independent kernel stores the seven digits and a 128² wood grain, about 131,128 B of tables (7 Float64 values and 16,384 Float64 grain values), not total RAM; each point handles the one rod it lies on and the one bead slot it lies in with at most seven smooth ramps, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the wood grain while the beads stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: the test rebuilds the bi-quinary rod rules from the page (for every digit 0-9 exactly one of the two upper slots and four of the five lower slots hold a bead, and reading them back gives the digit; the shown digits equal the last seven of 1234567890; 35 beads on seven rods), reads the sampler at the centre of all 7 slots of each rod and decodes them the way a user does (the five-bead at the bar means 5, the empty lower slot index counts the one-beads at the bar), and reads the reckoning bar at every rod for the dot. Every seed decodes 4567890 and the dot string 1001001 (rods 1, 4 and 7 from the right). A 1008 × 1008 pixel-centre raster labelled into connected raised-bead components at a height of 0.6 relief units gives 35 beads, 0 of them more than 0.02 rod pitch from the expected slot centre and 0 whose bounding box is more than 0.09 off the nominal 0.9 × 0.78 (the mask contour sits near 94% of the silhouette), the width halfway to the tips is 0.5 of the equator width within 0.041 (allowed 0.12, a double cone halves the width), the mean area is within 0.08% of the diamond area (allowed 15%), the equator ridge stands 0.1397 relief units above the shoulders (above 0.1) with 0 asymmetry, and a column between two rods crosses the bar threshold exactly four times at 0.52, 2.08, 2.58 and 6.48 within 0.033 (allowed 0.05). Stacking at probes: bead minus frame height 0.55, frame minus rod 0.25 and rod minus board 0.2 relief units, dot minus reckoning bar tone 0.79, rod minus board tone 0.235-0.244, board minus bead tone 0.236-0.245, board minus bead roughness 0.35, metallic violations 0. Seeds 7 and 0xffffffff flip 0 of 1,016,064 bead-mask pixels, decode the same digits and move the wood tone up to 0.0794/0.0781 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, sweeps horizontally, vertically and on both diagonals through each of the 49 bead slots (silhouette edges, equator ridge and the tips where beads meet) and across the bar, rod and dot edges, and curvature refinement: worst 0.0000534 for all seeds (below 0.04), signed-UV period error at most 8.1e-16 (below 5e-10). The 512 map has polished-pixel fraction 0.283825, board minus bead roughness 0.3085, luma range 143.9, AO 217-247, maximum tilt² 0.98747 (0.1-3) and all four signed normal directions at 0.1497-0.1604 (above 0.005); the 32 map keeps the same structure at fraction 0.277344, roughness gap 0.3131, tilt² 0.26282 and directions at 0.21-0.29. A regression control accepted 13 legal variants (10 preset variants: lighter and darker wood palettes, board roughness 0.7 and 0.9, bead roughness 0.35 and 0.55, relief 0.02 and 0.04, bead edge softness 0.05 and 0.12; plus three source variants: quintic ramps, a finer wood grain and larger rod dots) and rejected 18 genuine faults (4 preset faults: beads as rough as the board, a board smoother than the beads, unresolved relief, bead edges softened by 0.6; 14 source faults: last digit 1 instead of 0, inverted five-bead states, a mirrored one-bead gap, dots on every second rod, no unit-rod dots, flat beads without the equator ridge, beads wider than the rod pitch, square creased beads, a frame higher than the beads, no reckoning bar, missing rods, metallic beads, seed ignored by the grain, seed moving the digits). Compatibility: all 842 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,576 samples, 141,456 channel comparisons) and ten related kinds (`ean13label`, `embossedbraille`, `papertape`, `sevensegment`, `tactilepaving`, `dominoes`, `punchcard`, `seedbeads`, `wiremesh`, `bamboo`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (60 map sets, 300 buffers) are identical to the previous build; presets and tile sizes of the old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first kernel drew the beads smaller than their nominal size (0.842 × 0.737 instead of 0.9 × 0.78) because the rounded ridge of the double cone offset the silhouette by 0.025, which the bead-size check rejected for all 35 beads, so the kernel now subtracts that offset and rescales the silhouette to the nominal half sizes; the first 512/32 px check required a board-bead roughness gap above 0.25, equal to the gap of the legal board-roughness 0.7 variant (measured 0.2418), so it was relaxed to 0.15; and an unused helper was removed after lint flagged it.

`ean13label` adds an authored EAN-13 barcode label tile: the page's example number 4 003994 155486 printed as 30 black bars on pale paper, the start, centre and end guard bars longer than the rest, the ink slightly rougher and a little raised above the paper. It is not `papertape` (punched ASCII holes), `sevensegment` or any other existing striped preset, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for barcode, EAN-13/EAN13, UPC, QR code and label found no barcode preset (the barcode hits are search-word lists in the neighbouring `papertape` entries; label hits are unrelated entries). The actually read Wikipedia International Article Number page supplies the structure: 95 equal-width areas (3 start areas 101, 42 areas for the six digits after the first, 5 centre areas 01010, 42 areas for the last six digits, 3 end areas 101), the L-, G- and R-codes of the digits 0-9 (R-codes are the bitwise complements of the L-codes and G-codes are the R-codes in reverse bit order, each digit two bars and two spaces), the table that chooses L or G for the left six digits from the first digit (LGLLGG for 4), the example 4 003994 155486 with parities OEOOEE EEEEEE, and the check digit rule (weights alternating 3 and 1 with the last data digit weighing 3; the worked example 400638133393x gives 89 and x = 1). The fetched page text gives no X-dimension, quiet zone, bar height, printing or text layout, so the 9-area quiet zones on both sides (113 areas across, a square tile), the bars starting 14 areas from the top and running 70 areas down with the guard bars running 5 areas further, the blank band below where printed digits would go (no text is drawn), the paper tone 0.86 + 0.08 × grain against an ink tone of 0.04, the 22,22,26 / 246,244,236 palette, roughness 0.55 on paper and 0.8 on ink, ink 0.3 relief units higher than the paper (relief 0.012), occlusion 0.98 falling by 0.03 on ink, and bar edges that are soft by 0.1 area on each side of every module boundary are authored approximations; no GS1 conformance, scanner readability, print quality or product identification is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.0373 m (113 areas at an authored 0.33 mm X-dimension). The independent kernel stores the 113-area bit table, 113 bar-bottom values and a 128² grain, 132,089 B of tables (113 B, 113 Float64 values and 16,384 Float64 grain values), not total RAM; each point picks one module, blends at most two module columns across a boundary with a smooth step and multiplies two smooth steps for the bar ends, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the paper grain while the bars stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: the test types the L-, G- and R-code tables and the first-digit structure table from the page itself (checking that the R-codes complement the L-codes, the G-codes reverse the R-codes, every code has two bars and two spaces, the page's example encodes and decodes to 4 003994 155486 with parity OEOOEE EEEEEE, and the check digits are 1 for 400638133393 and 6 for 400399415548), then reads the sampler at the centre of each of the 95 areas on three rows through the bars (at 20, 50 and 80 areas from the top) and decodes the bits as a scanner would (markers, six left codes choosing L or G, the first digit from the L/G pattern, six right codes, check digit). Every seed reads 4003994155486 with a valid check digit and parity OEOOEEEEEEEE from all three rows, 0 mismatched areas and 0 mismatches on a guard row at 86.5 areas, below the normal bars. A 1130 × 1130 pixel-centre raster (10 px per area) labelled into connected ink components gives 30 bars (the reference has 30 runs: 19 of one area, 4 of two, 6 of three and 1 of four) whose left, right, top and bottom all lie within 0.06 area of the reference (tops at 14, normal bars ending at 84 and guard bars at 89), 0 ink pixels in the quiet zones or outside the bar band, and an ink fraction matching the reference 0.27097 within 1%; the first bar edge crosses 50% ink at the module boundary within 0.02 area and its 10-90% width is 0.1217 area (allowed 0.03-0.3). Ink and paper tones differ by 0.8367 (above 0.5), ink roughness exceeds paper roughness by 0.2433 (above 0.12), ink height exceeds paper height by 0.2919 relief units (above 0.15) and metallic violations are 0. The 512 map has ink fraction 0.272617 (0.61% from the reference), ink minus paper roughness 0.24202, AO 242-250, luma 31.2-230.6, maximum tilt² 0.58725 (0.1-3), sideways normal fractions at least 0.0997 and up/down fractions at least 0.002727 (the bar ends are thin); the 32 map keeps only sparse aliased ink (fraction 0.117188, tilt² 0.0034756, no decode asserted because a bar is narrower than a pixel). A regression control accepted 11 legal variants (9 preset variants: bluish-white and kraft paper palettes, paper roughness 0.4, paper 0.7 with ink 0.9, ink roughness 0.7, relief 0.008 and 0.02, bar edge half-widths 0.06 and 0.15, plus two source variants: a quintic edge profile and a finer paper grain) and rejected 19 genuine faults (4 preset faults: bars blurred by an edge half-width of 0.5, ink as rough as the paper, ink smoother than the paper, unresolved relief; 15 source faults: wrong check digit, L and G swapped in the left group, right group using L-codes, mirrored symbol, missing centre guard, guard bars as short as the others, bars too short, linear creased bar edges, inverted white bars on dark, seed ignored by the grain, seed moving the digits, metallic ink, debossed ink, ink barely darker than the paper, a 3-area quiet zone). Compatibility: all 841 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,548 samples, 141,288 channel comparisons) and eleven related kinds (`rule30`, `perfectmaze`, `sevensegment`, `ulamspiral`, `papertape`, `moorecurve`, `punchcard`, `dominoes`, `tactilepaving`, `sandpaper`, `embossedbraille`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (66 map sets, 330 buffers) are identical to the previous build; presets and tile sizes of the old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first 512 px check required all four signed normal directions above 0.005, but the thin bar ends tilt up and down over only 0.2727% of the pixels, so the check now asks 0.05 for the sideways pair and 0.001 for the up/down pair; the first 32 px check required an ink fraction above 0.1 and the measured 0.117188 was too close, so the bound was relaxed to 0.05; decoding at module centres cannot see blurred edges (a half-width of 0.5 still decodes exactly), so the grain-free edge width check was added after that fault was designed; a first draft of the fixture used toEqual, which the nested control harness does not support, and compares joined strings instead.

`embossedbraille` adds an authored embossed braille tile: a cream paper face of 7 × 4 braille cells whose smoothly raised round dots spell the letters a to z in order (w skipped, three blank cells at the end), the dots slightly smoother and a little darker than the flat paper. It is not `tactilepaving` (a regular grid of truncated-cone warning studs), `dominoes` (standard pips) or any other existing dotted preset, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for braille, tactile, emboss and raised dot found no braille preset (the braille hits are search-word lists in neighboring entries; tactile and emboss hit unrelated presets). The actually read Wikipedia Braille page (cells formed from six raised dots in two columns of three, 64 possible patterns including none, positions numbered top to bottom 1 to 3 on the left and 4 to 6 on the right, dot pattern 1-3-4 being the letter m; the first ten letters a-j use the upper four positions as ⠁⠃⠉⠙⠑⠋⠛⠓⠊⠚, k-t are the same with an added dot 3 as ⠅⠇⠍⠝⠕⠏⠟⠗⠎⠞, and the next decade u v x y z adds dots 3 and 6 with w left out) supplies the cells; the page gives no dot spacing, tile or rendering, so the 7 × 4 layout, the cell pitch of 2.4 and line pitch of 4.2 dot spacings (a 16.8 × 16.8 spacing square), the blank cells, the 0.3 spacing dome radius and every other value are authored: each raised dot is a dome with height profile (1 − s²)² of the squared normalized radius (zero slope at the rim, no square root) placed in a cell at columns ±0.5 and rows −1, 0, 1, the paper is 0.4 high and the dots reach 1.0, tone is 0.82 ± 0.1 grain less 0.12 on a dot with the 168,152,128 / 244,236,216 palette, roughness is 0.85 on the paper and 0.7 at a dot top, occlusion 0.97 falling by 0.1 and relief 0.03; these values are authored approximations, no paper material, dot spacing standard, embossing process or readability is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.042 m (16.8 dot spacings of 2.5 mm, an authored typical spacing). The independent kernel stores the 28-cell code table and a 128² grain, 131,100 B of tables (16,384 Float64 values for the grain), not total RAM; each point reads one cell code, picks the nearest dot position and evaluates at most one dome, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the paper grain while the raised dots stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: the test builds the reference cells itself from the page (the a-j cells as literal characters, k-t as those with dot 3 added, u v x y z as a-e with dots 3 and 6 added, three blank cells), reads the sampler at each of the six dot positions of all 28 cells, and labels a 1000 × 1000 pixel-center raster (59.5 px per dot spacing) into connected dome components at the half-roughness contour. The page's own pattern 1-3-4 is checked to be m and the a-j cells to avoid dots 3 and 6. Every seed decodes abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvxyz followed by three blank cells with 0 mismatched cells and 80 raised dots, the raster has 80 dome components, none more than 0.03 dot spacing from a grid position (columns ±0.5, rows −1, 0, 1), and the mean footprint is 0.082922 spacing² against the predicted π(0.3)²(1 − √½) = 0.082814 (0.13% off; the test allows 5%). Dot/paper colors are 0.78089/0.86877 (0.7818/0.86865 and 0.78288/0.86871 at seeds 7 and 0xffffffff), roughness 0.73969/0.84855, heights 0.84125/0.40579 in relief units and metallic violations 0; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff flip 0 of 1,000,000 dot mask pixels, decode the same text and move paper tone up to 0.098682/0.099058 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, lines at every cell border, cell center and dot column or row offset in both axes and curvature refinement; the worst value is 0.00004279 for all seeds (below 0.04) and the signed-UV period error at most 2.83e-15 (below 5e-10). The 512 pixel map has dot fraction 0.022972, dot/paper roughness 0.73883/0.84944, AO 222–247, luma 211.82–229.47 (range above 12), maximum tilt² 0.70622 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.0392–0.039742 (above 0.01); the 32 px map has no dot pixel at all (dot fraction 0, roughness 0.84995 everywhere, AO 241–247, tilt² 0.0055671 below 0.5). A regression control accepted 12 legal variants (10 preset variants: white and kraft paper palettes, paper roughness 0.75 with dot roughness 0.6, paper roughness 0.92, dot roughness 0.55, paper 0.9 with dot 0.72, relief 0.02/0.045 and dome radius 0.25/0.34, plus two source variants with softer dome occlusion and finer paper grain) and rejected 17 genuine faults (4 preset faults: dome radius 0.55 where neighboring dots merge, dome radius 0.08, dots as rough as the paper, unresolved relief; 13 source faults: m replaced by n, dots numbered by rows, rows reversed, columns mirrored, six cells per line, a narrow cell pitch, five lines, a linear dome profile, metallic dots, seed-ignored grain, seed-moved letters, debossed dots, dots lighter than the paper). Compatibility: all 840 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,520 samples, 141,120 channel comparisons) and ten related kinds (`rule30`, `perfectmaze`, `sevensegment`, `ulamspiral`, `papertape`, `moorecurve`, `punchcard`, `dominoes`, `tactilepaving`, `sandpaper`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (60 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: at 32 px every dot is smaller than a pixel and falls between pixel centers, so the 32 px check only validates the paper map and asserts no dot count; the dome mask is the half-roughness contour, so a raised-height check was added to reject debossed dots; the pixel dot threshold was first the constant 0.78, which classified a legal paper-roughness 0.75 variant entirely as dots, so it is derived from the preset roughness pair; the legal paper-roughness 0.75 variant first broke the 0.08 roughness-gap contract with the default dot roughness 0.7, so the variant carries dot roughness 0.6; the minimum-AO bound went from 235 to 240 because the legal softer-occlusion variant measures 235; and this kernel has no smoothstep, so the legal source variants are softer occlusion and finer grain rather than the quintic substitution used elsewhere.

`rule30` adds an authored Rule 30 cellular-automaton tile: a 33 × 33 cell tile showing 33 generations of Wolfram's elementary cellular automaton Rule 30 grown from a single black cell in the middle of the top row (time running down), the black cells raised glossy dark squares and the white cells lower, rougher pale squares, separated by recessed fine grooves. It is not `sierpinskicarpet`, `moorecurve`, `ulamspiral`, `perfectmaze` or any other existing geometric or number-derived preset, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for cellular automaton, Wolfram, rule 30, cone snail and pseudorandom found no preset (the only hits are search-word lists in neighboring entries). The actually read Wikipedia Rule 30 page (an elementary cellular automaton introduced by Stephen Wolfram in 1983, a Class III rule with aperiodic, chaotic behaviour; the rule set 111→0, 110→0, 101→0, 100→1, 011→1, 010→1, 001→1, 000→0, that is left xor (center or right), named because 00011110 in binary is 30; from a single cell with state 1 among 0s, time running down, it shows frequent white triangles and a well-defined striped pattern on the left side; the numbers of black cells per generation are 1, 3, 3, 6, 4, 9, 5, 12, 7, 12, 11, 14, 12, 19, 13, 22, 15, 19, ...; a similar pattern appears on the shell of the cone snail Conus textile) supplies the rule and the counts; the page gives no tile, grid size, boundary or appearance, so the 33 × 33 grid (cells outside the array are 0, so generations beyond the sixteenth are clipped by the side edges) and every dimension are authored: each cell is a square of half size 0.42 cell with 0.05 cell shoulders (the product of two smooth intervals, 0.79 cell wide at the half-coverage contour), the black cells are raised to 0.9 with tone 0.1 and roughness 0.3, the white cells sit at 0.4 with tone 0.7 ± 0.08 grain and roughness 0.8, the grooves are at 0.3 with tone 0.35, the palette is 20,22,30 / 226,222,208, occlusion is 0.97 falling by 0.3 in the grooves and relief is 0.03; these values are authored approximations, no material, size standard or randomness property is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.66 m (33 cells of 2 cm). The independent kernel stores a 1,089-byte cell table and a 128² grain, 132,161 B of tables (16,384 Float64 values for the grain), not total RAM; the automaton runs only while the sampler is created, and each point reads one cell byte and evaluates two intervals, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the white-cell grain while the pattern stays fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: the test grows Rule 30 itself from the rule table printed on the page (one 1 in the middle of the top row, 0 outside the array), reads the sampler at the center of every one of the 1,089 cells, and labels a 1000 × 1000 pixel-center raster (30.3 px per cell, so the pixel alignment differs from cell to cell) into connected black-cell components. Every seed reads all 1,089 cells equal to the independent automaton (0 mismatches) with 445 black cells, the black-cell counts of the first 17 generations are 1, 3, 3, 6, 4, 9, 5, 12, 7, 12, 11, 14, 12, 19, 13, 22, 15 exactly as printed on the page (later generations are clipped by the 33 columns), and 402 cells differ from their mirror image so the triangle is not symmetric (a mirror image would be Rule 86). The raster has 445 black components in 445 different cells, none more than 0.03 cell from its cell center, with a mean area of 0.62356 cell² against the predicted 0.6241 for the half-coverage square (0.09% off; the test allows 3%). Black/non-black colors are 0.10569/0.54131 (0.10569/0.54113 and 0.10569/0.54109 at seeds 7 and 0xffffffff; the non-black average includes the grooves), roughness 0.31137/0.79596, heights 0.88635/0.35437 in relief units and metallic violations 0; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff flip 0 of 1,000,000 mask pixels, keep 0 mismatches and move white-cell tone up to 0.078553/0.078962 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, lines at every cell border, cell center and tile edge offset in both axes, diagonals through every cell across the tile corners and curvature refinement; the worst value is 0.00064474 for all seeds (below 0.04) and the signed-UV period error at most 4.44e-16 (below 5e-10). The 512 pixel map has black fraction 0.25616, black/white roughness 0.31457/0.79631, AO 171–247, luma 42.221–177.78 (range above 80, darkest below 70), maximum tilt² 0.98562 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.13696–0.13888 (above 0.01); the 32 px map keeps black fraction 0.22168, roughness 0.33606/0.79925, the same AO range, luma 42.221–177.99, tilt² 0.10719 (below 0.5) and signed fractions 0.13184–0.14063. A regression control accepted 13 legal variants (12 preset variants: blue-grey and sepia tile palettes, white-cell roughness 0.65/0.9, black-cell roughness 0.15/0.45, relief 0.02/0.045, half size 0.38/0.45 and shoulder 0.03/0.08, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 21 genuine faults (5 preset faults: half size 0.58 that its cell cuts off, half size 0.1, no color range, black cells as rough as white cells, unresolved relief; 16 source faults: Rule 90, the mirror image Rule 86, the complement Rule 135, a reversed neighbour bit order, a seed cell off center, a wrap-around boundary, time running upward, linear edges, metallic black cells, seed-ignored grain, a seed-moved starting cell, grout gray blended into the black cells, black cells not raised, black and white swapped, 31 columns, creased tile corners). Compatibility: all 839 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,492 samples, 140,952 channel comparisons) and ten related kinds (`perfectmaze`, `sevensegment`, `ulamspiral`, `papertape`, `moorecurve`, `sierpinskicarpet`, `chladnifigure`, `punchcard`, `dominoes`, `crackleglaze`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (60 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first raster used 32 px per cell, so every tile was counted at the same pixel alignment (26 pixel centers across a 25.28 px tile) and the mean area read 5.15% high, so the raster became 1000 × 1000 (the ratio is now 0.99914) and the 3% tolerance was kept; the centroid tolerance went from 0.02 to 0.03 cell (about one pixel) because the legal shoulder 0.08 variant measured 0.0209 and the default 0.0196 sat at the old bound; a grout-gray fault was accepted because the luma range did not change and then rejected only marginally (darkest luma 92 against 90), so the darkest-luma bound became 70 (the default measures 42.221 and every legal palette variant passes); and the nested test harness has no toEqual, so the generation counts are compared as joined strings.

`perfectmaze` adds an authored seeded perfect-maze tile: an 8 × 8 cell maze whose corridors are recessed, dark, smoother channels between pale, rougher raised walls, the 64 cells joined by 63 links so that every cell is reachable and no loop exists, and a different maze for every seed. It is not `moorecurve` (one deterministic closed groove loop without branches), `braincoral` (natural labyrinthine ridges), `guilloche`, `greekkey`, `truchettiles`, `hextruchettiles`, `circuitboard` or the other existing groove and tiled presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for maze, labyrinth, spanning tree and backtrack found no maze preset (the labyrinth hits are `braincoral`'s natural ridges and `moorecurve`'s own wording). The actually read Wikipedia Maze generation algorithm page (a maze can be treated as a connected graph whose nodes are cells and whose edges are wall sites, and generation is often approached as a random spanning tree so that no region is unreachable and no loop confuses a solver; randomized depth-first search, the recursive backtracker, starts from a cell, moves to a random unvisited neighbour while removing the wall between them, backtracks at dead ends, and gives a low branching factor with many long corridors) supplies the construction; the 8 × 8 size, the xorshift generator seeded from the seed, the neighbour order (east, south, west, north), the corridor geometry and every dimension are authored: each cell joins its linked neighbours with a horizontal and a vertical band, each the product of two smooth intervals with half width 0.25 cell and shoulder 0.05 cell (so the half-coverage corridor is 0.45 cell wide, 3.6 cm at 8 cm cells), the bands run straight through the cell border toward a linked neighbour so cells join C1, the floor is the union 1 − (1 − horizontal)(1 − vertical), and no link crosses the tile border so every repeated tile holds its own maze. The floor is recessed 0.45 below the 0.8 wall; wall tone is 0.8 ± 0.1 grain and floor tone 0.2 with the 48,42,36 / 214,204,184 palette, roughness 0.55 on the walls and 0.85 in the corridors, occlusion 0.97 falling to 0.6 in the corridors and relief 0.03; these values are authored approximations, no material, size standard or difficulty is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.64 m (8 × 8 cells of 8 cm). The independent kernel stores 64 link bytes and a 128² grain, 131,264 B of tables including the 128 scratch bytes of the generator (16,384 Float64 values for the grain), not total RAM; the depth-first search runs only while the sampler is created, and each point reads one link byte and evaluates four intervals, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: the test reads the maze the way a walker sees it, one sampler read at each of the 64 cell centers and at each of the 112 shared edge midpoints (a read is open when it is recessed floor), builds the graph and checks it with a union-find and two breadth-first searches, and labels a 1024 × 1024 pixel-center raster (128 px per cell) into connected floor and wall components. Every seed gives 64 open cell centers, 63 links, 0 cycles, 64 cells reached from cell (0,0), and 0 open reads at the 16 tile-border midpoints; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff differ from seed 0 in 60 and 54 of the 112 possible links, re-creating a sampler for the same seed gives the same links, and the depth-first signature is 6/8/7 junction cells, 8/10/9 dead ends and a longest route of 50/47/41 steps at seeds 0/7/0xffffffff. The raster has 1 floor component and 1 wall component per seed, and the floor fraction is 0.45614/0.45615/0.45615 against 0.44613 predicted from the half-coverage corridor width (0.45 cell: 64 center squares plus 63 arms; 2.2% above because the unions round the inner corners, the test allows 5%). Floor/wall colors are 0.21505/0.84209 (0.21508/0.84253 and 0.21509/0.84274 at seeds 7 and 0xffffffff), roughness 0.84305/0.55353, occlusion 0.60858/0.96565 and metallic violations 0; the always-wall strip at u = 0.01 moves tone up to 0.066155/0.067177 between seeds (above 0.01). Compatibility: all 838 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,464 samples, 140,784 channel comparisons) and ten related kinds (`sevensegment`, `ulamspiral`, `papertape`, `moorecurve`, `sierpinskicarpet`, `chladnifigure`, `punchcard`, `dominoes`, `truchettiles`, `hextruchettiles`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (60 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first fixture accepted a Prim-like growth fault because its depth-first bounds (fewer than 20 junctions, diameter above 20) were too loose, so they were measured (Prim-like growth on eight seeds gave 13–21 junctions, 16–24 dead ends and diameter 16–26; depth-first on twelve seeds gave 4–9, 6–11 and 41–53) and tightened to fewer than 12 junctions, fewer than 14 dead ends and a diameter above 33, which is a statistical signature on three seeds and not a proof of the algorithm; a seed-ignored-grain fault was accepted because seeds also move the maze, so the always-wall strip probe was added; a creased-junction fault (the maximum of the two bands) was accepted because no checked line crossed its crease, so diagonals through every cell were added and it is now rejected (163.10 against 0.04); the floor fraction tolerance went from 3% to 5% after the measured 2.2% surplus from the rounded inner corners; and the AO bound went from 150 to 170 because the corridor occlusion is 0.6 (153).

`sevensegment` adds an authored seven-segment display panel tile: a dark, glossy-faced non-metallic panel in a 5 × 2 grid of digit cells showing 0123456789, the lit segments bright amber chamfered bars and the unlit segments dim ghosts, all recessed below the face. It is not `chipresistors` (a white 103 marking drawn as continuous strokes on component bodies) or any other existing preset that renders characters, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for seven-segment, segment display, digit and calculator found no preset that draws digits as segments. The actually read Wikipedia Segment display page (a seven-segment display shows digits and some letters; its segments are referred to by the letters a to g, with an optional decimal point; a byte can hold the whole state, and in the popular gfedcba encoding 0x06 lights segments c and b to display a 1; the most common decimal patterns are 0 abcdef, 1 bc, 2 abdeg, 3 abcdg, 4 bcfg, 5 acdfg, 6 acdefg, 7 abc, 8 abcdefg and 9 abcdfg, with alternatives such as a 7 with a tail) supplies the digit patterns; the fetched text gives no segment positions, proportions or appearance, so the layout (a top, b upper right, c lower right, d bottom, e lower left, f upper left, g middle, y running down in UV), the 5 × 2 grid in reading order and every dimension are authored: each bar has half length 0.3 and half width 0.06 of a digit cell width with 45° chamfered ends, centered at (0, ±0.8), (±0.34, ±0.4) and (0, 0) in a cell that is 1 wide and 2.5 tall, and each bar is the product of four smooth half-plane masks (two sides, two chamfers, the sign along the bar folded) so the pointed tips stay C1. The bars are recessed 0.1 below the 0.6 face; tone is 0.05 ± 0.02 grain on the panel, +0.15 on the unlit ghosts and +0.75 on the lit bars with the 14,10,10 / 255,150,40 palette, roughness 0.45 on the panel and 0.2 on the lit bars, occlusion 0.97 falling by 0.25 on the ghosts and relief 0.03; these values are authored approximations, no LED, LCD, emission or standard is modeled or claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.2 m (a 5 × 2 grid of cells 4 cm wide and 10 cm tall). The independent kernel stores a 128² grain, 131,072 B of table (16,384 Float64 values), not total RAM; each point folds one pattern code, skips bars that are out of reach and evaluates at most a few smooth masks, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the panel grain while the digits stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency, emission or displacement.

Every seed decodes the text 0123456789 (49 lit slots and 21 unlit ghost slots, the gfedcba bytes of 1 and 8 being 0x06 and 0x7f), the raster has 70 bar components on 70 distinct slots, 49 of them lit on 49 distinct slots, each within 2e-16 digit widths of its slot center, the mean bar area is 0.0523 digit-width² against the predicted 0.052172 for the half-coverage contour (the nominal 4Lw − 2w² = 0.07735 less an inset of half the shoulder; 0.25% off, the test allows 3%) and the lit fraction is 0.10251 against 0.10226 predicted. `ulamspiral` adds an authored Ulam prime spiral tile: the integers 1-225 written in a 15 × 15 cell square spiral with 1 at the center, the cells holding primes marked by glossy dark raised domes on a pale, rougher non-metallic slab cut by recessed cell grooves. It is not `tactilepaving` (a regular grid of truncated-cone warning studs), `dominoes` (standard 0-6 pip layouts) or any other existing dotted or perforated preset, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for ulam, prime, spiral and number theory found no preset whose pattern comes from numbers (the existing spiral hits are curled forms such as fiddleheads, cinnamon bark coils and palmiers). The actually read Wikipedia Ulam spiral page (devised by Stanisław Ulam in 1963 and popularized by Martin Gardner; the positive integers are written in a square spiral, most often with 1 at the center, and the primes are marked; lines in the spiral correspond to quadratic polynomials 4n² + bn + c, and since all numbers on a diagonal line are odd or all are even, all primes other than 2 lie in alternate diagonals) supplies the construction; the fetched text does not describe the figure's orientation, so the direction (2 to the right of 1, then counterclockwise, rows running downward in UV), the 15 × 15 size and every dimension are authored: the cell at offset (x, y) from the center is numbered by ring r = max(|x|, |y|) from (2r + 1)² and the side it lies on, and a 226-entry sieve marks the primes (48 of 225). Each marked cell holds one dome of radius 0.38 cell with height profile (1 − s²)² of the squared normalized radius (zero slope at the rim, no square root), the slab is 0.3 high with grooves 0.12 deep and a half width of 0.05 cell at every cell border (a product union of two smooth one-dimensional boxes so cell corners join C1), domes reach 0.9, slab tone is 0.74 ± 0.12 grain minus 0.3 in the grooves and 0.09 on the domes with the 30,38,58 / 234,226,206 palette, roughness 0.8 on the slab and 0.3 on the domes, occlusion 0.97 falling to 0.65 in the grooves and relief 0.02; these values are authored approximations, no material, standard, product or mathematical certification is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.375 m (15 cells of 2.5 cm). The independent kernel stores a 226-byte sieve, 225 prime flags and a 128² grain, 131,523 B of tables (16,384 Float64 values for the grain), not total RAM; the spiral numbering and sieve run only while the sampler is created, and each point reads one flag and evaluates two boxes plus at most one dome, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the slab grain while the marked primes stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Every seed marks exactly the 48 prime cells (0 mismatches over 225 cells, one mark on 2, none on 1, and all 47 odd primes on cells with x + y even, the alternate diagonals), the raster has 48 dome components in 48 different cells, none more than 0.02 cell from its cell center, and the mean footprint is 0.22776 cell² against the predicted 0.5π(0.38)² = 0.22682 (0.4% off; the test allows 3%; the footprint is where the profile exceeds a quarter, s < 0.7071). Dome/slab colors are 0.09/0.74523 (0.09/0.74537 and 0.09/0.74549 at seeds 7 and 0xffffffff), roughness 0.3/0.78315, groove/slab heights 0.18/0.3 (relief units) and occlusion 0.65/0.97 with metallic violations 0; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff flip 0 of 1,102,500 dome mask pixels, keep the same marked primes and move slab tone up to 0.11787/0.11904 (above 0.01). A regression control accepted 13 legal variants (12 preset variants: blue-grey and warm slab palettes, slab roughness 0.65/0.9, dome roughness 0.2/0.45, relief 0.012/0.03, dome radius 0.33/0.42 and groove half width 0.03/0.07, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 23 genuine faults (6 preset faults: dome radius 0.9 that its cell cuts off, dome radius 0.15, no color range, domes as rough as the slab, unresolved or extreme relief; 17 source faults: clockwise spiral, 1 not at the center, 1 counted as prime, composites marked, 2 skipped, an incomplete sieve, a 13 × 13 grid, seed-moved primes, a linear dome profile, metallic domes, no cell grooves, creased groove corners, seed-ignored grain, grout gray blended into the domes, domes not raised, light domes, swapped grid axes). `papertape` adds an authored punched paper tape tile: one inch of eight-level tape (ten 0.1 inch character rows by nine hole tracks) in a pale non-metallic paper that encodes the ASCII text PAPER TAPE in punched holes, with a row of smaller sprocket holes nearer one edge and dark backing visible through every hole, the holes rougher, darker and with lower occlusion. It is not `punchcard` (2 × 4 cream cards with 20 × 8 rectangular punches) or any other existing perforated or dotted preset, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for punched tape, braille, morse, barcode, QR, seven-segment, dot-matrix, ulam, cellular automaton, piano roll and music box found no preset that encodes data in its pattern. The actually read Wikipedia Punched tape page (data are the presence or absence of holes in rows across the tape; a row of smaller sprocket holes is always punched, slightly closer to one edge so that it divides the tape into unequal widths with the narrower side holding the least significant bits; a common 1 inch wide tape for six or more bits, hole spacing 0.1 inch in both directions, data holes 0.072 inch (1.8 mm) and sprocket holes 0.046 inch (1.2 mm) in diameter; its example of binary 01011010 as ASCII Z) supplies the geometry; the fetched text gives no message, track assignment or parity convention, so these are authored: a hole is a 1 bit, the sprocket row is track 4 of nine (0.4 of the tape width from the narrow edge, 0.6 from the other), tracks 1-3 hold bits 0-2 and tracks 5-9 hold bits 3-7, and bit 7 is the even-parity bit, so every character row has an even number of data holes. The kernel builds each row byte from the ASCII code of PAPER TAPE plus that parity bit; the holes are discs of radius 0.36 (data) and 0.23 (sprocket) row pitches with a 0.05 smooth shoulder (the page's 0.072 and 0.046 inch diameters over the 0.1 inch pitch), the paper is 0.7 high and the backing 0.1 (a 0.6 drop), a tape-edge seam line is 0.012 of the tile wide and 0.15 deep, paper tone is 0.72 ± 0.14 grain with the 58,48,38 / 236,224,196 palette, roughness is 0.75 on the paper and 0.92 in the holes, occlusion falls from 0.97 to 0.30 in the holes and relief is 0.008; these values are authored approximations, the 0.1 mm tape thickness, translucency, oiled or chadless paper, tape reels and punching tolerances are not modeled, and no standard, device or product is claimed and no image is copied or bundled. One UV tile represents 0.0254 m (one inch of tape, ten character rows). The independent kernel stores 10 row bytes and a 128² grain, 131,082 B of tables (16,384 Float64 values for the grain), not total RAM; each point reads one row byte, selects the nearest track and evaluates at most one disc with one square root, so no hypot, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the paper fibres while the punched text stays fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: the tape is read the way a reader would, one sampler read at each of the nine track centers of every one of the ten character rows, and then a 1000 × 1000 pixel-center raster (100 px per 0.1 inch pitch) is labeled into connected hole components. Every seed decodes the bit rows into the text PAPER TAPE (bits 0-6 as ASCII) with 0 rows of odd parity, 10 sprocket holes (one per row) and 28 data holes, so the raster has 38 hole components, none of them more than 0.02 pitch from a track center, 10 on track 4 and 28 elsewhere. Mean hole areas are 0.1304 pitch² for the sprocket holes and 0.3512 for the data holes against the predicted π(R − 0.025)² = 0.13203 and 0.35257 (1.2% and 0.4% off; the test allows 3%), their ratio is 2.69 (above 1.8), and every sprocket hole centroid sits at track 4.0000 (0.4 of the tape width from the narrow edge, not at the center). The 512 pixel map has hole fraction 0.10985, hole/paper roughness 0.91772/0.74991, AO 76–247, luma 63.3318–199.746 (range above 80), maximum tilt² 0.62945 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.02205–0.03191 (above 0.01); the 32 px map keeps hole fraction 0.10352, roughness 0.92053/0.74965, the same AO and luma range, tilt² 0.011103 (below 0.5) and signed fractions 0.09473–0.09668. `moorecurve` adds an authored Moore-curve groove tile: one closed, continuous dark groove looping through every cell of an 8 × 8 cell tile in a pale non-metallic face, the groove recessed, rougher and darker. It is not `braincoral` (natural labyrinthine ridges), `guilloche`, `greekkey`, `truchettiles`, `hextruchettiles`, `circuitboard` or the other existing groove, maze and tiled presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for hilbert, peano, moore and space-filling found no preset with this curve (the existing meander and labyrinth hits are natural ridges and chains). The actually read Wikipedia Moore curve page (a continuous fractal space-filling curve, the loop version of the Hilbert curve, which may be thought of as the union of four copies of Hilbert curves combined so that the endpoints coincide) supplies the idea; the fetched text did not include its L-system rules, so the discrete construction is authored and numerically checked here: an order-2 Hilbert curve on a 4 × 4 block (iterative bit-conversion from curve index to cell, starting at its corner (0,0) and ending at (3,0) with adjacent steps) is rotated into the four quadrants (counter-clockwise bottom-left and top-left, clockwise top-right and bottom-right, entering and leaving at the vertical midline) so that the 64 cells form one Hamiltonian cycle whose closing step is also a neighbor step. The groove is the union of a central square and an arm toward each linked neighbor, each a product of smooth one-dimensional boxes (half width 0.17 cell, shoulder 0.04 cell, so the width is 0.3 cell, 2.4 cm at the 0.64 m nominal tile with 8 cm cells), the union is 1 − ∏(1 − part), and arms run straight to the cell border so neighboring cells join C1; no arm crosses the tile border, so each repeated tile holds its own loop. The groove is recessed 0.45 below the 0.7 face, face tone 0.70–0.80 and groove tone about 0.14–0.24 with the 46,42,40 / 228,220,202 palette, roughness 0.45 on the face and 0.9 in the groove, occlusion 0.96 falling to 0.46 and relief 0.015 are authored approximations; no material, engraving process, standard or product is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. The independent kernel stores 64 link bytes, 128 path bytes and a 128² grain, 131,264 B of tables (16,384 Float64 values for the grain), not total RAM; the Hilbert conversion runs only while the sampler is created, and each point reads one link byte and evaluates two boxes plus at most four arms, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0. Seeds change only the face grain while the loop stays fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: the groove at all 64 cell centers and at the shared edge midpoints between neighboring cells is read directly from the sampler. Every seed gives 64 groove cell centers, 0 groove links across the tile border, 64 internal links (every cell has exactly 2 links, minimum and maximum degree 2), one groove component and two face components (inside and outside of the closed loop) in a 1024×1024 periodic raster. Walking the measured links from cell (0,0) visits 64 distinct cells and closes back at the start (one Hamiltonian cycle), and every aligned 2 × 2 and 4 × 4 cell block occupies consecutive steps of the cyclic walk (the Hilbert-curve locality that distinguishes it from other loops; the 4 × 4 blocks are the four quadrants). The measured link set is mirror symmetric across the vertical midline (120 of 120 link comparisons), the groove mask agrees with its mirror image at 0.99993/0.999931/0.999918 of the pixels, and the groove area fraction is 0.30012/0.30012/0.30011 against the predicted 2 × 0.17 − 0.04 = 0.3 (the test allows 5%). Groove/face colors are 0.1524/0.7434 (0.1524/0.7431 and 0.1524/0.7433 at seeds 7 and 0xffffffff), roughness 0.8908/0.4551, occlusion 0.4702/0.9543 and metallic violations 0; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff flip only 73 and 70 of 1,048,576 mask pixels (grain moves the 0.01 height term; the test allows 0.1%) and move tone up to 0.09812/0.09728 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, lines at every cell border and cell center in both axes and curvature refinement along eight lines per axis; the worst value is 0.000041008 for all seeds (below 0.04) and the signed-UV period error at most 7.77e-16 (below 5e-10). The 512 pixel map has groove fraction 0.3119, groove/face roughness 0.88389/0.45261, AO 117–245, luma 67.5616–184.405 (range above 80), maximum tilt² 0.73464 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.03096–0.03469 (above 0.01); the 32 px map keeps groove fraction 0.5 (the groove spans two of every four pixels per cell), roughness 0.90196/0.45098, the same AO and luma range, tilt² 0.022422 (below 0.5) and signed fractions 0.2344–0.2656. A regression control accepted 11 legal variants (10 preset variants over stone-grey and warm-sand palettes, face roughness 0.3/0.6, relief 0.01/0.025, half width 0.15/0.27 and shoulder 0.02/0.07, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 20 genuine faults (7 preset faults: half width 0.5 that fills every cell, half width 0.02 that erases the groove, shoulder 0.4, no color range, face as rough as the groove, unresolved or extreme relief; 13 source faults: wrong quadrant orientation, open Hilbert path without the closing link, cell centers without arms, one-sided arms, linear groove edges, metallic groove, seed-ignored grain, seed-shifted path, light groove, no groove occlusion, groove as smooth as the face, grout gray blended into the groove, groove not recessed). Compatibility: all 834 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,352 comparisons) and eleven related kinds (`sierpinskicarpet`, `chladnifigure`, `kisrhombilletiles`, `greekkey`, `truchettiles`, `hextruchettiles`, `circuitboard`, `pythagoreantiles`, `puzzletile`, `tactilepaving`, `guilloche`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (66 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first tile was a 16 × 16 cell order-4 loop, but at 32 px its pixel centers sit 0.25 cell off the groove center line, so the groove vanished from the 32 px map (fraction 0 against the 0.1 minimum); it was redesigned as the 8 × 8 order-3 loop, where 4 px per cell keeps groove hits; the roughness gap bound went from 0.3 to 0.25 after a legal face-roughness 0.6 variant measured 0.29, the width tolerance from 2% to 5% after the legal half-width 0.15 variant measured 2.16% off, and the seed mask comparison from exactly 0 flips to below 0.1% because the grain moves 70–73 edge pixels; and the first half-width 0.05 fault was rejected only marginally (5.06% against 5%), so it was replaced by 0.02.

`sierpinskicarpet` adds an authored Sierpinski-carpet stone tile: four levels of the carpet on an 81 × 81 cell tile, with the central third of every surviving block recessed, giving 1 recess of 27 × 27 cells, 8 of 9 × 9, 64 of 3 × 3 and 512 of 1 × 1 (585 in total) in a pale non-metallic stone face, the larger recesses deeper and darker. It is not `perforatedmetal`, `cofferedconcrete`, `splitfaceblock`, `breezeblock`, `tactilepaving` or the other existing pitted, panelled or tiled presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for sierpinski, fractal, menger, cantor and space-filling found no preset with this recursive pattern. The actually read Wikipedia page (Sierpiński carpet: a square is cut into 9 congruent subsquares in a 3-by-3 grid, the central one removed and the same procedure applied recursively to the remaining 8, equivalently the points of the unit square whose base-three coordinates do not both have a digit 1 in the same position, area zero and Hausdorff dimension log 8 / log 3 ≈ 1.8928 in the limit) supplies the construction rule. The texture is a finite four-level approximation, not the limit set: 4,096 = 8⁴ surviving cells and 2,465 = 81² − 8⁴ recessed cells, so the nominal recessed fraction is 1 − (8/9)⁴ ≈ 0.3757. Each recess is the product of two smooth one-dimensional boxes, inset 0.04 cell per side with a 0.14 cell shoulder, so edges are C1 without a smooth minimum, and the tile border cells are never recessed so the tile repeats seamlessly. The recess floors sit at relative heights 0.1, 0.17, 0.24 and 0.31 against the 0.7 face (larger recesses deeper), floor tones 0.14–0.32 against the face 0.58–0.70, roughness 0.55 on the face and 0.88 in recesses, occlusion 0.96 falling to 0.46, the 62,52,44 / 218,200,168 palette, 0.02 UV-relative relief and the 0.81 m nominal tile (1 cm cells) are authored approximations; no stone species, carving process, cell standard or product is claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. The independent kernel stores a 128² grain, 16,384 Float64 values / 131,072 B of table, not total RAM, plus four-entry constants; each point tests at most four levels with a base-3 digit loop and evaluates two smooth boxes per surviving level, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped and mortar stays 0 so no grout gray is blended. Seeds change only the stone grain and tone while the recess layout stays fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Every seed yields exactly 585 recess components, 1, 8, 64 and 512 at the four levels (classified by the independent base-3 digit rule at each component centroid, 0 misplaced), with mean areas 717.05, 77.049, 7.716 and 0.60494 cell² against the predicted 717.168, 77.088, 7.728 and 0.608 (within 0.5%; the test allows 5% and 20% for the one-cell recesses, which are only 7–8 px wide). Classifying all 81 × 81 = 6,561 cell centers against the same digit rule gives 2,465 recessed cells and 0 wrong cells, the recess area fraction is 0.32571 (0.1% from the predicted sum; the test allows 6%), the surface forms 1 connected component and the mean recess floors rise 0.1 < 0.17 < 0.24 < 0.31 < 0.45 from the largest to the smallest recesses. Recess/face colors are 0.2273/0.6387 at seed 0 (0.2275/0.6396 and 0.2271/0.6389 at seeds 7 and 0xffffffff), roughness 0.8788/0.5508, occlusion 0.4618/0.9588 and metallic violations 0; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff flip 0 mask pixels while pixel tone moves by up to 0.117/0.119 (above 0.01).
