The 512 pixel map has recess fraction 0.32199, recess/face roughness 0.87508/0.55272, AO 117–245, luma 74.4722–157.384 (range above 60), maximum tilt² 0.94195 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.04663–0.04666 (above 0.01); the 32 px map has recess fraction 0.29297, roughness 0.87843/0.55036, the same AO and luma range, tilt² 0.067943 (below 0.5) and signed fractions 0.1563, so only the coarse levels survive at 32. A regression control accepted 11 legal variants (10 preset variants over blue-slate and terracotta palettes, face roughness 0.45/0.65, relief 0.012/0.03, shoulder 0.08/0.2 and inset 0.02/0.07, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 19 genuine faults (6 preset faults: inset 0.45 that erases the one-cell recesses, shoulder 0.9, no color range, face as rough as the recesses, unresolved or extreme relief; 13 source faults: recess where either digit is 1, missing finest level, recesses inside removed blocks, shifted recess centers, equal recess depth, linear recess edges, metallic recesses, light recess floors, seed-moved layout, seed-ignored grain, no recess occlusion, recesses as smooth as the face, grout gray blended into recesses). Compatibility: all 833 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,324 comparisons) and eleven related kinds (`chladnifigure`, `kisrhombilletiles`, `perforatedmetal`, `sandstone`, `limestone`, `cofferedconcrete`, `splitfaceblock`, `breezeblock`, `tactilepaving`, `diamondplate`, `honeycomb`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (66 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first control run failed a legal shoulder-0.08 variant on the 5% area bounds because one-cell recesses are only 7–8 px wide at 9 px per cell (about 14% quantization), so the fixture now allows 20% for that level and 6% for the total area (I relaxed the fixture and kept the variant); and the first inset-0.3 fault was rejected only marginally (5.6% against 5%), so it was replaced by inset 0.45, which erases the one-cell recesses outright.

`chladnifigure` adds an authored Chladni-figure surface: pale sand collected along the nodal lines of a standing-wave pattern on a dark, glossier non-metallic plate, with the sand raised slightly above the plate and rougher than it. It is not `sanddune`, `pebblebeach`, `sandstone`, `perforatedmetal` or the other existing sand, stone and plate presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for chladni and cymatic found no preset with this pattern (Fibonacci/phyllotaxis, sierpinski, hilbert and similar mathematical-pattern searches were also empty). The actually read Wikipedia page (the requested Chladni figure URL returned the page titled Ernst Chladni, whose Chladni figures section says a resonating plate or membrane divides into regions vibrating in opposite directions bounded by nodal lines where no vibration occurs, and that Chladni bowed a piece of metal lightly covered with sand so that the sand concentrated along the nodal lines where the surface stays still) supplies only the physical idea. The page gives no formula, so the nodal function is an authored idealization and not a model of any physical plate: f(u,v) = cos(aπu)cos(bπv) − cos(bπu)cos(aπv) with a = 5 and b = 9, where equal-parity modes give f(u+1,v) = ±f and f(u,v+1) = ±f, so its zero set repeats exactly with the UV tile (mismatched parity breaks the seam), swapping u and v negates f, and u → 1−u or v → 1−v only flips its sign, so the pattern mirrors across both axes and the diagonal. Sand width is a first-order distance to the zero set, |f| / √(|∇f|² + 3²), instead of a threshold on f, so the line width stays even and only the crossings pile up a little; the sand coverage is smooth(1 − distance / (0.012 × (0.75 + 0.5 × grain))) with a seeded periodic 128² grain, which roughens the sand edge by ±25% of the width (a line is about 0.012 of the tile, roughly 7 mm at the 0.6 m nominal tile), the sand rises about 0.5 of the relief above the plate, roughness goes from 0.34 on the plate to 0.93 on the sand, occlusion from 0.97 to 0.72 and the 26,29,34 / 232,220,194 palette gives a very dark plate (about 0.12–0.15) and pale sand (0.82–0.95). The mode numbers, width, gradient floor 3, relief 0.01 and roughness are authored; boundary conditions, material, excitation, sand-grain physics and any product are not claimed, and no image is copied or bundled. The independent kernel stores a 128² grain, 16,384 Float64 values / 131,072 B of table, not total RAM, and each point evaluates four cosines, four sines and one square root with no hash or allocation; generic detail is skipped. It writes zero mortar because a nonzero value would blend the grout gray over the plate. Seeds change only the sand grain (edge roughness and tone) while the nodal lines stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters, and an independent analytic nodal distance is computed in the test from the preset's mode numbers, width and gradient floor: at 1024×1024 pixel centers, every pixel closer than 0.3 width to the nodal set is sand (height/relief above 0.37) and every pixel farther than 0.7 width is plate, with 0 violations at all three seeds. The sand area fraction is 0.15424/0.15398/0.15377, between the analytic fractions 0.10216 (distance below 0.34 width) and 0.1983 (below 0.68 width); the sand forms 5 connected pieces (the analytic count is 5 at both thresholds, periodic 4-connectivity) and the plate splits into 20 regions (nodal domains; 20 at both thresholds). Mirror agreement of sand pixels across u → 1−u, v → 1−v and the u/v diagonal is 0.9372/0.9378/0.937 at seed 0, 0.9369/0.9353/0.9345 at seed 7 and 0.9342/0.9348/0.9341 at seed 0xffffffff (above 0.88; not exact because the grain moves the edges). Sand colors average 0.7429 against plate 0.1558 (gap above 0.5), roughness 0.8165 against 0.3565 (gap above 0.3), occlusion 0.7681 against 0.963 (gap above 0.15) and 0 metallic violations; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff flip 1.96% and 2.00% of mask pixels (below 3%, edge pixels only) and move individual pixel tones by up to 0.3655/0.3576 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, lines at u and v = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 (tile seams and the u = 0.5 nodal line) and curvature refinement along eight lines per axis; the worst value is 0.00064948/0.00064282/0.00053402 (below 0.04) and the signed-UV period error at most 1.39e-16 (below 5e-10). The 512 pixel map has sand fraction 0.15984, sand/plate roughness 0.80913/0.35554, AO 184–247, luma 51.8596–210.606 (range above 100), maximum tilt² 0.52795 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.1222–0.1233 (above 0.01); the 32 px map has sand fraction 0.15625, roughness 0.82782/0.35263, AO 184–247, the same luma range and tilt² 0.016271 (below 0.5), so the figure survives coarsely even at 32. A regression control accepted 13 legal variants (12 preset variants over cool steel and warm bronze palettes, plate roughness 0.25/0.45, relief 0.007/0.014, width 0.009/0.016, gradient floor 2/4 and mode pairs 3/7 and 4/8, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 21 genuine faults (9 preset faults: 0.06 wide lines, 0.0004 sub-pixel lines, gradient floor 40, no color range, plate as rough as sand, unresolved or extreme relief, mismatched mode parity 4/9, identical modes 5/5; 12 source faults: threshold on f instead of distance, wrong gradient sign, seed-moved nodal lines, unraised sand, metallic sand, bright plate, sand as glossy as the plate, seed-ignored grain, grout gray blended into the plate, linear sand profile, no sand occlusion, anisotropic distance). Compatibility: all 832 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,296 comparisons) and twelve related kinds (`kisrhombilletiles`, `truncatedtrihexagonaltiles`, `trihexagonaltiles`, `rhombille`, `sandstone`, `pebblebeach`, `cobblestone`, `gongsurface`, `drumskin`, `sanddune`, `perforatedmetal`, `diamondplate`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (72 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first prototype wrote mortar = 1 − sand and so blended the grout gray (153,153,139) into the plate, which I saw in the preview and fixed before integration; the first fixture thresholds were measured against the prototype and then relaxed to the observed values with margin (color gap 0.6 → 0.5, sand color 0.75 → 0.6, roughness gap 0.5 → 0.3 after a legal plate-roughness 0.45 variant failed the 0.4 bound); and the first 0.0015 hairline-width fault was accepted (the 1.5 px line is still resolved at 1024), so it was replaced by a 0.0004 sub-pixel fault.

`kisrhombilletiles` adds an authored kisrhombille (V4.6.12) glazed tiling: every hexagon of a triangular lattice is cut into twelve congruent 30-60-90 right triangles by six spokes to its corners and six to its edge midpoints, and the triangles alternate deep teal and cream around each hexagon, so every straight edge lies on one of six parallel line families 30° apart; every face has a narrow bevelled edge inside rougher gray grout. It is not `rhombille` (three lozenges per hexagon), `trihexagonaltiles` (hexagons and triangles, 3.6.3.6), `righttriangletiles` (right-isosceles triangles in split squares), its dual `truncatedtrihexagonaltiles` (4.6.12) or the other existing tile presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT and the preset catalog for kisrhombille, 30-60-90, deltoidal, tetrakis, triakis, floret and prismatic pentagon found no preset with this tiling (the only floret hit was an unrelated broccoli bud). The actually read Wikipedia page (the requested Kisrhombille tiling URL returned the page titled Truncated trihexagonal tiling, whose Kisrhombille tiling section says the tiling is constructed by congruent 30-60-90 triangles with 4, 6 and 12 triangles meeting at each vertex, can be seen as an equilateral hexagonal tiling with each hexagon divided into 12 triangles from the center point, alternatively as a bisected triangular tiling or as an infinite arrangement of lines in six parallel families, is labeled V4.6.12, and has the triangles as fundamental domains of p6m [6,3] symmetry) supplies the topology. The geometry is derived and numerically checked rather than copied: with hexagon edge 1 the hexagon apothem is √3/2, hexagon centers sit on a triangular lattice of pitch √3 ≈ 1.73205, each triangle has hypotenuse 1 (the spoke to a corner), long leg √3/2 and short leg 1/2 (area √3/8 ≈ 0.21651), a hexagon has area 3√3/2 ≈ 2.59808, and a 300,000-point sampler check of the 12 sectors gave a tile fraction of 0.72137 against the 0.72205 predicted from the inset 30-60-90 geometry. The 7 columns × 4 double rows per UV tile (56 hexagons = 672 triangles, a 1.04% wider-than-tall supercell stretched onto the square UV tile, the same near-square convention as the existing 7 × 8 hexagonal tile presets), 0.02 grout per side, 0.015 shoulder, teal/cream palette (28,70,84 / 236,226,200), glaze roughness 0.3, grout roughness 0.92, 0.012 UV-relative relief and the 1.2 m nominal tile (hexagon edge about 0.1 m) are authored approximations; no tile thickness, glaze chemistry, grout material, size standard or product is claimed. The independent kernel stores 26 spoke cosine/sine values, 672 per-triangle tones and a 96² grain, 9,914 Float64 values / 79,312 B of tables, not total RAM; each point picks the nearest of nine lattice nodes, then tests the 12 sectors with two spoke half-planes and evaluates the hexagon-edge half-plane and three smooth edges only for sectors that pass, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped. Each face is a product of three smooth half-planes inset by the grout, so neighboring supports never overlap and corners need no smooth minimum. Seeds change only triangle tone (deep teal 0.11–0.24, cream 0.80–0.92) and fine grain while the lattice stays fixed; the tone table is indexed with the lattice shift of its slanted period, but every seam lies along grout, so that index is not observable. Opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: a 768×768 raster (about 63.67 px per unit edge) is thresholded at relief-normalized height 0.41, flood-filled with periodic wrapping and 8-connectivity, and each tile is classified by its 720-ray radial corner count. Every seed yields 672 tiles (12 × 56 lattice nodes), every one with exactly three corners; areas are 0.1512–0.1626 edge² (preset-derived inset prediction 0.15632, all within 5%) and the grout fraction is 0.27946 against a predicted 0.27800 (within 0.012). The interior angles between the three detected corners are 26.23–31.10°, 58.07–63.90° and 87.71–92.62° (30°, 60° and 90° within 5°), so every tile is a 30-60-90 right triangle. Each of the 56 lattice nodes (taken from the public preset lattice) is surrounded by exactly 12 triangle centroids within 0.85 edge, at radii 0.6036–0.6342 (within 2.53% of their node mean, below 4%), consecutive angular gaps of 27.43–32.78° (alternating about 28° and 32° by mirror symmetry, inside 24–36°, each adjacent pair summing to 60° within 3°), centroid directions within 1.265° of the derived 15.9°/44.1° modulo 60° (below 4°) and colors alternating dark and light around the node. Dark triangles number 336 per seed with colors 0.1127–0.2413 (means 0.1742–0.1762, below 0.3) and light triangles 336 with 0.7987–0.9246 (means 0.8625–0.8643, above 0.7); grout roughness is 0.89307 against tile 0.32552–0.32567 (gap above 0.4), AO 0.5214 against 0.9715 (gap above 0.3) and metallic violations 0; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff move no triangle centroid (0 px by nearest-centroid pairing, below 0.5) while tone moves up to 0.1127/0.1156 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, column and node-row border lines and curvature refinement along eight lines per axis; the worst value is 0.0017941 for all three seeds (below 0.04) and the signed-UV period error is at most 1.84e-13 (below 5e-10). The 512 pixel map has grout fraction 0.2695 (0.02–0.4), grout/tile roughness 0.89975/0.326, AO 128–250, luma 78.8558–215.5428 (range above 80), maximum tilt² 0.87957 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.1642–0.1787 (above 0.02); the 32 px map has grout fraction 0.375 (0.02–0.6, because the triangles are only a few pixels wide), roughness 0.80159/0.31516, AO 128–250, luma 79.7836–214.8276 and tilt² 0.02956 (below 0.5), so only the macro star pattern survives at 32. A regression control accepted 11 legal variants (10 preset variants over palette, glaze roughness 0.22/0.42, relief 0.009/0.016, grout 0.015/0.025 and shoulder 0.01/0.02, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 20 genuine faults (9 preset faults: 0.1 grout that swallows the triangles, 0.002 grout, 0.09 shoulders, no color range, glaze as rough as the grout, unresolved or extreme relief, 5-column and 3-row stretched lattices; 11 source faults: hexagons rotated off the lattice, wrong lattice pitch, linear edge shoulders, metallic tiles, all triangles one tone, tone alternating by hexagon instead of triangle, grout as smooth as glaze, seed-moved lattice, seed-ignored tone, missing hexagon-edge half-plane, all hexagon edges facing one way). Compatibility: all 831 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,268 comparisons) and eleven related tile kinds (`truncatedtrihexagonaltiles`, `snubsquaretiles`, `rhombitrihexagonaltiles`, `elongatedtriangulartiles`, `trihexagonaltiles`, `dodecagontiles`, `cairotiles`, `righttriangletiles`, `rhombille`, `octagondot`, `windmillpavers`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (66 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged. Incidents recorded honestly: the first fixture run failed its own size-32 grout bound (0.375 against 0.3), so the bound is now 0.6 at 32 and 0.4 at 512, and a legal grout 0.03 variant that exceeded the old 512 bound (0.3776) was replaced by grout 0.025 (the 0.03 variant itself was not rerun against the final bound); 4-connected labeling split off 128 one-pixel apex fragments (0.0002 edge²) at the star centers, so labeling is 8-connected; equal-radius plateaus made 112 triangles read as four-cornered at grout 0.03, so corner peaks break ties toward the first ray; index-paired seed comparison mismatched at grout 0.015 (18.95 px from raster-order label swaps), so triangles are paired by nearest centroid; and a "row wrap without lattice shift" fault was accepted by the fixture because the tone-table wrap lies on grout along spokes and hexagon edges and is unobservable, so it is not counted as a control.

`truncatedtrihexagonaltiles` adds an authored truncated trihexagonal (4.6.12) glazed tiling: large cream regular dodecagons on a triangular lattice, a small indigo square on every lattice edge turned to one of three directions 60° apart, and a lavender regular hexagon at the center of every lattice triangle, so each vertex meets one square, one hexagon and one dodecagon; every face has a narrow bevelled edge inside rougher gray grout. It is not `dodecagontiles` (canonical 3.12.12), `trihexagonaltiles` (3.6.3.6), `rhombitrihexagonaltiles` (3.4.6.4) or the other existing tile presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT/TECHNICAL and the preset catalog for truncated trihexagonal and 4.6.12 found no preset with this vertex type. The actually read Wikipedia Truncated trihexagonal tiling page (one of the eight semiregular tilings, one square, one hexagon and one dodecagon on each vertex, Schläfli symbol tr{3,6}, a name that is misleading because an actual truncation of the trihexagonal tiling has rectangles and cannot make both hexagon and dodecagon regular, only one uniform coloring, with the kisrhombille tiling V4.6.12 as its dual) supplies the topology; the alternate-name list of the fetched page was empty, so "great rhombitrihexagonal" is only the common alternative name and not taken from that page. The geometry is derived and numerically checked rather than copied: for unit edges the dodecagon apothem is (2 + √3)/2, dodecagon centers sit on a triangular lattice of pitch 3 + √3 ≈ 4.73205 (two apothems plus one square edge), each lattice edge carries a square centered on its midpoint with its sides facing dodecagons along the edge and hexagons across it, each lattice triangle holds one hexagon at its centroid with edges alternately facing squares and dodecagons, a cell is 1 dodecagon + 3 squares + 2 hexagons of area (3 + √3)²√3/2 ≈ 19.3923, and 300,000 random points in the 7 × 4 supercell each land in exactly one polygon with both ±1 and ±2 node neighborhoods (no gaps or overlaps). The 7 columns × 4 double rows per UV tile (56 dodecagons + 168 squares + 112 hexagons, a 1.04% wider-than-tall supercell stretched onto the square UV tile, the same near-square convention as the existing 7 × 8 hexagonal tile presets), 0.03 grout per side (0.06 edge in total), 0.02 shoulder, indigo/cream palette (40,40,86 / 242,230,206), glaze roughness 0.3, grout roughness 0.92, 0.012 UV-relative relief and the 1.6 m nominal tile (edge about 0.0483 m) are authored approximations; no tile thickness, glaze chemistry, grout material, size standard or product is claimed. The independent kernel stores 12 polygon-center values, 144 edge-normal values, 336 per-tile tones and a 96² grain, 9,708 Float64 values / 77,664 B of tables, not total RAM, plus three six-entry constants; each point tests the 3 × 3 lattice-node neighborhood × 6 polygons (54 squared circumradius checks) and evaluates one smooth half-plane per edge only for polygons that can contain it, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped. Each face is a product of smooth half-planes inset by the grout, so neighboring supports never overlap and corners need no smooth minimum; tone indices wrap across the supercell with the lattice shift of its slanted period. Seeds change only tile tone (dodecagons 0.82–0.94, hexagons 0.3–0.4, squares 0.08–0.18) and fine grain while the lattice stays fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: a 1344×1344 raster (about 40.78 px per unit edge) is thresholded at relief-normalized height 0.41, flood-filled with periodic wrapping, and each tile is classified by its 720-ray radial corner count. Every seed yields 336 tiles, exactly 56 twelve-corner dodecagons, 168 four-corner squares and 112 six-corner hexagons (1:3:2 per lattice cell) and no other shapes; areas are dodecagons 10.72 edge² (preset-derived inset prediction 10.721), hexagons 2.371 (2.3637) and squares 0.8465–0.8681 (0.8464), all within 5%, and the grout fraction is 0.07044 against a predicted 0.07244 (within 0.012). Squares come in three orientation classes of 56 each with corner angles 16°, 45° and 74.5° (15°/45°/75° within 5°); dodecagon corners sit at 16° (15° within 5°), hexagon corners at 0.5° (a multiple of 60° within 5°), and each dodecagon's six nearest dodecagons are 4.732 edges away (pitch 4.7321, within 3%). Adjacency, probed by rays through the middle of every tile edge, shows all 56 dodecagons alternating square and hexagon sides over their 12 neighbors, all 112 hexagons alternating square and dodecagon sides, and all 168 squares alternating dodecagon and hexagon sides — the 4.6.12 incidence rather than a raw vertex count. Dodecagon colors are 0.8279–0.9463, hexagons 0.3079–0.4088 and squares 0.09059–0.193 (mean gaps 0.5269–0.5346 and 0.2147–0.2223, above 0.4 and 0.1), grout roughness 0.9014 against tile 0.3168–0.317 (gap above 0.4), AO 0.5147 against 0.9785 (gap above 0.3), and 0 metallic violations; seeds 7 and 0xffffffff move no tile centroid (0 px, below 0.5) while tile tone moves up to 0.1024/0.1061 (above 0.01). Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, column and node-row border lines and curvature refinement along eight lines per axis; the worst value is 0.0054501 for all three seeds (below 0.04) and the signed-UV period error is at most 7.2e-16 (below 5e-10). The 512 pixel map has grout fraction 0.07071 (0.02–0.3), grout/tile roughness 0.89191/0.31898, AO 128–250, luma 58.1728–222.1072 (range above 80), maximum tilt² 0.88043 (0.1–3) and signed direction fractions 0.062–0.0732 (above 0.02); the 32 px map keeps grout fraction 0.15625, roughness 0.92157/0.31544, AO 128–250, luma 59.1006–221.8224 and tilt² 0.02956 (below 0.5), so only the macro tiling survives at 32. A regression control accepted 11 legal variants (10 preset variants over palette, glaze roughness 0.22/0.42, relief, grout 0.02/0.045 and shoulder 0.012/0.03, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 19 genuine faults (7 preset faults: 0.5 grout that erases the squares, 0.3 shoulders, no color range, glaze as rough as the grout, unresolved or extreme relief, a 5-column stretched lattice; 12 source faults: no hexagons, no downward hexagons, no squares, all squares in one direction, wrong lattice pitch, row wrap without the lattice shift, linear edge shoulders, metallic tiles, squares as light as dodecagons, grout as smooth as glaze, seed-moved lattice, seed-ignored tone). Compatibility: all 830 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,240 comparisons) and ten related tile kinds (`snubsquaretiles`, `rhombitrihexagonaltiles`, `elongatedtriangulartiles`, `trihexagonaltiles`, `dodecagontiles`, `cairotiles`, `righttriangletiles`, `rhombille`, `octagondot`, `windmillpavers`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (60 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged and the five code catalogs stay unique with old order retained. Incident recorded honestly: the kind was first integrated as `greatrhombitrihexagonaltiles`, but the page actually read is titled Truncated trihexagonal tiling and its alternate-name list was empty, so before commit my uncommitted feature edits were reverted and redone under the verifiable name, with the fixture and the 11/19 regression control rerun and giving the same results.

`elongatedtriangulartiles` adds an authored elongated triangular (3.3.3.4.4) glazed tiling: terracotta unit-edge squares in upright rows alternate with cream rows of up and down equilateral triangles, successive square rows are offset by half an edge, and every vertex meets three triangles and two squares side by side; every face has a narrow bevelled edge inside rougher gray grout. It has the same three-triangle, two-square vertex content as `snubsquaretiles` but in a different order (there the squares are turned ±15° and never share an edge; here they are upright and share vertical edges in rows), and it is not the existing hexagon–triangle (`trihexagonaltiles`), `rhombitrihexagonaltiles` (3.4.6.4), Cairo-pentagon or right-triangle tile presets; a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT/TECHNICAL and the preset catalog for elongated triangular and 3.3.3.4.4 found no preset with this tiling. The 15 columns × 4 periods per UV tile (120 squares + 240 triangles, a 0.5% wider-than-tall tile stretched onto the square UV tile), 0.035 grout per side (0.07 edge in total), 0.02 shoulder, terracotta/cream palette (112,48,36 / 232,214,170), glaze roughness 0.34, grout roughness 0.92, 0.012 UV-relative relief and the 1.2 m nominal tile (edge 0.08 m) are authored approximations; no tile thickness, glaze chemistry, grout material, size standard or product is claimed. The independent kernel stores 12 polygon-center values, 48 edge-normal values, 360 per-tile tones and a 96² grain, 9,636 Float64 values / 77,088 B of tables, not total RAM, plus three six-entry constants; each point tests the 3 × 3 period-cell neighborhood × 6 polygons (54 squared circumradius checks) and evaluates one smooth half-plane per edge only for polygons that can contain it, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped. Each face is a product of smooth half-planes inset by the grout, so neighboring supports never overlap and corners need no smooth minimum. `snubsquaretiles` adds an authored snub square (3.3.4.3.4) glazed tiling: unit-edge squares alternately turned about +15° and −15° on a half-lattice checkerboard, with equilateral triangles filling every gap so each vertex meets three triangles and two squares; the squares are dark blue glaze, the triangles cream glaze, and every face has a narrow bevelled edge inside rougher gray grout. It is not the existing hexagon–triangle (`trihexagonaltiles`), Cairo-pentagon (`cairotiles`) or right-isosceles-triangle (`righttriangletiles`) tile presets, and a search of README/PLAN/DESIGN/CURRENT/TECHNICAL and the preset catalog for snub, 3.3.4.3.4 and Archimedean found no preset with this vertex type (the only hit was the Archimedean spiral of `cinnamonbarkcoils`). The actually read Wikipedia Snub square tiling page (a semiregular tiling with three triangles and two squares at every vertex, Schläfli symbol s{4,4}, related to the elongated triangular tiling 3.3.3.4.4) supplies the topology; the geometry is derived and numerically checked rather than copied from a source: for unit edges the square lattice constant is (1 + √3)/√2 ≈ 1.93185, squares sit on lattice nodes (turned +15°) and cell centers (turned −15°), the four outward equilateral triangles on each node square's edges complete the cell, and 200,000 random points each land in exactly one of the 2 squares + 4 triangles per cell (no gaps or overlaps, areas sum to the cell area). The 3 × 3 lattice cells per UV tile (18 squares + 36 triangles), 0.035 grout per side (0.07 edge in total), 0.02 shoulder, blue/cream palette (34,64,98 / 238,226,192), glaze roughness 0.3, grout roughness 0.92, 0.012 UV-relative relief and the 0.6 m nominal tile (edge about 0.1035 m) are authored approximations; no tile thickness, glaze chemistry, grout material, size standard or product is claimed. The independent kernel stores 12 polygon-center values, 48 edge-normal values, 54 per-tile tones and a 96² grain, 9,330 Float64 values / 74,640 B of tables, not total RAM, plus three six-entry constants; each point tests the 3 × 3 lattice-node neighborhood × 6 polygons (54 squared circumradius checks) and evaluates one smooth half-plane per edge only for polygons that can contain it, so no hypot, square root, trigonometry, hash or allocation runs per point; generic detail is skipped. Each face is a product of smooth half-planes inset by the grout, so neighboring supports never overlap and corners need no smooth minimum. Seeds change only tile tone (squares 0.1–0.22, triangles 0.78–0.92) and fine grain while the lattice stays fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or displacement.

`starfish` adds an authored five-armed sea-star approximation: most owner cells each hold one randomly rotated star made of a rounded central disc and five arms that taper from base to tip, with slightly irregular angular gaps and arm lengths, a raised dome and spine ridge along every arm, three rows of small tubercles along and beside the ridge, and a rougher darker gray-sand host between the stars. It is not Starcoral's corallite cups with radial septa, Staranise's eight woody pods around recessed seed cavities, Seaurchintest's ivory shell with paired pore rows, or the scalloped overlap family (`scalemail`, `fishscales`). The actually read Wikipedia Starfish article (a central disc with usually five arms, an aboral surface that is smooth, granular or spiny with overlapping plates, often red or orange, and a sieve-like madreporite) and the actually viewed Wikimedia Commons Starfish montage supply the shape idea; the silhouette of the orange specimen in the montage, measured with PIL from the downloaded image, gives five tips 171–183 px from the center, valleys at about 0.17–0.26 of the tip radius, arm widths of about 0.195 R at 0.5 R and 0.148 R at 0.85 R, and tip gaps of 63.5–88.5°. Other specimens in the same montage are narrower or wider (about 0.25–0.3 R for the wide horned sandy one), so these numbers describe one specimen, not the species. The 3 × 3 grid, exactly five arms, ±0.1 rad axis jitter, ±6% length jitter, 0.4 cell radius, 0.25 R disc, base/tip half-widths 0.1 R / 0.07 R, tubercle rows (pitch 0.05 cell, radius 0.017), gray-sand host, gray-to-orange palette, roughness 0.66, 0.02 UV-relative relief and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored approximations: no species, madreporite, tube feet, spines, color calibration, real size or marine-biology data is claimed. The independent kernel stores 180 pose Float64 values (9 owners × 20) plus a 128² grain and a 16² host field, 16,820 Float64 values / 134,560 B of tables, not total RAM; each point picks the arm with the largest projection (no angle trigonometry), uses two hypot calls and twelve SmoothStep calls, and has no per-point allocation, hash or trigonometry (`cos`/`sin` only while building poses); generic detail is skipped. Arm width tapers with a smoothstep so the slope vanishes at the tip and base; arm-owned relief fades in only beyond 0.2 R–0.25 R from the center so the fold line where neighboring arms hand over shows no relief kink; disc and arms combine as `1 − (1 − arm)(1 − disc)`. Seeds change which owners hold a star, plus rotation, arm jitter, tone and fine grain; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency or real arm geometry.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: a 576×576 raster with 192 px cells, a 0.15 height-threshold star mask and 720 rays from each star centroid locate every star's tips, gaps, valleys, widths and tubercles. Each seed has 9/9/8 detected stars (above 0.75 × 9 − 1 and at most 9), each with exactly 5 tips; angular gaps are 62–82° (55–92°), tip radii 0.388–0.4766 cell (0.3–0.5), tip max/min 1.025–1.124 (below 1.25), valley/tip radius 0.1881–0.2216 (0.12–0.3), star area 0.113–0.1389 of its cell (0.08–0.2), and orientation concentration 0.247–0.406 (below 0.75), so rotation is random rather than fixed. Arm full width relative to tip radius is 0.1349–0.1693 at half radius (per-star mean 0.1–0.22) and 0.1112–0.1408 at 0.85 radius (above 0.09 and below the half-radius mean); the viewed orange specimen measured about 0.195 and 0.148, so this preset is slimmer. Spine tubercles number 4–8 per arm (each arm above 0, each star above 12 in total). Star coverage is 0.1111–0.1289 (0.07–0.2), star/host color gap 0.378–0.422 (above 0.3), roughness gap 0.277–0.279 (above 0.2) and AO gap 0.166–0.168 (above 0.12), with 0 metallic/mortar violations. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, cell-border lines and curvature refinement along eight lines per axis; the worst value is 0.00010103/0.00008106/0.00011772 (below 0.04) and signed-UV period errors are at most 7.2e-15 (below 5e-10). The 512 pixel map has a star fraction of 0.12016 (0.07–0.2), star/host roughness 0.65736/0.93924, AO 156–255, luma 98.0166–147.3082, maximum tilt² 0.86087 (0.1–3) and every signed direction fraction 0.0688–0.0697 (above 0.02); the 32 px map keeps a face fraction of 0.12207, AO 156–254, luma 98.7318–147.3082 and tilt² 0.06807 (below 0.4), so only macro arms and shading survive at 32. A regression control accepted 29 legal variants (28 preset variants over palette, finish, relief, cells, star and disc radius, arm widths, arm/length/center jitter, shoulders, ridge, tubercles and chance, plus a quintic-smoothstep source variant) and rejected 22 genuine faults (14 preset faults: fat, hair-thin or outward-widening arms, huge disc, owner-clipped, tiny or sparse stars, tangled arms, very unequal arms, no tubercles, no color range, mirror finish, unresolved or extreme relief; 8 source faults: disc only, fixed orientation, metallic stars, linear shoulders, unfaded arm relief, star roughness equal to the host, no tubercle relief, inverted dome). Compatibility: all 826 old kinds × four seeds × seven points (23,128 comparisons) and ten related kinds (`starcoral`, `staranise`, `seaurchintest`, `scalemail`, `fishscales`, `cowrieshells`, `musselshells`, `scallopshell`, `oystershell`, `nautilusshell`) × sizes 32/512 × three seeds (60 map sets) are byte-identical to the previous build; presets, tiles and limits of old kinds are unchanged and the seven catalogs stay unique with old order retained. Incidents recorded honestly: the first draft used a linear taper, and a legal 0.56 roughness variant exposed a 0.155 slope kink at an arm tip (default roughness stayed below 0.04, so the default fixture alone would not have caught it), which the smoothstep taper fixed; the first legal 0.74 roughness variant was too close to the host (gap 0.19967, below 0.2) and was replaced by 0.72; per-arm tubercle counts ranged from 2 to 11 across legal variants, so only a loose total bound is asserted, and a 0.2-amplitude grain-speckle source fault plus the reintroduced linear-taper kink remain undetected by this fixture.

`fishscaleshingles` adds an authored fish-scale metal shingle approximation: eight courses of twelve semicircular lower-edge lobes, each shingle two lobes wide, alternate courses staggered by half a lobe, upper courses overlapping lower ones with an under-lap shadow, and narrow dark seams between slightly different painted shingles. It is not Hopsack/Waffleweave cloth cells, Slate/Tiles rectangular tiles, or Snowflaketiles/Circularpavers geometric paving. The actually read Berridge Fish Scale Shingles page (24-gauge steel, lightly textured rounded scalloped profile, each shingle covering 8 1/2 in tall by 11 1/2 in wide, 148 per square; 8.5 × 11.5 × 148 = 14,467 in², roughly consistent with 100 ft² = 14,400 in² (about 0.5% apart)) and two actually viewed white/beige product images (two semicircular lobes along each shingle's lower edge, neighboring courses offset and overlapping, faint wavy embossing) supply the geometry; the Yusheng fish-scale stone-coated tile page (small overlapping scalloped unit, about 2.8 tiles per m²) was read but none of its numbers are used. The Berridge coverage ratio gives a course-height to lobe-width ratio of 2 × 8.5 / 11.5 ≈ 1.478 for two lobes per shingle; this material's 12 lobes × 8 courses give 1.5 (about 1.5% away) and uses 12 × 5.75 in ≈ 1.75 m as the nominal tile. The sources and images give no readable course offset, lip thickness, shadow width, seam width, paint color or per-shingle tone difference, so the half-lobe stagger, lip, shadow, seam and palette values are authored approximations; no embossing, metallic reflection, steel bending, fasteners, specification certification or wood shingle is claimed. The independent kernel has only a 48-entry shingle tone table (8 × 6) and a 128² grain, 16,432 Float64 values / 131,456 B of tables, not total RAM; each point uses four hypot calls and twelve SmoothStep calls, merges the two nearest lobe distances with a polynomial smooth minimum (avoiding a slope crease along the distance-field medial axis), and has no per-point allocation, hash or trigonometry; generic detail is skipped. Each course computes its own color, height and AO before coverage blends them, so a seam's tone step stays hidden under the seam color instead of leaving a jump. The 0.012 UV-relative relief and palette are authored approximations; seeds change only shingle tone and fine grain while lobes, seams and courses stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency, refraction or real overlap geometry. It belongs to the same scalloped-overlap family as the existing `scallopedslate` (4 columns × 6 rows, 1.2 m tile, one rounded tail per blue-grey slate tile, no seams between tiles), `fishscaletiles` (4 columns × 8 rows of coplanar glazed mosaic) and `scalemail`, so treat it as a variant derived from the Berridge coverage ratio — 12 lobes × 8 courses, two lobes per shingle, narrow seams with painted tone differences, a 1.75 m tile and under-lap shadows — rather than a new roof-tile class.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: a 576×576 raster with 48 px lobes, shifted by half a course so boundaries stay inside it, locates each course's lower edge from height steps and then measures lobes, semicircularity, course pitch, stagger and seams. The preset must have 8–16 lobes and 6–10 courses; each seed has 8 courses of exactly 12 lobes (equal to the preset), lobe spacing spread 0 px (below 3), depth/lobe-width 0.5 (0.42–0.58), semicircle residual RMS 0.018803–0.018926 radius (below 0.06), and step-detection failure columns of 0 for the standard preset (below 15%; soft cusp columns are interpolated circularly). Course pitch is 71.992–72.007 px (within 72 ± 2) and neighboring-course lobe offset is 24 px (within half a lobe, 24 ± 3). Each course has 6 seams (equal to lobes/2), seam spacing spread 0 px (below 3), seam/face color drop 0.26329–0.32178 (above 0.15), neighboring-course seam offset 24 px (24 ± 3), and per-shingle mean-color deviation 0.02679–0.02943 (0.01–0.08). Minimum AO under the upper edge is 0.55392 (below 0.7), calm AO is 1 (above 0.9), roughness is 0.5–0.53 (0.45–0.58), and metallic/mortar violations are 0. Seeds 0 and 7 differ by 0 px in lobe and seam positions (below 2) and by up to 0.09055 in shingle color (above 0.01), so only tone and grain move. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, vertical lobe/seam lines, horizontal course/cusp lines and 4096 signed UV samples: worst is 0.000027756 for all seeds, below 0.04, with signed period at most 3.0087e-14. Actual 512 has face/backing roughness 0.51501/0.51507, AO 71–255, luma 144.33–185.83, max tilt² 0.41415 and signed normal fractions 0.053974/0.054024/0.063618/0.0072136; 32 px has AO 144–255, luma 169.83–185.76 and tilt² 0.0037216, retaining only macro shading and coarse normals. Thirty-one valid variants — cool/warm palettes, two roughness values, two reliefs, 10×6/14×8 lobes×courses, sharp/soft shoulders, short/long ramp, low/high base, low/high lip, light/dark shadow, narrow/wide shadow, narrow/wide seams, shallow/deep seams, weak/strong tone spread, light/dark seam color, weak/strong seam AO and quintic shoulders — pass all 18 cases. Twenty-two real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: absent/faint lip, coarse/fine lattice, no seams, absent/excessive tone spread, no shadow, near-black palette, no color range, mirror finish, unresolved/extreme relief, no stagger, seams without grooves, linear shoulders, metallic shingles, upward steps, no height ramp, diamond lobes, seed-moved lobes and noisy roughness; no color range is rejected only because the pixel observer yields NaN (not an independent diagnostic), extreme relief by the 32 px coarse-normal bound, mirror finish and noisy roughness by the roughness range and the near-black palette by the luma spread. Limits are in ACCEPTANCE.

`waffleweave` adds an authored waffle-weave cloth approximation: rounded float ridges on a fixed 14×16 lattice enclose recessed square pockets with shallow bowl floors, weft-direction (horizontal) ridges stand higher than warp-direction (vertical) ridges, and the two ridge directions rise into small knots where they cross. It is not Matelasse's raised quilted diamonds, Basketweave/Hopsack continuous basket floats, or Honeycomb's golden hexagonal comb. The actually read Wikipedia Waffle fabric (also called honeycomb fabric; long warp and weft floats around plain-weave centers form square ridges and hollows), Ashford's "The Squish is real" (long floats interlock on a grid, ridges outline the cells, pockets are the tighter interlacing, finishing puffs the floats) and LinenMe's waffle-towel guide (recessed cells and raised ridges; new cloth is flatter and washing makes the structure more pronounced), plus the actually viewed Wikimedia Commons "An example of waffle fabric" close-up (stronger horizontal ridges, rounded knots at crossings, hollow cells), are the sources; the Ashford and LinenMe page images were viewed but showed only a loom and hanging towels with no readable structure, so they are not appearance evidence. None gives cell sizes, ridge heights or warp/weft ridge ratios, so the 14×16 cells (about 8.6×7.5 mm on the 0.12 m tile), pocket width, 0.9/0.7 weft/warp ridge heights, bowl depth and knot strength are authored approximations; "horizontal ridges stronger" is one photograph's observation, not a fabric specification. No real warp/weft interlacement, weave draft, cloth physics, absorbency or cotton/linen/microfibre specification is claimed. The independent kernel has no per-cell table: only a 128² grain and 8² cloud, 16,448 Float64 values / 131,584 B of tables, not total RAM; each point uses two fract/abs reductions and at most four SmoothStep calls, with no allocation, hash, trigonometry or square root, and generic detail is skipped. The 0.12 m nominal tile, 0.012 UV-relative relief and cool grey-white palette are authored approximations; seeds move only fine grain and cloud tone while the lattice and ridge positions stay fixed; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparent holes, cloth simulation, real knit/woven structure or specification certification. It belongs to the same fabric family as the existing `wafflecloth` (8×8 symmetric raised rims; measured warp and weft crests differ by only about 0.6% and crossings are no higher than the crests), so treat it as a finer 14×16 variant rather than a new fabric class: here weft crests stand about 0.08 relief units above warp crests, pockets are bowl-shaped, each crossing adds a knot about 0.10 units above the weft crest, and the references are different.

Five behaviors use the actual sampler on three seeds without copying private parameters: a 896×1024 raster with 64 px cells yields each pocket mask, while pocket centers, vertical crests, horizontal crests and crossings are sampled exactly. Each seed must contain 224 cells (14×16; the preset must have 10–20 columns and 12–20 rows), pocket area of 0.25–0.45 of a cell (measured 0.34619–0.35059, cross-cell spread at most 0.00415 and required below 0.02), centroid offset below 0.02 cell (maximum 0.0021735), box width 0.5–0.8 (0.65625) and height 0.5–0.75 (0.59375), width/height 0.9–1.3 (1.1053), area/box fill above 0.75 (0.88847–0.89975; a circular fault measured 0.711–0.715), and edge-position spread below 0.1 cell (0.015625, one raster step). Each height class has cross-cell spread below 0.02 (0.003885–0.003966): pocket floor 0.1–0.25 (0.18005–0.18395), vertical crest above floor by more than 0.25 (0.31608–0.31612), horizontal crest above vertical by more than 0.05 (0.076033–0.076119), and crossing knot above horizontal by more than 0.07 (0.094304–0.094401) and below 0.8 (maximum 0.68218). Crossing/horizontal color gaps over the floor exceed 0.25/0.2 (0.30834–0.36058/0.2663–0.31154), AO gap exceeds 0.3 (0.49824), roughness is 0.78–0.97 (0.88–0.90996), and metallic/mortar violations are 0. Seeds 0 and 7 differ in only 0.002582 of pocket-mask pixels (below 0.005) with mean height difference 0.00097172 (between 1e-5 and 0.02), so only grain moves while the lattice stays fixed. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized observed-curvature C1 includes a 128×128 grid, vertical/horizontal cell boundaries, pocket-edge scan lines and 4096 signed UV samples: worst is 0.000007228 for all three seeds, below 0.04, with signed period at most 2.2407e-15. Actual 512 has ridge-brightness fraction 0.46283, face/backing roughness 0.89516/0.89486 (difference below 0.05), AO 128–254, luma 185.787–231.711, max tilt² 0.098577 and signed normal fractions 0.26265/0.26175/0.36829/0.36762; 32 px has fraction 0.30469, AO 150–222, luma 190.50–219.57 (spread 29.07, above 20) and tilt² 0.00076894, retaining only macro shading and coarse normals. Twenty-three valid variants — cool/warm palettes, two roughness values, two reliefs, 12×14/16×18 lattices, narrow/wide pockets, low/high vertical crests, low/high horizontal crests, low/high floors, shallow/deep weave, shallow/deep bowls, weak/strong knots and quintic shoulders — pass all 15 cases. Twenty-seven real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: absent/faint ridges, tiny/huge pockets, vertical crest as high as or above horizontal, knot below crest, coarse/fine lattice, black palette, no color range, mirror finish, unresolved/extreme relief, high floor, circular pockets, sheared lattice, linear shoulders, metallic ridges, ribs only, per-cell height steps, inverted waffle, strong grain height, seed-moved lattice, noisy roughness, no pocket AO and dark ridges; circular pockets are rejected by area 0.2256 rather than fill, per-cell steps and inverted waffle by area, the seed-moved lattice by the cell-box checks (the separate cross-seed case is not proven independently) and extreme relief by the 32 px coarse-normal bound, not by independent diagnostics. Limits are in ACCEPTANCE.

`halite` adds an authored milky cube hopper-face approximation: most owners carry one flush, randomly rotated square cube face with two concentric square terraces stepping down inside it, like the stepped hollows of a hopper crystal; the face is milky and low-roughness on a rough pale grey-pink salt host. It is not Calcite's 75-degree oblique plates, Celestine/Barite rectangular plates, Wulfenite near-square plates, or an unstepped flat square. The actually read Handbook of Mineralogy (isometric, perfect {001} cleavage, skeletal/hopper-shaped faces, colorless or white when pure) and Minerals.net (cubes sometimes distorted with hopper growths), plus its actually viewed pink hopper cluster and white Death Valley cube cluster photographs, give no readable terrace ratio or depth numbers; the face radius, terrace radii of about 0.74/0.44 of the face half-size (each ±0.06) and the 0.08 height-unit drop per terrace are therefore authored approximations, with no measured or certified salt-crystal dimensions, transparency, dissolution physics or mineral identification. The independent kernel stores 9 pose/terrace values for each of 16 seeded owners plus a 128² grain and 16² host table: 16,784 Float64 values / 134,272 B of tables, not total RAM. The largest square face support including jitter is about 0.4455, below the 0.5 owner boundary; each point uses one rotation and at most six SmoothStep calls, with no allocation, hash, trigonometry or square root, and generic detail is skipped. The 0.08 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief and palette are authored approximations; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency, refraction, lattice, dissolution simulation or chemical certification. It belongs to the same rotated nested-square hopper family as the existing `bismuthhoppers` (4×4 rotated square faces, six metal terraces, gold-violet, 0.16 m tile); this is only a white dielectric salt variant with two terraces, smaller face half-widths of 0.21–0.27 (versus 0.34), a 0.08 m tile and a rough salt host, not a new crystal class.

Five behaviors use the actual 512² sampler on three seeds without copying private poses: each owner yields an outer-face mask, then a first-terrace mask below height 0.52 and a second-terrace mask below 0.44, checked with centroid-ray corner lobes, four straight-line edge fits and concentricity. Each seed must contain 10–16 faces (measured 16/15/15); the outer face and first terrace each need four lobes, a longest/shortest corner-radius ratio below 1.08 (outer 1–1.0205, first terrace 1.0072–1.0397), four edge-line angles of 84–96 degrees (86.691–90), line RMS below 0.006 cell (maximum 0.0024625), opposite-edge parallel error below 5 degrees (maximum 3.3059), center-symmetry error below 0.06 (maximum 0.039139), and face area of 0.13–0.32 owner (0.16852–0.27765). The first terrace covers 0.4–0.75 of the face (0.48494–0.66324), the second 0.12–0.32 (0.15423–0.25484), with a difference above 0.15 (0.23393–0.49724); centroid offsets are below 0.02/0.04 cell (maximum 0.0039029/0.018096), and the first-terrace turn differs from the outer face by under 5 degrees (maximum 2). Rim/first/lowest heights are about 0.56/0.48/0.40 (0.56087–0.56162/0.48163–0.48246/0.39625–0.39961), with each step down exceeding 0.06 (0.078712–0.079776, 0.082398–0.085779). The lowest terrace is small enough that measured outlines once showed five lobes, a corner-radius ratio up to 1.209 and a turn up to 7 degrees, so only its area, concentricity and height are asserted, not edge straightness or turn (see ACCEPTANCE). Whole-tile coverage is 0.12–0.32 (0.18969–0.23801), face/host color gap exceeds 0.3 (0.40094–0.40647), roughness gap exceeds 0.4 (0.48861–0.48981), AO gap exceeds 0.2 (0.27271–0.27608), face roughness is 0.3–0.55 (0.43649–0.43709), metallic/mortar violations are 0, and random-turn concentration is below 0.75 (0.16348–0.38433). Seventeen valid variants — cool/warm palettes, two roughness values, two reliefs, small/large faces, shallow/deep terraces (0.07/0.095), narrow/wide first terrace (0.71/0.78), small/large second terrace (0.42/0.47), low/high coverage and quintic shoulders — pass all 14 cases. Twenty-six real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: absent/shallow/excessive terrace depth, tiny/owner-clipped/sparse faces, huge first terrace, tiny terraces, second terrace as large as the first, black palette, no color range, same roughness, mirror finish, unresolved/extreme relief, circular faces, oblique rhomb faces, fixed orientation, metallic faces, C0 host step, linear shoulders, smooth host, nonconcentric lowest terrace, 45-degree-rotated first terrace, face height speckle and inverted terraces; circular faces are rejected by lobe count 14≠4, extreme relief by the 32 px coarse-normal bound and the nonconcentric floor by edge RMS 0.006625, not by independent diagnostics. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 worst is 0.0000711/0.0000455/0.0000467 below 0.04, with signed period at most 2.6645e-15. Actual 512 has face fraction 0.1885, face/backing roughness 0.43539/0.92481, AO 153–252, max tilt² 0.28349 and signed normal fractions 0.022064/0.022057/0.021996/0.022015; 32 px keeps only macro color and coarse normals (tilt² 0.0015071). Limits are in ACCEPTANCE.

`calcite` adds an authored milky oblique cleavage-plate approximation: most owners carry one flush rhomb-shaped plate whose two edge pairs meet at about 75 degrees, with a parallel nested step plate slightly off center; the plate is milky and low-roughness on a rough dark brown mineral host. It is not Celestine/Barite rectangular plates, Wulfenite near-square plates, or Pyromorphite/Vanadinite hexagonal ends. The 75-degree angle is authored: the actually read Handbook of Mineralogy (perfect {1011} cleavage), Wikipedia and LibreTexts (rhombohedral cleavage, commonly white cleavage fragments) and the Minerals.net transparent Iceland spar photograph provide no readable face-angle value, so no measured or certified cleavage angle, crystal optics, transparency or birefringence is claimed. The independent kernel stores 10 pose/step values for each of 16 seeded owners plus a 128² grain and 16² host table: 16,800 Float64 values / 134,400 B of tables, not total RAM. The largest plate support including jitter is about 0.4692, below the 0.5 owner boundary; each point uses one rotation, one oblique conversion and at most four SmoothStep calls, with no allocation, hash, trigonometry or square root, and generic detail is skipped. The 0.1 m nominal tile, 0.0035 UV-relative relief and palette are authored approximations; opaque dielectric four maps, default metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership stay unchanged, without added meshes, transparency, refraction, lattice or chemical certification.

Five behaviors use the actual 512² sampler on three seeds without copying private poses: each owner mask yields corner lobes from centroid rays, four straight-line edge fits, then the outer plate and nested step are checked. Each seed must contain 10–16 plates with four lobes each, a long/short corner-radius ratio of 1.22–1.38 (measured 1.2808–1.3266; about 1.303 for 75 degrees), four edge-line angles of 72–78 degrees (73.824–75.717), line RMS below 0.006 cell (maximum 0.002428), opposite-edge parallel error below 3 degrees (maximum 1.2788), center-symmetry error below 0.03 (maximum 0.016793), and plate area of 0.12–0.3 owner (0.16431–0.24902). The nested step covers 0.12–0.55 of the plate (0.20323–0.45133), has shape ratio 0.9–1.1 (0.95963–1.0311), axis difference below 4 degrees (maximum 2.2677), stays fully inside and rises 0.05–0.09 relief units above the plate (0.067794–0.069066). Whole-tile coverage is 0.12–0.3 (0.15759–0.19664), plate/host color gap exceeds 0.5 (0.66433–0.67151), roughness gap exceeds 0.4 (0.5385–0.53955), AO gap exceeds 0.3 (0.41917–0.41946), plate roughness is 0.25–0.5 (0.37055–0.37081), metallic/mortar violations are 0, and random-turn concentration is below 0.75 (0.28922–0.36418). Seventeen valid variants — cool/warm palettes, two roughness values, two reliefs, 74/76 degrees, small/large plates, low/high step rise, low/high coverage, small/large steps and quintic shoulders — pass all 14 cases. Twenty-six real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: 90/70/80 degree angles, tiny/owner-clipped plates, sparse plates, absent/excessive step rise, tiny/filling/escaping steps, black palette, no color range, same roughness, mirror finish, absent/extreme relief, rectangular plates, circular plates, fixed orientation, metallic plates, C0 host step, linear shoulders, smooth host, axis-aligned square step and plate height speckle; circular plates are rejected by lobe count and extreme relief by the 32 px coarse-normal bound, not by independent diagnostics. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 worst is 0.000110/0.0000905/0.000106 below 0.04, with signed period at most 1.6653e-16. Actual 512 has face fraction 0.16197, face/backing roughness 0.37486/0.90829, AO 140–250, max tilt² 0.2018 and signed normal fractions 0.01513/0.01529/0.01382/0.01378; 32 px keeps only macro color and coarse normals (tilt² 0.0015). Limits are in ACCEPTANCE.

`flangenuts` adds an authored top-view approximation of steel hexagonal flange nuts: a trimmed six-flat hex body stands on a lower circular conical flange with an open central bore revealing rougher dark steel backing; it is neither flangeless Hex Nuts nor the closed dome of Cap Nuts. Proportions follow only the DIN 6923 M5–M20 table and drawing trend: flange diameter dc is about 1.38–1.48 across-flats s, minimum across-corners e is about 1.10–1.115 s, minimum bore da is about 0.60–0.67 s, and the drawing shows a 15–30 degree flange face; this material uses a flange/flat ratio near 1.40 and a bore/flat ratio near 0.68. Sixteen seeded owners cache six plane normals; 16×12 plane values plus 96² grain use 9,408 Float64 elements / 75,264 table bytes, not total RAM. The 0.413 flange radius stays inside the 0.5 owner; each point uses six smooth plane products, one hypot and a few SmoothStep calls, with no allocation, hash, trigonometry or neighboring-cell scan, and generic detail is skipped. The 0.08 m nominal tile follows Hex Nuts; the 0.03 UV-relative relief and palette are authored approximations. The whole tile including dark steel backing is metallic 1, the root-factory default is 1, and explicit factor 0 does not rewrite maps. It does not include underside serrations, full 3D nuts, internal threads, transparency, steel hardness, corrosion data or DIN/ISO certification.

Eight behaviors use the actual sampler on each seed’s 16 owners without copying private planes: 720-ray bisection first finds the mask’s flange edge and bore edge, then a height isocontour finds the hex-body outline. It requires six corner lobes, about 60-degree spacing, a 1.05–1.15 corner/flat ratio, flat-edge projection spread below 0.006, near-circular flange and bore (max/min below 1.03), a minimum flange radius 1.25–1.6 times the flat radius and at least 1.1 times the corner radius, a bore of 0.45–0.85 flat radius whose floor is within 0.02 of backing, a hex top 0.2–0.5 above the flange rim, a flange rim 0.15–0.4 above backing, a 0.03–0.15 cone rise, and bounded wall AO, backing roughness/color separation and random-orientation concentration. Twenty-one valid variants — cool/warm steel palettes, two roughness values, two reliefs, larger/smaller nuts, two flange ratios, two bore sizes, two cone heights, two hex and flange heights, two wall-AO strengths and a quintic flange shoulder — pass all eight cases. Twenty-eight real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: flange hugging the hex corners, flange smaller than the hex, owner-clipped flange, closed/oversized bore, no height step, flange as tall as hex, no/steep cone, no wall AO, no backing roughness/color separation, black palette, absent/extreme relief, tiny nut, height speckle, over-clipped octagon corners, pentagon/octagon body, square/oval flange, oval bore, nonmetal, C0 grain, linear bevel, fixed orientation and missing hex body. `capnuts` adds an authored top-view approximation of steel hexagonal cap nuts: six straight flats on a lightly trimmed hex body, a closed circular dome and rougher dark steel backing; it is not the through-bored Hex Nuts material. Proportions follow only the DIN 1587 table trend: dome diameter dk is about 0.93–0.96 of across-flats s, minimum across-corners e is about 1.106–1.113 s, and a lower 30-degree chamfer ring approximates the corners. Sixteen seeded owners cache six plane normals in the constructor; 16×12 plane values plus 96² grain use 9,408 Float64 elements / 75,264 table bytes, not total RAM. The 0.421 corner trim radius stays inside the 0.5 owner; each point uses six smooth plane products, one hypot and a few squares/SmoothStep calls, with no allocation, hash, trigonometry or neighboring-cell scan, and generic detail is skipped. The 0.08 m nominal tile follows Hex Nuts; the 0.03 UV-relative relief, dome crown and palette are authored approximations, not real nut dimensions, threads, corrosion or material certification. The whole tile including dark steel backing is metallic 1, the root-factory default is 1, and explicit factor 0 does not rewrite maps. It does not include full 3D nuts, internal threads, transparency, steel hardness, DIN/ISO certification or measured steel data.

Eight behaviors use the actual sampler on each seed’s 16 owners: the dark-backing mask centroid and 720 bisected true-contour rays require six corner lobes, about 60-degree spacing, a 1.05–1.15 corner/flat ratio and flat-edge projection spread below 0.006, without copying private planes. The dome must be closed, descend monotonically from the center in every direction, have a near-circular half-height isocontour at 0.6–0.85 of the flat radius, a rim at about 0.88–1.0 of the flat radius, stand 0.35–0.55 above the hex top, and the hex top must stand 0.35–0.55 above backing; corner chamfer drop, neck AO, backing roughness/color separation and random-orientation concentration are also bounded. Nineteen valid variants — cool/warm steel palettes, two roughness values, two reliefs, larger/smaller nuts, two dome ratios, two crown heights, tighter/wider and unclipped corners, a true spherical cap and quintic shoulder — pass all eight cases. Twenty-seven real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: no/tiny/oversized dome, over-clipped octagon corners, no/excessive chamfer, hex top collapsed to backing, over-tall dome, no neck AO, no roughness/color separation, black palette, absent/extreme relief, tiny or owner-clipped giant nuts, height speckle, pentagon/octagon, through bore, hex-shaped/oval dome, nonmetal, C0 grain, linear bevel, fixed orientation and pointed dome. `eudialyte` approximates interlocking angular dark-raspberry fragments, black matrix and fine dark intergrain contacts in a selected cabochon. No false parallel crystal ribs are added: fragments and matrix share one fine-micrograin polished plane with AO 1 / M0 / mortar 0 / factor 0, without carving intergrain contacts into cavities. No transparent hole, geometry/backside, screw/assembly, standardized angle, load/torque/pull-through performance or electrical-insulation safety is added or certified.

`makore` approximates a selected reddish-brown mottled/curly Makore veneer: fine longitudinal grain carries transverse curls of locally varying, fading strength and sparse relatively wider short recessed longitudinal vessels—not uniform washboard stripes, straight zebrawood streaks, cream-gold Anigre or an endgrain pore diagram. It reuses the Anigre synthesizer and old arithmetic order; only the new kind adds a 5×9 C1 figure gate. Twenty-two integer-period curls change pigment, not height, roughness or AO; only vessels genuinely recess. The authored 0.18 m nominal tile retains four-value pores over 28×18 owners plus 3×5 warp, 96×4 fiber, 128² grain, 5² cloud and 5×9 figure: 18,869 Float64 values / 150,952 bytes of tables, not total RAM. Seed data is cached in the constructor; points allocate nothing and use no hashes, trigonometry, square roots or neighbor searches; generic detail is bypassed. Maximum pore half-width 0.04 / half-length 0.16 stay inside each owner, and the conservative main-axis curl derivative bound is 10.75 > 0. Opaque dielectric metallic-zero maps, optional height, tint/Worker/cache/repeats and ownership remain unchanged; UV relief is not metre-valued geometry displacement. Not all Makore is claimed curly; no photographs, directional optical sheen, fiber geometry, anatomical simulation or species, physical pore density, finishing/aging, mechanical or safety certification is supplied.

`anigre` approximates a selected light golden-pink figured Anigre veneer: irregular transverse curl bands cross fine longitudinal fibers and sparse open vessels—not zebrawood dark longitudinal streaks, birdseye knots, an endgrain diagram or raised corrugations. The 0.16 m tile uses 24 integer-period curl phases with seeded warp and the existing C1 smooth periodic-profile convention. Curl changes pigment only, not height, roughness or AO; only open vessels recess. Four-value pores over 32×16 sites, 3×5 warp, 96×4 fiber, 5² cloud and 128² grain retain 18,856 Float64 values / 150,848 bytes. Point sampling allocates nothing, hashes nothing, uses no sqrt/trig or neighboring-site scan, and bypasses shared detail. Pore support vanishes inside each owner; the conservative phase-axis derivative lower bound is 15 > 0. Opaque dielectric maps, metallic 0 / mortar 0 and existing tint, worker, cache, optional height, repeats and ownership remain unchanged. This is an appearance approximation, not a guarantee that every Anigre board is figured, species identification, a scanned section, a directional optical shader, rippled geometry or durability/mechanical/safety certification; UV relief is not meter-unit geometry displacement.

`adzukibeans` approximates red adzuki seeds (Vigna angularis) with burgundy-to-russet coats, one long central cream hilum and an intact convex face—not flattened lentils, an apical castor caruncle or an open split. A 0.05 m tile has 25 seeded rotated oval seeds. A thin round-ended capsule changes hilum pigment only: it neither raises nor engraves height and does not cut an AO hole. Five-value poses, a 5×7 coat field and 128² grain retain 16,544 Float64 values / 132,352 bytes. Squared-ellipse and squared-capsule smooth shoulders reuse the existing C1 convention; point sampling allocates nothing, hashes nothing, uses no sqrt/trig and bypasses shared detail. The maximum rotated support is 0.28 + 0.035 jitter < 0.5; the conservative hilum q bound is about 0.291 < the 0.88 full-body boundary, keeping the scar inside one coat and owner. Coat tones, cream scar, fine grain and backing use opaque dielectric maps / optional height with default metallic 0 and unchanged tint, worker, cache, repeats and ownership. The 5.6×4.4 mm outline is a tile-reference scale only; UV height is not meter-unit geometry displacement. This stylized outward-facing seed per cell is not a scanned cultivar, packed seed geometry, internal cotyledons, SEM microcracks or food/optical simulation.

`amazonite` approximates a polished aqua feldspar face with broken intersecting pale streaks and fine cloud variation—not circular larimar pools, a complete grid, recessed cracks, raised threads or transparent crystals. Two integer UV phases run along (32,8) / (−8,32), reusing existing band/cached-field and C1 smooth-shoulder conventions. Finer seeded warp, variable widths and gates break regular long stripes; bounded product union smooths crossings. The 5² cloud, 7×9/9×7 warp, 32×16/16×32 widths, 8×32/32×8 gates and 128² grain cache 18,071 Float64 values / 144,568 B once. No per-point allocation, hashing, trigonometry or square roots; needsDetail bypass remains. Maximum phase support 0.1485 is below wrap half-width 0.5; the signed shoulder equation has a positive primary-axis derivative bound 19.898. Every phase is opaque M0/mortar0/AO1, with pigment-only streaks on one plane. The theoretical grain-height span 0.000002 UV corresponds to 0.12 μm at the 0.06 m reference tile / 0.001 UV relief, not measured lattice detail or displacement geometry. No optical twinning, cleavage fracture, geological or healing simulation. Existing options/tint/Worker/cache/ownership remain unchanged.

Tatami (`tatami`) has yellow-green rush ridges, recessed gaps, transverse bindings alternating over and under neighboring reeds, and fine longitudinal fibers. Its four seeded periodic maps remain opaque dielectric with metallic 0; one UV tile represents 0.16 m. This is surface shading/normal mapping only, not reed geometry, transparent openings or physics; existing options, repeats and ownership are unchanged.

Fruit-rind surfaces include pineapple with golden/olive diamond-like polygonal eyes in diagonal staggered rows, narrow brown-green recessed seams and a recessed central eye within a rounded crown; strawberry with red skin, irregularly staggered elongated recessed pockets and small ochre seeds inside them; and lychee with pink/red densely packed irregular polygonal raised tubercles, softened pointed crowns and narrow dark recessed fissures. These are distinct from overlapping pinecone scales, round orange-peel glands and orderly pineapple eyes, respectively. Relief is shading/normal mapping only: no geometry, displacement, transparency, subsurface scattering (SSS), transmission or new BRDF. Existing options, physical repeats, caller ownership and borrowed-map lifetimes are unchanged.

Bulk-grain presets include rice with slender ivory kernels, varied orientations and gentle longitudinal relief; sesame with small warm tan asymmetric teardrop seeds, rounded raised keels and tapered tips; and coffeebeans with broader dark roasted-brown oval beans, curved central splits and fine uneven roasting grain. These are stylized surface-shading/normal-map textures, not individually simulated grains, physical stacking, geometry, displacement, transparency or subsurface scattering.

The caller owns the returned preset, whose readonly `kind`, `material: PBRMaterial` and `textures` expose four `Texture` sources: `baseColor` (sRGB RGB), `normal` (linear tangent-space), `metallicRoughness` (linear G roughness/B metallic) and `occlusion` (linear R). Defaults are opaque, repeat sampling for all slots, roughness factor 1 and metallic factor 1 for presets with authored metal regions (including fully metallic nickelsilver and mixed-metallic rust or copperpatina), preserving the B channel; pure dielectric presets use factor 0. See the individual kind descriptions for the complete contract. Rust's metallic channel varies between remaining metal and corrosion; chainmail's varies between metallic rings and opaque dielectric backing. `createMaterial(options?: Partial<PBRMaterialOptions>)` creates a fresh material borrowing its maps, with caller overrides applied last.

Pavement presets are opaque dielectrics: asphalt has dark granular binder with embedded aggregate, gravel has irregular pebbles and dark recesses, and cobblestone has staggered rounded paving blocks.

Natural-surface presets are also opaque dielectrics using the same four maps: bark has ridges and deep fissures, moss has dense soft green growth, and mud has earthy clumps and shallow cracks.

Stone-finish presets use the same four maps as opaque dielectrics with a zero metallic channel: granite has speckled mineral grains, slate has layered dark stone with fine ridges, and terrazzo has contrasting stone chips in a smooth binder.

Textile presets include denim with diagonal twill, burlap with a coarse cross weave, and carpet with a cut-pile surface. All three use the same four repeating maps as opaque dielectrics with a zero metallic channel, not geometry or hair simulation or transparent weave holes.

Soft textiles include knit with muted stockinette-like repeating V-shaped stitches, rounded raised yarn and recessed loop gaps; corduroy with warm brown parallel rounded raised wales, fine pile speckle and deep narrow valleys; and felt with a muted slate-green matte nonwoven surface, randomly oriented fine fibers and low relief. All three are opaque dielectrics with zero metallic channel and factor, using the same four deterministic periodic maps. Relief is normal-map-only, without yarn/fur geometry or transparent loops.

Building finishes include plaster with pale gypsum, shallow sweeping trowel marks and fine pores; terracotta with unglazed reddish fired clay, irregular kiln mottling and pits, without tile grout; and cork with tan/brown compressed flakes and cellular boundaries. These are opaque dielectrics using the same four repeating maps with a zero metallic channel, not geometry or physical simulation.

Industrial surfaces include rubber with charcoal molded elastomer and fine pebbled stipple, and carbonfiber with dark resin-coated tow bundles and alternating diagonal twill directions. Both are opaque dielectrics with a zero metallic channel. Diamondplate has silver rolled metal with raised alternating diagonal lozenges, metallic channel 1 and default metallic factor 1. All use the same four periodic RGBA maps; relief is normal-map-only, not geometry. Carbon weave does not add a special anisotropic shader, clearcoat or physical simulation.

Craft materials include paper with ivory uncoated pulp fibers, fine irregular grain and subtle formation clouding, not recolored plaster; wicker with broad rounded tan rattan strips interlaced over deep opaque recesses, with fine longitudinal strip grain distinct from coarse burlap; and bamboo with golden longitudinal fibers and periodically staggered darker node bands. Formed metals include hammeredmetal with warm copper-like metal, overlapping shallow rounded hammer dimples and smooth continuous relief, not rough rock; galvanized with cool silver zinc spangles, crystallite tonal/roughness contrast and very shallow relief, not gravel; and corrugatedmetal with rolled silver sheet, parallel smooth flutes and faint longitudinal wear. Floor finishes include parquet with basketweave wood blocks made of several narrow slats, alternating longitudinal grain directions and dark recessed seams; mosaic with tiny square glazed tesserae, seeded tile-to-tile tonal variation and narrow recessed grout, distinct from larger tiles; and hexagontiles with six-sided ceramic cells and narrow recessed grout in a seamless periodic tiling. Relief is a surface-shading/normal-map effect, without paver, stone, board or screw geometry and without displacement.
